text:
THE KIO SOLUTION — LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM

A PARTY OF OUR OWN: WHY SWEDEN'S IMMIGRANTS NEED THEIR OWN SEAT AT THE TABLE

By Kio Amachree, Stockholm

THE VOTE THAT CHANGED THE ARITHMETIC

On 13 September 2026 Sweden went to the polls and the country split down the middle. Magdalena Andersson's bloc took 175 seats, Ulf Kristersson's took 174. The Sweden Democrats lost ten seats and fell to 17.7 percent. Within hours of the count, the losers had found their culprit. Not their own policies. Not the return migration bounties, not the eight year citizenship rule, not the ankle bracelets for children. The culprit was us. The foreign voter. Some 206,000 people became Swedish citizens between October 2022 and the middle of 2026, and the exit polls show that roughly two out of three voters of non European background voted for the left bloc, exactly as they did in 2022. Nothing changed in how we voted. What changed is that we are now numerous enough to be blamed for the result.

Take that in. In a democracy, citizens voted, and one half of the political class treats their votes as a fraud committed against the nation. That is the moment a community either accepts its place as a permanent guest, or organises.

I say organise.

WHAT THE LAST FOUR YEARS DID TO US

Under the Tidö Agreement, the rules were rewritten one by one. From 6 June 2026 you need eight years of residence for citizenship instead of five, plus a language and society test, plus proof of "good conduct" and self sufficiency. From 12 July 2026 nobody with asylum based status can obtain permanent residence at all. From 1 January 2026 the state pays a lawful resident up to 350,000 kronor, and a family up to 600,000 kronor, to leave the country. From 1 September 2026 more offences trigger expulsion. The work permit salary threshold rose to 90 percent of the median wage, shutting out the very people who clean the hospitals and drive the buses.

And the labour market tells the truth that the speeches hide. In August 2026 unemployment among the foreign born stood at 13.4 percent. Among native born Swedes it was 4.2 percent. Three times higher. That gap did not appear last year. It has been there for decades, through boom and bust, through Social Democratic and Moderate governments alike. It is not a gap of ability. It is a gap of access.

Meanwhile the gangs have made all of us suspects. Reported explosion offences rose from 162 in 2018 to 621 in 2025. Police estimate around 17,500 active gang criminals, and children of thirteen and fourteen are being used as hitmen because they sit below the age of criminal responsibility. Let me be plain: the gangs are the enemy of the immigrant family before they are the enemy of anyone else. It is our sons they recruit, our daughters they threaten, our shops they burn, our neighbourhoods they turn into ghettos. Any immigrant party that is soft on the gangs is not an immigrant party. It is a suicide pact.

WHY THE EXISTING PARTIES WILL NOT DO IT

The left takes our vote for granted and delivers nothing but the absence of the far right. The right treats us as a problem to be managed, deported or bought out. Partiet Nyans, the one attempt so far at an ethnic party, collapsed this September, went to zero in Rinkeby where it had polled around 26 percent in 2022, and its founder Mikail Yüksel resigned on election night blaming the mosques. Nyans failed because it was a Turkish and Islamist vehicle dressed up as an immigrant movement. A quarter of Sweden's population is now foreign born or has two foreign born parents. We are Nigerians and Somalis, Iranians and Iraqis, Syrians and Eritreans, Chileans and Bosnians, Poles and Indians, Christians, Muslims, Jews and unbelievers. No single mosque, church or homeland can carry that. Only a professional, secular, pan immigrant party can.

THE PROPOSAL: NYA SVENSKAR — THE NEW SWEDES PARTY

I propose a new party, working title Nya Svenskar, built to cross the four percent threshold for the Riksdag in 2030 and to enter municipal councils in Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmö, Botkyrka, Södertälje and Örebro long before that. The 271,335 new eligible voters added since 2022 are already more than the four percent threshold requires. The votes exist. What is missing is the vehicle.

Its charter would rest on ten commitments.

One. Representation. Immigrant Swedes in the Riksdag, in county councils, on municipal boards, in government, in proportion to our numbers, and a demand that every ministry publishes the share of foreign born staff at every grade.

Two. An Anti Racism Act with teeth. The Discrimination Ombudsman becomes a prosecuting authority with the power to fine, not a letter writing service. Mandatory anonymous CV procedures in the public sector and in all companies bidding for public contracts. A standing Racism Commission with staff, budget and the power to subpoena.

Three. Jobs. Fast track recognition of foreign degrees and professional licences within six months, not six years. Public procurement conditioned on workforce diversity. Tax relief for the first foreign born hire in every small business.

Four. Housing. Testing of landlords by paired applications, as is done in the United States, with licence loss for those who discriminate. An end to the queue systems that lock the newly arrived out of the rental market for a generation.

Five. Families and social services. An independent review board, with immigrant and legal representation, for every compulsory care order under LVU affecting a foreign born family. Interpreters and culturally competent caseworkers as a legal right. I do not repeat the wilder claims of the online LVU campaign, and I do not need to. The fear in our communities is real, the opacity of the system is real, and an independent review costs the state nothing but pride.

Six. Police. Body cameras on every officer in every interaction. An independent police complaints authority outside the police, on the British model. Stop and search statistics broken down by background and published quarterly. Respect the police, fund the police, and hold the police to account. Those three are not in conflict.

Seven. Gangs. Zero tolerance, and immigrant led. Full support for the police against the shooters and the bombers. But also the things the Tidö parties never funded: youth centres open until midnight, exit programmes, mentors from our own communities, and a legal duty on schools to report recruitment. The far right needs the gangs. We need them gone.

Eight. Citizenship and residence. Repeal the eight year rule. Restore permanent residence for those who have earned it. Scrap the return migration bounty, which is nothing but a state funded invitation to go away.

Nine. Media and the far right. A statutory right of reply for communities defamed in the press, and a Riksdag committee on extremism that treats the far right's networks with the same seriousness the state applies to gangs.

Ten. Diaspora power. A Swedish party that uses its members' foreign connections, in Lagos, Tehran, Istanbul, Mogadishu, Warsaw, Santiago, as a national asset for trade, investment and diplomacy, rather than as evidence of divided loyalty.

MY OWN TESTIMONY: THIRTY YEARS OF BEING INVISIBLE

I write this as a man Sweden chose not to see. I was educated at Eton College and at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. I worked on Wall Street and in corporate America. My father was Nigeria's first Solicitor General and the first African Under Secretary General of the United Nations, a man who worked in Dag Hammarskjöld's United Nations at the height of the Congo crisis. My grandfather sat in the Eastern House of Assembly and went to London in 1958 to negotiate Nigeria's independence. My friends from Wharton include the head of the Wallenberg family.

For thirty years in Sweden, none of it counted. Not the education, not the experience, not the family, not the connections. Ignored, sidelined, dismissed. I sent the applications. I sat in the meetings. I watched Swedes with a fraction of my record walk through doors that stayed shut for me, and I understood, slowly and then all at once, that the door was never going to open, because the problem was not my CV. The problem was my face.

So I did what my father taught me. I stopped asking. I financed myself. I built my own record label and kept every right to every song. I protected myself and my family by my own means. I used my connections abroad, in London, in New York, in Lagos, in Paris, to build a life in Sweden that Sweden itself refused to offer me. I created my own world inside this country, a world that owes the Swedish establishment nothing, because the Swedish establishment gave it nothing.

And here is the lesson for every immigrant reading this. They tell you to assimilate. They tell you that if you learn the language, adopt the customs, lower your voice and lower your expectations, you will be accepted. It is a lie. I speak the language. I know the customs. I have more connections than any Swede alive, and I am still the foreigner. Assimilation is a debt they never intend to repay. So my answer is no. Integration, yes: obey the law, pay your taxes, educate your children, respect your neighbour. Assimilation, no. I will not erase myself to please people who will not see me even when I do. I am an Old Etonian, a Wharton man, a Kalabari son, a Swedish citizen, and I am all of these at once, without apology.

That is what a party of our own must say out loud, in the Riksdag, to their faces.

THE KIO SOLUTION

First, form the party in 2027, with a founding congress that is deliberately multi ethnic and multi faith, and a constitution that bars any single national or religious group from holding more than a quarter of the board.

Second, contest the 2030 municipal elections in the twenty largest immigrant municipalities and the Riksdag in the same year, with the four percent threshold as the sole target.

Third, register a foundation alongside the party to fund legal action, test case litigation on employment and housing discrimination, and an annual Racism Audit of the Swedish state.

Fourth, build the party on professionals, the doctors, engineers, lawyers, entrepreneurs and academics that Sweden imported and then parked, because the establishment cannot dismiss as uneducated a party led by people it could not be bothered to hire.

Fifth, make one promise and keep it: this party will be harder on the gangs than the Sweden Democrats and harder on racism than the Social Democrats, because we are the people who suffer from both.

text:
THE KIO SOLUTION — LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM

A PARTY OF OUR OWN: WHY SWEDEN'S IMMIGRANTS NEED THEIR OWN SEAT AT THE TABLE

By Kio Amachree, Stockholm

THE VOTE THAT CHANGED THE ARITHMETIC

On 13 September 2026 Sweden went to the polls and the country split down the middle. Magdalena Andersson's bloc took 175 seats, Ulf Kristersson's took 174. The Sweden Democrats lost ten seats and fell to 17.7 percent. Within hours of the count, the losers had found their culprit. Not their own policies. Not the return migration bounties, not the eight year citizenship rule, not the ankle bracelets for children. The culprit was us. The foreign voter. Some 206,000 people became Swedish citizens between October 2022 and the middle of 2026, and the exit polls show that roughly two out of three voters of non European background voted for the left bloc, exactly as they did in 2022. Nothing changed in how we voted. What changed is that we are now numerous enough to be blamed for the result.

Take that in. In a democracy, citizens voted, and one half of the political class treats their votes as a fraud committed against the nation. That is the moment a community either accepts its place as a permanent guest, or organises.

I say organise.

WHAT THE LAST FOUR YEARS DID TO US

Under the Tidö Agreement, the rules were rewritten one by one. From 6 June 2026 you need eight years of residence for citizenship instead of five, plus a language and society test, plus proof of "good conduct" and self sufficiency. From 12 July 2026 nobody with asylum based status can obtain permanent residence at all. From 1 January 2026 the state pays a lawful resident up to 350,000 kronor, and a family up to 600,000 kronor, to leave the country. From 1 September 2026 more offences trigger expulsion. The work permit salary threshold rose to 90 percent of the median wage, shutting out the very people who clean the hospitals and drive the buses.

And the labour market tells the truth that the speeches hide. In August 2026 unemployment among the foreign born stood at 13.4 percent. Among native born Swedes it was 4.2 percent. Three times higher. That gap did not appear last year. It has been there for decades, through boom and bust, through Social Democratic and Moderate governments alike. It is not a gap of ability. It is a gap of access.

Meanwhile the gangs have made all of us suspects. Reported explosion offences rose from 162 in 2018 to 621 in 2025. Police estimate around 17,500 active gang criminals, and children of thirteen and fourteen are being used as hitmen because they sit below the age of criminal responsibility. Let me be plain: the gangs are the enemy of the immigrant family before they are the enemy of anyone else. It is our sons they recruit, our daughters they threaten, our shops they burn, our neighbourhoods they turn into ghettos. Any immigrant party that is soft on the gangs is not an immigrant party. It is a suicide pact.

WHY THE EXISTING PARTIES WILL NOT DO IT

The left takes our vote for granted and delivers nothing but the absence of the far right. The right treats us as a problem to be managed, deported or bought out. Partiet Nyans, the one attempt so far at an ethnic party, collapsed this September, went to zero in Rinkeby where it had polled around 26 percent in 2022, and its founder Mikail Yüksel resigned on election night blaming the mosques. Nyans failed because it was a Turkish and Islamist vehicle dressed up as an immigrant movement. A quarter of Sweden's population is now foreign born or has two foreign born parents. We are Nigerians and Somalis, Iranians and Iraqis, Syrians and Eritreans, Chileans and Bosnians, Poles and Indians, Christians, Muslims, Jews and unbelievers. No single mosque, church or homeland can carry that. Only a professional, secular, pan immigrant party can.

THE PROPOSAL: NYA SVENSKAR — THE NEW SWEDES PARTY

I propose a new party, working title Nya Svenskar, built to cross the four percent threshold for the Riksdag in 2030 and to enter municipal councils in Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmö, Botkyrka, Södertälje and Örebro long before that. The 271,335 new eligible voters added since 2022 are already more than the four percent threshold requires. The votes exist. What is missing is the vehicle.

Its charter would rest on ten commitments.

One. Representation. Immigrant Swedes in the Riksdag, in county councils, on municipal boards, in government, in proportion to our numbers, and a demand that every ministry publishes the share of foreign born staff at every grade.

Two. An Anti Racism Act with teeth. The Discrimination Ombudsman becomes a prosecuting authority with the power to fine, not a letter writing service. Mandatory anonymous CV procedures in the public sector and in all companies bidding for public contracts. A standing Racism Commission with staff, budget and the power to subpoena.

Three. Jobs. Fast track recognition of foreign degrees and professional licences within six months, not six years. Public procurement conditioned on workforce diversity. Tax relief for the first foreign born hire in every small business.

Four. Housing. Testing of landlords by paired applications, as is done in the United States, with licence loss for those who discriminate. An end to the queue systems that lock the newly arrived out of the rental market for a generation.

Five. Families and social services. An independent review board, with immigrant and legal representation, for every compulsory care order under LVU affecting a foreign born family. Interpreters and culturally competent caseworkers as a legal right. I do not repeat the wilder claims of the online LVU campaign, and I do not need to. The fear in our communities is real, the opacity of the system is real, and an independent review costs the state nothing but pride.

Six. Police. Body cameras on every officer in every interaction. An independent police complaints authority outside the police, on the British model. Stop and search statistics broken down by background and published quarterly. Respect the police, fund the police, and hold the police to account. Those three are not in conflict.

Seven. Gangs. Zero tolerance, and immigrant led. Full support for the police against the shooters and the bombers. But also the things the Tidö parties never funded: youth centres open until midnight, exit programmes, mentors from our own communities, and a legal duty on schools to report recruitment. The far right needs the gangs. We need them gone.

Eight. Citizenship and residence. Repeal the eight year rule. Restore permanent residence for those who have earned it. Scrap the return migration bounty, which is nothing but a state funded invitation to go away.

Nine. Media and the far right. A statutory right of reply for communities defamed in the press, and a Riksdag committee on extremism that treats the far right's networks with the same seriousness the state applies to gangs.

Ten. Diaspora power. A Swedish party that uses its members' foreign connections, in Lagos, Tehran, Istanbul, Mogadishu, Warsaw, Santiago, as a national asset for trade, investment and diplomacy, rather than as evidence of divided loyalty.

MY OWN TESTIMONY: THIRTY YEARS OF BEING INVISIBLE

I write this as a man Sweden chose not to see. I was educated at Eton College and at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. I worked on Wall Street and in corporate America. My father was Nigeria's first Solicitor General and the first African Under Secretary General of the United Nations, a man who worked in Dag Hammarskjöld's United Nations at the height of the Congo crisis. My grandfather sat in the Eastern House of Assembly and went to London in 1958 to negotiate Nigeria's independence. My friends from Wharton include the head of the Wallenberg family.

For thirty years in Sweden, none of it counted. Not the education, not the experience, not the family, not the connections. Ignored, sidelined, dismissed. I sent the applications. I sat in the meetings. I watched Swedes with a fraction of my record walk through doors that stayed shut for me, and I understood, slowly and then all at once, that the door was never going to open, because the problem was not my CV. The problem was my face.

So I did what my father taught me. I stopped asking. I financed myself. I built my own record label and kept every right to every song. I protected myself and my family by my own means. I used my connections abroad, in London, in New York, in Lagos, in Paris, to build a life in Sweden that Sweden itself refused to offer me. I created my own world inside this country, a world that owes the Swedish establishment nothing, because the Swedish establishment gave it nothing.

And here is the lesson for every immigrant reading this. They tell you to assimilate. They tell you that if you learn the language, adopt the customs, lower your voice and lower your expectations, you will be accepted. It is a lie. I speak the language. I know the customs. I have more connections than any Swede alive, and I am still the foreigner. Assimilation is a debt they never intend to repay. So my answer is no. Integration, yes: obey the law, pay your taxes, educate your children, respect your neighbour. Assimilation, no. I will not erase myself to please people who will not see me even when I do. I am an Old Etonian, a Wharton man, a Kalabari son, a Swedish citizen, and I am all of these at once, without apology.

That is what a party of our own must say out loud, in the Riksdag, to their faces.

THE KIO SOLUTION

First, form the party in 2027, with a founding congress that is deliberately multi ethnic and multi faith, and a constitution that bars any single national or religious group from holding more than a quarter of the board.

Second, contest the 2030 municipal elections in the twenty largest immigrant municipalities and the Riksdag in the same year, with the four percent threshold as the sole target.

Third, register a foundation alongside the party to fund legal action, test case litigation on employment and housing discrimination, and an annual Racism Audit of the Swedish state.

Fourth, build the party on professionals, the doctors, engineers, lawyers, entrepreneurs and academics that Sweden imported and then parked, because the establishment cannot dismiss as uneducated a party led by people it could not be bothered to hire.

Fifth, make one promise and keep it: this party will be harder on the gangs than the Sweden Democrats and harder on racism than the Social Democrats, because we are the people who suffer from both.

They have spent thirty years telling us to wait our turn. On 13 September they told us that even our votes are illegitimate. Very well. We will stop waiting. We will stand.

Regime Change: Inside the Imperial presidency of donald trump (in a review weirdly titled "Trump's Constitutional Democracy," nothing of the kind) by Mark Danner. He leads with short summary of the mobster's disastrous reign, then moves to an episode illustrating his lust for absolute power:

"A loyal-unto-death aide, Natalie Harp—known to her colleagues as “the human printer”—is dispatched to fetch a document, and the president begins to read from it, 'reciting the names of some of history’s most powerful figures, explaining how each fell short of his own power as US President. Alexander the Great, the Caesars, William the Conqueror—“They didn’t have airplanes, right? You couldn’t travel around.” Genghis Khan. Attila the Hun. Tamerlane. “Napoleon,” he said with relish. “Hitler. Mao. Stalin.”

    'These leaders “maintained power through fear,” he said. “Who would ever do a thing like that? Right?” Trump lingered on the document’s central argument: that each leader, however fearsome in his day, had no global reach. Their power was local. But his was not. “I never thought of it in terms of that,” Trump said. “It’s very interesting, the power.” Then he added: “But when I read it, I said, ‘He’s right.’”

"And the “he” in question? The “historian” whose name had slipped the president’s mind, Harp later texts them, was actually the golfer Gary Player’s longtime caddy. No matter. “What was revealing,” they write,

    was not really that Trump agreed with the thesis but the way he inhabited it: the evident pleasure he took in the company of Mao, Hitler, and Stalin, masters of state control through murder, torture, and detention, and Napoleon—and the untroubled ease with which he accepted a place among men who had reshaped the world through conquest and fear. He drew no distinction between those who built and those who destroyed.

"The scene is irresistible: the president of the United States sitting at the Resolute Desk and comparing himself blithely to Mao, Hitler, and Stalin.
... 
"Trump’s true innovation as an American authoritarian is not the profligate abuse of emergency powers but the full-on castration of a Congress that allowed him to do it. As we all learned in school, Congress, cantankerous and jealous of its powers, particularly the power of the purse, was meant to be the immediate bulwark against an unbound executive. But during his decade of dominance, Trump has wielded his charisma and his fury and his unquenchable taste for vengeance to systematically destroy any Republicans who would dare raise a voice against him. Though these days a few so-called YOLO—“You only live once”—Republicans, who are retiring or have lost primaries thanks to Trump, are nervously raising their heads from under a rock, since his reelection senators and congressmen have been only too happy to remain silent as he relentlessly increases his power by suborning theirs.
...
"The president wields sticks, yes—we have all seen how the insufficiently “loyal” are wiped out by Trump-backed primary challengers—but even more he offers carrots, aggressively seducing those who show the least reluctance to comply. Power in Congress, having increasingly in recent years flowed upward to the leadership, now “flowed out of the Speaker’s office directly into the Oval Office.” 
...
"The sums are truly fantastical: $1.9 billion raised from corporate donors. Trump’s political apparatus, much more organized and efficient than it had been during his first term, made full “use [of these] outside groups as weapons to enforce compliance” with his agenda. Next to corporate resources, mere politicians are cheap: a couple billion buys a lot of compliance. And should the campaign cash and the phone calls fall short, there was always the social media army, a bevy of MAGA influencers “who had massive audiences and threatened any Republican who would consider voting against Trump’s nominees.” 

'Senator Joni Ernst, a combat veteran who expressed doubts about Pete Hegseth’s nomination as secretary of defense (for his part Hegseth, one of the dimmer of the dim bulbs among Trump’s appointees, had doubts about whether women should even be in combat), found herself beset with a full-on social media campaign that included nasty details of her divorce. She voted for Hegseth.

"And so even before his second term had commenced, Trump and his minions, who make up in loyalty and obedience what they lack in competence, were able very quickly to reduce the United States’ three branches of government to two.
...
"... although Trump as a politician certainly has elements of genius—his aggression and energy, his uncanny instinct for finding weakness in adversaries, his mastery in dominating the news cycle, his endlessly creative shaping and projecting of his own grievances, his sheer shameless willfulness in making his reality our own—he also remains an ignorant blowhard. He lies so much that he often forgets what the truth is. He doesn’t read. He knows little or no history. And he is so captivated by the sound of his own voice that he almost entirely lacks the ability to listen. 

:Finally, he is wholly in the grip of a decades-old set of beliefs—imposing tariffs will make the United States rich with other countries’ money, American cities are so ravaged by criminal immigrants that only the military can restore order, alliances are simply the means by which freeloader countries “take advantage” of the United States, climate change is nothing more than a fallacious “green new scam”—that are demonstrably false.

What remains astonishing is that Trump, through his indefatigable showmanship, was able to ride his reality show fame to such power in the world’s strongest country that he has been able to impose these aberrant views on nearly 350 million people, with consequences for billions more. As Haberman and Swan show, Trump in his second term has built a government that, but for a few important exceptions (Susie Wiles, Stephen Miller, Russell Vought), is made up of incompetent toadies who are wholly responsive to his wishes—a government that, forced to choose between his fantasies and reality, will choose the 
fantasies every time."

This is illustrated by Cheato's utter refusal to listen to facts on his tariff scheme, and its result:

"In the event, Trump’s announcement crashed the markets, with the S&P 500 losing $2 trillion in one day, and soon the bond market began to plunge as well. Finally, faced with financial Armageddon, Trump backed down, “pausing the tariffs” for ninety days [quoting Haberman and Swan):

    'That afternoon, the markets surged nearly 10 percent on the news, and Trump surrogates rushed to the cameras to clean up the mess, claiming that pausing the tariffs was the plan all along. This was, they said, a genius negotiating strategy from the dealmaker of dealmakers…. The world had just witnessed a master class in economic brinkmanship, they would all say.

    'But in fact, Trump had blinked. The collapsing bond markets left him no choice. Investors were losing faith that the United States would be able to make good on its debt.'

"One lived through these events, of course, but in reliving them through this inside account one feels a kind of terrible awe at the blithe incompetence and sheer irresponsibility on display. In service to his obsessions, the president is willing to take the country right up to the edge of catastrophe, and no one is willing to incur his ire by trying to stop him. Only the reality of the consequences of what he had done—the collapsing bond markets—persuaded him to reverse course."

Then on to the mad emperor's precipitation of imperail collapse: 

"The catastrophe of Iran may mark this country’s decline no less than the Suez Crisis marked Great Britain’s. There is the same stunned realization abroad of having seen the limits of the late imperial mind. Haberman and Swan’s account of the decision to attack Iran—a decision presidents have resisted for very good reasons since 1979—is a bravura piece of reporting and, for those who retain any faith in American power in the world, deeply saddening to read. 

"As he has with previous presidents, the Israeli prime minister comes to the White House Situation Room with a war to sell, and he promises that regime change will follow and the nuclear threat will be removed forever. Trump will be a hero, doing what presidents before him have lacked the audacity to attempt. And although US intelligence analysts call the Israeli scenarios “farcical”—“In other words, it’s bullshit,” helpfully translates Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio—Trump decides to buy in anyway. [dreaming of his glory] The chairman of the Joint Chiefs mentions something about Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz—one of the principal reasons presidents have resisted similar Israeli importunings for decades—but Trump in his vast ignorance says not to worry, it’ll all be over in a few days. And anyway what do we have to lose?

"The account put me in mind of a phrase from an essay published early in this administration: “The Dumbest Imperial Collapse in History.” "

The outcome of that foolish move to war was that trump was forced to capitulate to Iran and settle for a deal far worse than the agreement negotiated by Obama. The war he started is causing suffering around the world, and is about to get worse. 

"The signs are everywhere that the failed assault on Iran marked the high tide of his power. The Supreme Court ruled that he lacked the authority to impose his tariffs or to end birthright citizenship. Lower courts in dozens of decisions have blocked his more presumptuous emergency actions. His high-profile campaign of deportations in “blue cities” crashed on the shoals of Minneapolis’s civic resistance, including that of the two protesters ICE agents shot and killed there. 

"Confronted with a wave of bad press and plunging poll numbers, the administration backed down, ignoring the urgings of some within it (including Stephen Miller and, as Haberman and Swan reveal, Vice President J.D. Vance) that the president invoke the Insurrection Act and send troops into the city. Here, as with the tariffs and the war, faced with darkening reality he retreated, though his administration, working more quietly now, continues to deport tens of thousands.

"He will leave us having succeeded in putting an end to the country’s imperial dominance and in closing borders that were once more welcoming to outsiders. He will have helped ensure that the rich grow ever richer and that millions with less will not have insurance when they get sick. He will have made the government weaker and less responsive and the society around it starkly more corrupt. He will have politicized many parts of the country’s public life that were not politicized before." 

I don't know if the lamentation of loss of imperial power is Danner's or the authors he's quoting, but that's not the real loss, and not what's important. He does enumerate some of the lives lost , though not the bombings of boats in the Caribbean, nor the deaths at the hands of ICE, in its concentration camps or on the streets). Even these killings are greatly outnumber by the far larger number of deaths Mr Supremacist caused from cutting off US AID programs providing food and medicine (including life-preserving HIV medications and Ebola research). Those figures are incalculable, and we haven't even gotten to the free hand Cheato has given to poisoning food and water, and all his other attacks on Mother Earth on behalf of oligarchy.

India needs an opposition like Israel has.

An opposition that aggressively raises genuine public issues, challenges bad policies and keeps the government accountable, while still standing with the government on matters of national interest.

National security, foreign policy and strategic issues should not become partisan battles.

Oppose the government, not the country.

When India faces the world, defend India. When our soldiers are at war, stand with the Army. When the government gets something wrong, question it without hesitation.

A strong opposition should offer a genuine alternative, not oppose everything simply because it comes from the ruling party.

If India had such an opposition, voters would have better choices, the government would face greater accountability, and democracy would become stronger.

Sadly, sometimes it feels like India is cursed when it comes to having a truly constructive opposition.

text:
📜 THIS DAY IN DIPLOMATIC HISTORY
        September 20, 1870

Italian artillery breaches the Aurelian Walls at Porta Pia. Bersaglieri troops pour through the gap. Within hours, Pope Pius IX orders the white flag raised over St Peter's. The Papal States, which had existed since 756 AD, more than eleven centuries, cease to exist. Italian unification is complete. And it happened only because, nineteen days earlier, a French army had surrendered at Sedan.

By 1861, the Kingdom of Italy had unified most of the peninsula under Victor Emmanuel II. On March 27, 1861, the Italian Parliament declared Rome the capital of the kingdom. But Italy did not control Rome. The city and the surrounding region remained under the temporal rule of the Pope, and that rule was protected by a French garrison stationed there by Napoleon III.

This was the heart of the matter. Napoleon III wanted good relations with Italy, but he could not abandon the Pope. As the historian Raffaele De Cesare put it, the Roman Question was "the stone tied to Napoleon's feet that dragged him into the abyss." For twenty years, the French garrison in Rome made the completion of Italian unification impossible.

In the years before the Franco-Prussian War, negotiations had been underway for a triple alliance between France, Austria, and Italy. They failed — and the decisive obstacle was the Roman Question. Italy made its condition explicit: France must withdraw its garrison from Rome and allow Italy to take the city. Napoleon III could not agree. Abandoning the Pope would have alienated the French Catholics on whom his regime depended. And so, when war came in July 1870, Italy stood aside a potential ally lost over the very city it would seize the moment France collapsed.

Sedan changes everything. On September 1, 1870, the French army was destroyed at Sedan. Napoleon III surrendered to the Prussians. The Second Empire collapsed in Paris. And the French garrison protecting Rome was gone. Suddenly the Pope found himself without his protector. It was the opportunity the Italian government had been waiting for two decades.

Victor Emmanuel first tried diplomacy. He sent an envoy, Count Ponza di San Martino, to Pius IX on September 10 with a personal letter proposing a face-saving arrangement: Italian troops would enter Rome to maintain order while the Pope retained spiritual sovereignty. The Pope's reception was furious. "Fine loyalty," he reportedly exclaimed. "You are all a set of vipers." He refused.

General Cadorna's forces crossed the papal frontier on September 11 and reached the Aurelian Walls on September 19. Pius IX made a fateful decision: he would offer only token resistance - enough to demonstrate that the takeover was not freely accepted, that Rome was being taken by force. He instructed his commander to surrender once the walls were breached.

On the morning of September 20, after a three-hour cannonade, Italian artillery opened a breach in the wall near Porta Pia. The Bersaglieri entered. Pius IX ordered the white flag raised. Forty-nine Italian soldiers and nineteen Papal Zouaves had died in the token defence.

Rome was annexed after a plebiscite on October 2 and became the capital of Italy on February 3, 1871. Pius IX refused to accept it. He rejected the Italian Law of Guarantees, which offered him sovereign privileges and an annual stipend. He declared himself a "prisoner in the Vatican" and never again set foot outside its walls. His successors maintained the same position for nearly sixty years.

The "Roman Question" was not resolved until 1929, when Mussolini signed the Lateran Treaty, recognising the sovereignty of Vatican City in exchange for papal recognition of the Italian state. The Pope became sovereign of 44 hectares — the smallest state in the world, all that remained of an eleven-century dominion.

Towns and cities across Italy commemorate the date with a street name: Via XX Settembre (the Twentieth of September). It is one of the most common street names in the country.

text: The political establishment has spent decades deriding the working classes, dismissing their concerns - particularly over large scale legal and illegal migration which has artificially depressed their wages, increased their rents and cost of living, left them competing for manual jobs offered by employers lulled by an endless supply of cheap labour, completely changed the faces of their communities, eroded trust and devalued traditional working class mores - and depicting them as unintelligent, incapable, bigoted, out of touch, ‘far right’ and ignorant. This particularly applies to the Labour party (established to support the working classes and achieve their control of the means of production) post-1997, when Blair enacted the largest social engineering project in recent history: to lift huge numbers out of the working class into the middle class via university education, and to ignore and discriminate against those left behind. Many of our armed forces are working class men and women. When they leave the Army, they are ignored or treated like scum by the establishment; veterans lack help with PTSD and injuries, many are homeless, and charities cannot keep up with the number of ex-servicemen who need help. They shiver on the streets, reliant on charities and the kindness of strangers, whilst those who arrive illegally on our shores daily are offered the kind of accommodation, nutrition, medical treatment and governmental support that a former soldier (or indeed, current soldiers in squalid, unfit accommodation paid miserably to put their lives on the line) would love to receive. And now the government, who has been stigmatising the working class as ‘far right’, ‘fascists’, ‘Nazis’ and ‘bigots’, has conveniently forgotten that they have discriminated endlessly against the absolute backbone of our society, those who provide all the essential services without which our country would not function, and expect the working classes to fight and die for a country *they* have deliberately altered and degraded out of recognition? They expect veterans and reservists to simply pick up an SA80 and battle against our enemies without a hint of remorse for all the damage they have done to the bedrock of their country? They will, outrageously, be surprised that the working classes do not jump through hoops when their ‘masters’ click their fingers; they, knowing full well that neither the new arrivals nor the smug, financially-comfortable middle class socialists will ever be fit for service, or want to serve. Completely lacking in introspection and humility, they will be astonished by the refusal of those whom they treat like scum and pillory as Public Enemy No.1 (Mahmood’s outrageous remarks about Danny Tommo, no matter what one thinks of him personally, show a terminal descent into totalitarianism: he has committed no crime and is responding to the damage done to working class communities by this and previous governments) to serve an elite who treat them like dirt, only remembering their existence when it is politically useful to them.

text:
The morning after. 

A long read, if you can be arsed.

Can’t sugarcoat how poor that was yesterday from us. The players and manager have rightly had plaudits, even in defeat, this season but yesterday we were miles off it and I genuinely don’t think any single player got pass marks it was that bad.

The first goal was pretty awful. We were slightly unfortunate in winning the first header only for the ball to ricochet back off the Utd player who then did well to poke the ball through and set up the chance for the through ball which the boy put away well.

These things happen, it wasn’t great but there was a shade of misfortune about it.

The 2nd and 3rd goals however were an absolute shambles.

First one we literally set up the chance for Utd by gifting them the ball from our own possession through a woeful pass back from I think Sule.

Third one we totally got caught napping at the free kick and in this league, you switch off and you get punished.

So the game is pretty much done at 0-3 at the break and if we are honest the second half wasn’t much better and we were fortunate not to be on the end of an absolute hiding in the end.

This is a young team, under a young coach, and we WILL make mistakes and have games like this along the way. 

The hope is that they learn from it and they absolutely will.

On the team, obviously Nik was a big loss. 

Personally I think Sule looks more suited to playing in a two but either way his pace is his biggest attribute and once Utd got a couple goals ahead they rightly sat deep and countered and that game script absolutely killed Sule.

Could we have started with Young up there?

KP being back was great news but the experiment of pushing Nsio wide did not work at all. Tait and Cameron ran riot in the middle of the park where Paul was badly missed.

Dropping Mochrie also seemed a bit mental, unless he was carrying a knock of course. I felt we missed him carrying the ball forwards. We really didn’t offer much at all as an attacking threat and zero shots on target at home is a pretty damning stat.

We did have a couple of things go against us of course. To lose the penalty through a toenail offside call was very sore and had Nsio’s shot gone in rather then smack the bar at 0-2 then we might have got back into the game.

But end of the day, no complaints, we were very soundly beaten and Utd did play well.

One to take on the chin, learn from, and hopefully bounce back.

Three weeks off now, next game Hearts away on Oct 10th.

NSG Black Cats Storm the Training Ground: High-Intensity Tactical Display Captivates NCC Cadets

Over 100 NSG Commandos, 600+ Cadets: Black Cats Showcase Elite Tactical Skills in Ahmedabad

The #NCC #Headquarters at Law Garden, #Ahmedabad, witnessed a high-intensity tactical #demonstration by the National Security Guard (#NSG), as more than 100 #BlackCat #Commandos from the 30 Special Composite Group (#SCG) showcased specialised counter-#terrorism skills before NCC #cadets, #officers and their #families.

The demonstration was organised as part of the concluding activities of Combined Annual Training Camp (#CATC) 124, hosted by 37 Gujarat Battalion NCC under the aegis of the #NCCDirectorate of #Gujarat, #Dadra & #Nagar #Haveli and #Daman & Diu.

The #live demonstration offered the audience a close view of the operational techniques, coordination and specialised capabilities associated with India’s #premier counter-terrorism force. Senior NCC officers, Associate NCC Officers, Permanent Instructor Staff, more than 600 NCC cadets and their #parents attended the #event.

Through coordinated tactical sequences and real-time commentary, the NSG personnel demonstrated a range of specialised #operations, including urban intervention and building-clearing #drills, #hostage #rescue procedures, slithering and rope-craft operations, assault K-9 tactics, squad drills, #explosive-threat response and #IED render-safe procedures.

The demonstration also featured a Mixed Martial Arts display, along with an exhibition of specialised #weapons and operational #equipment used in counter-terrorism operations.

Simulated #explosions and realistic combat sequences added to the intensity of the presentation, while tactical commentary helped the audience understand the operational aspects of each demonstration.

For the NCC cadets, the event provided an opportunity to observe the #discipline, #physical conditioning, #teamwork and tactical coordination required in specialised military and counter-terrorism operations.

The demonstration concluded the CATC 124 activities on a high note, giving young cadets a firsthand exposure to the demanding standards of specialised security operations and reinforcing the values of discipline, teamwork, courage and service to the nation.

text:
Taylor Cavanaugh, a former U.S. Navy SEAL and French Foreign Legionnaire. He is widely recognized as the only known person to serve in both elite military units...

Turned away by the Marines and told to clean up his record first, he served four months in jail to get his probation expunged, then walked out and told a skeptical corrections officer he was going to become a Navy SEAL. He did, graduating training and earning his place at SEAL Team Seven, deploying overseas. He's been candid that his time in the Teams eventually unraveled, a spiral of poor decisions that ended with him being discharged from the Navy for steroid use. From there it got darker, another stretch in jail, homelessness, and by his own account genuine suicidal despair.

The turnaround came in a single moment of clarity, an internal voice, as he describes it, that told him plainly to stop feeling sorry for himself. Eight days later he was in Paris, enlisting in the French Foreign Legion, the storied corps that has offered foreign nationals a second chance and a new identity for nearly two centuries. His service there took him from busting illegal gold mining operations in the South American jungle to running security in Algeria, and in the Legion's brutal discipline, relearning to soldier in a language not his own, he found the structure that had eluded him at home.

Today Cavanaugh coaches and writes, using his own hard-earned discipline to help others rebuild. Not every warrior's story is a clean one, and his willingness to tell the messy parts is exactly what gives it weight.

text:
This why companies are leaving California. Companies leave California mainly for cost and rules, not because the state lacks talent. Destination states usually offer lower taxes, lighter regulation, cheaper housing and energy, and easier expansion. Remote work made the HQ address easier to change without moving every job.
PPIC found California headquarters tend to move to states with lower taxes and less regulation. The same pattern shows up nationwide. California did not cut that burden as fast as rival states during the period they studied.
CBRE’s 2026 HQ-relocation update lists the same cluster: high taxes, labor rules, and cost of living for firms leaving California metros. In 2025, growth opportunity and portfolio consolidation also rose as stated reasons.
The main drivers
1. Taxes California has the highest state personal income tax rate in the U.S. (13.3%). It also has high sales taxes and a complex corporate tax system. Texas and Florida have no state income tax. That gap hits founders, executives, and highly paid staff first. High earners have been more mobile after tax-law changes.
2. Regulation and compliance cost California ranks near the bottom on economic-freedom and regulatory indexes. Firms cite permitting delays, labor rules, contractor requirements, environmental reviews, and litigation risk. Those costs hit manufacturing, energy, housing, and mid-size companies hardest. Large firms can absorb them; smaller ones often cannot.
3. Cost of living and housing Housing, energy, and wages are among the highest in the country. Companies say it is hard to hire and retain mid-level staff when workers face long commutes and unaffordable homes. Tesla cited scaling limits in the Bay Area for that reason. KB Home cited high costs and housing prices when it chose Arizona.
4. Industry clusters in other states Chevron moved toward Houston because that is the U.S. energy center, not only because of California policy. Aerospace, energy, and some manufacturing follow customers, suppliers, and cheaper power. Film and media firms also chase tax credits in Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas.
5. Politics and culture (secondary, but loud) Some CEOs name specific laws. Musk cited a school parental-notification law as the last straw for SpaceX and X. Others describe California as anti-business in public statements. Surveys of residents who leave also mix cost of living with political disagreement. Policy research treats this as real for some firms but not the main statistical driver.
6. Remote work and M&A Once most executives can work from anywhere, the legal HQ can follow the CEO, the tax code, or a merger. CBRE now sees consolidation and growth opportunity as frequent official reasons, not only tax flight.
What this does not mean
California still has a huge economy, dense specialized talent, ports, universities, and climate amenities. Some aerospace and AI firms still move into Southern California for that talent. Many companies that relocate headquarters keep factories, labs, or large offices in the state. Job loss is concentrated in HQ roles, not always in total in-state employment.
New business formation and closures still dwarf HQ moves in raw numbers. The relocation story matters most for high-profile employers, tax base, and the signal it sends to the next company considering a move.
Practical takeaway
If a firm is cost-sensitive, labor-heavy, or energy-intensive, California’s tax-plus-rules package is a competitive disadvantage versus Texas, Florida, Arizona, Georgia, and Tennessee. If a firm lives on unique Bay Area or L.A. talent density, many stay or keep a large footprint even after the HQ address changes.

text:
It is with a sad heavy heart I inform you of Lee o’toole’s (David’s brother) death. He fought for answers and justice for his brother (David) and his friend (Patrick) until the end. A story that rocked our community when I was a child. Many of us never gave up hope of them being found and justice being served. R.I.P I hope you are all together at last 🙏🏼 

Patrick Warren and David Spencer were two close friends from Chelmsley Wood in the West Midlands. Patrick, known affectionately as Paddy, was 11 and came from a large family. His mother remembered him as a cheeky boy with a mischievous sense of humour who liked to tease her about her Irish accent.

David was 13 and a keen boxer. His mother, Christine, described him as an adorable and lovely lad.

On December 26, 1996, the boys were at David's house before heading out later that day.

That afternoon, a police officer reportedly saw the boys playing with a larger group of children near a frozen pond. The officer warned them not to play on the ice.

After spending the day together, the boys eventually returned to David's house. They told their parents they planned to visit one of Patrick's brothers that evening. 

Patrick left on his new bicycle while David went on foot.

Instead of going directly to their destination, the boys spent some time around the streets of their neighbourhood. Eventually, they made their way to a local Shell petrol station.

At approximately 12:45 am on December 27, a petrol station attendant saw the boys and spoke to them. He gave them a packet of biscuits, which they had asked for, and the pair then walked away in the direction of Chelmsley Wood Shopping Centre.

It was the last confirmed sighting of Patrick and David.

When the boys failed to arrive, Patrick's brother Derek began searching for them. He checked the places he thought they might have gone, but when he couldn't find them, in the early hours of December 27th, he contacted the police.

The initial investigation focused on finding the boys. Officers knocked on doors, spoke to residents and searched places where they were known to spend time. Appeals were made through the local press, and a £500 reward was offered for information.

Patrick's brand new red bicycle had been left behind the petrol station near the bins, where it remained for several weeks before police realised that it belonged to him.

At first, police believed the boys may have run away. Senior officers told the media there was no reason to believe that Patrick and David had come to any harm. At the time, local reporters understood that investigators were treating the boys as runaways.

Just days after Patrick and David vanished, 17 year old Nicola Dixon was found murdered in Sutton Coldfield, around eight miles from Chelmsley Wood. Her murder attracted considerable police and media attention, but investigators found no connection between her death and the boys' disappearance.

In April 1997, four months after the boys disappeared, their photographs were placed on milk cartons across Britain as part of a campaign launched by the National Missing Persons Helpline and supported by Iceland. Patrick and David were the first missing children in the UK to feature in such a campaign. The boys became known in the media as the “Milk Carton Kids”.

Despite the increased publicity, there was still no breakthrough.

The investigation remained open, but years passed without an answer. In 2003, police arrested a 37 year old man. He was later released on bail and was never charged. According to David's mother, police had received a letter claiming that the boys' bodies were buried in Woodgate Valley.

By the 10th anniversary of their disappearance in 2006, police had launched a fresh review of the case.

One name that attracted particular attention was Brian Field.

20/09/2026 / https://t.co/sBTcfvZfnS
ÖYLE BİR HAYATA ÇATTIK Kİ!
Ne garip bir hayata çattık! İnsan hayatında akıl, iman ve ahlaktan sonra belki de en değerli şey adalettir. Ne yazık ki bugün bunların hepsi yerlerde sürünüyor. Birileri LGBT’ye “pozitif ayrımcılığı” savunuyor; i İş, LGBT’yi aşmış,  Satanist, Pedefolik, Ensest, Siyonist bir noktaya gelmiş, içimizde birileri hala onları savunuyor. İçimizde hâlâ bunu savunanlar var.  âdeta esirgeyen ve bağışlayan Allah ile alay edercesine. Kimse de bunlara güç yetiremiyor. Bunları koruyan uluslararası sözleşmeler vardı: İstanbul Sözleşmesi (Türkiye 2021’de çekildi dediler ama sözleşmenin bütün hükümleri yasada mer’i), CEDAW, Lanzarote gibi. Bunlara; vergi ve yargı muafiyeti tanıdığımız, diplomatik dokunulmazlığı olan, pozitif ayrımcılık yaptığımız; kamu, özel sektör, STK’lar, yerel yönetimler, merkezî hükümet, üniversiteler, eğitim kuruluşları, şirketler ve kooperatiflerle doğrudan temas imkânı sağladığımız GREVİO ve UN Women gibi uluslararası örgütler eşlik ediyor. (En son, aşı ve topuk kanı konusu üzerinden çocukların ailelerinden alınmasının yolunu açan bir düzenleme de yapıldı.) Bizimse sadece Allah’ımız var. Bu, abartılı bir eleştiri değil; somut ve yaşanan bir gerçek. Korkarım birileri yangına körükle gidiyor; kaçtığını sandığı şeye doğru koşuyor.
Öyle bir noktaya geldik ki; çok akıllı, çok dürüst, çok bilgili; ahlak, iffet, edep ve hayâ sahibi dindar biriyseniz, CV’niz “çok çok iyi” de olsa bu dünyada size iş yok! Bu özellikler artık para etmiyor, aksine risk sayılıyor.
Neyse ki kadere, rızka ve ecele hükmeden bir Allah’ımız var. O, din gününün sahibidir; kim zerre kadar iyilik ya da kötülük yaptıysa hesabının görüleceği bir gün var. Hasbunallahu ve ni’mel vekîl, ni’me’l-mevlâ ve ni’me’n-nasîr. Yeter ki biz O’nun yolunda, sırat-ı müstakim üzere olalım — imanı kalpte tutmanın, ateşi elde tutmaktan daha zor olduğu bir zamana doğru insanlık yokuş aşağı gitse de. “Ve’l-asr, inne’l-insâne le-fî husr, ille’llezîne âmenû ve amilü’s-salihât…” Bu gidişat karşısında iman edip salih amel işleyenler, direnenler, sabredenler ve sabrı tavsiye edenler müstesna, herkes hüsrandadır.

Bu, yalnızca kişiler ve topluluklar arasında bir sorun değil; devletler arasında da, aile içinde de durum aynı. ABD’ye, AB’ye, İngiltere’ye ya da Arap ülkelerine bakın; değişen fazla bir şey yok. Ahlaksızlık âdeta metastaz yapmış; bu anlamda bir “pandemi” yaşanıyor. Önerilen ilaç ise: “Boş ver, sana ne, keyfine bak, takma kafana, eğlen!” Sanki bu dünyaya “oyun ve eğlence için” gelmişiz gibi. Şeytan kulağımıza hep bunu fısıldamıyor mu?

Birçok şeyi değil, her şeyi yeniden düşünmemiz gerekiyor: kavramları, kurumları; evet, dinimizi, ideolojimizi, siyasetimizi, ait olduğumuz sosyal çevreyi — Allah’ın emri, Resulün sireti ve sünneti üzere yeniden tanımlamamız gerekiyor. Yani iman edenler olarak “yeniden iman etmemiz” gerekiyor. Tarih algımızı, gelecek tasavvurumuzu, aile içinden beşerî ilişkilere kadar her şeyi yeniden düşünmek zorundayız, hem de şimdi!

İmam-Hatipler, Kur’an kursları, ilahiyatlar ve bugünkü camiler, sözünü ettiğim dertlere bugün deva değil. “Cemaat” denilen yapıların düştüğü hâli de görüyorsunuz.

Hayal, gerçeğin anasıdır, onun içini akıl, bilgi, hikmet ve sorumlulukla doldurursanız. Mekke-i Mükerreme’ye gittik; “Arapların Mustafa Kemal’i” olmaya aday bir adamla ve İmran Han’a zulmeden bir Pakistanlı siyasetçiyle “Mekke anlaşması”nı imzaladık, değil mi? Dünden bugüne bir ilerleme var mı? Selman, ABD’yi ve İsrail’i yardıma çağırıyor. Bu ittifaka Sisi’nin Mısır’ını, BAE emirini ve Gazze karşısında İsrail’in yanında duran Aliyev’i de ekleyin, olsun bitsin.

Daha önce de, Trump’ın önderliğinde Gazze sorununa “çözüm” üretecek ittifakta yer almadık mı? Bir “Osmanlı Milletler Topluluğu” kuramadık; ama o coğrafyanın sınırlarını, rejimlerini ve iktidarlarını dönüştürmeyi amaçlayan BOP’ta (Büyük Ortadoğu Projesi) “eş başkan” değil miydik? Peki gelinen durum ne? Lübnan, Suriye, Irak, Yemen, Sudan, Somali, Libya, Tunus, BAE,  kısacası Arap yarımadası, Kuzey Afrika ve Kızıldeniz ülkeleri… Bu ülkelerdeki durum ne, ne oluyor?

Şimdi de TÜRKPOL’ü kuracakmışız. İyi niyetli bir girişim olabilir, kulağa hoş da gelebilir. Ama yarın bu örgüt, hayra vesile olup şerre fren olmak yerine; zalim yönetimlerden kaçıp nispeten ılımlı ülkelere sığınanların takip edilip iade edildiği bir zulüm çarkına dönüşürse ne olacak? Türk dünyasındaki hükümetler ne kadar adil? O ülkelerin yasaları ne kadar hukuka uygun? Siyasi suçluların durumu ne?

Bunu yapacaksanız önce şunları yapmalısınız: Batıdaki AİHM’in ötesinde bir “Türk Dünyası İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi” kurun. Hak ihlali yapan hükümetleri, siyasetçileri ve bürokratları yargılamak için, Lahey Adalet Divanı’nın ötesinde “Müdafaa-i Hukuk Mahkemeleri” kurun. TÜRKPOL’ün bağlı olacağı, “BM İnsan Hakları Yüksek Komiserliği” benzeri bir üst çatı kurun. Katılan ülkeler, hukuklarını bunun esasını oluşturacak bir uluslararası sözleşmeye göre yeniden düzenlesin. Yasama içinde bizdeki TBMM İnsan Hakları Komisyonu gibi bir komisyon, yürütme içinde ayrı bir başkanlık kursunlar; yargı içinde de, AYM’ye tanınan bireysel başvuru hakkı gibi bir üst yargı imkânı sunsunlar. Sivil denetim için insan haklarını savunacak STK’lar ve çatı örgütleri kurulabilsin. TÜRKPOL’de görev yapacak polisleri eğitip sertifikalandıracak bir Adalet Akademisi kurulsun. Demem o ki, TÜRKPOL’e giden yol ince ve uzundur; “kuruyoruz” demekle kurulmaz. Yoksa o iş de döner dolaşır, “Mekke ittifakı”na benzer!

Sahi, bizdeki “Ortadoğu Amme İdaresi Enstitüsü” kimler tarafından, niçin kurulmuştu? Biz Fulbright, Exeter deyip duruyoruz ama; ABD ve İngiltere, Osmanlı bakiyesi ülkelerin bürokratlarının eğitimi için Ankara’da böyle bir birim kurmuştu. Biz o mektebe yalnızca ev sahipliği yapmadık; orada ders verecekleri de eğitim için ABD’ye, İngiltere’ye gönderdik. Özel Harp, JİTEM, kontrgerilla kimler tarafından, nasıl örgütlendi? İşte bu yüzden, İNTERPOL’ü örnek alıp TÜRKPOL demekle; batıda gördüğümüz şeylerin başına “Türk” ya da “İslam” yazmakla (İslam BM’si, İslam NATO’su, İslam Ortak Pazarı, İslam IMF’si gibi) bu işler olmuyor.

Sahi, “para, para” diye her kapıyı çalıyor, BlackRock gibi dev yabancı fonları yatırıma çağırıyoruz da; D-8 ülkeleri arasında neden bir ortak yatırım fonu kur(a)mıyoruz? Tabii “Zarrab korkusu” ve “Rahip Brunson deneyimi” var. Kaygı verici bir gidiş de var: İflaslar başladı; batmakta olan tesis ve markalar ile tarım arazileri yabancı sermayenin eline geçebilir. (Bill Gates’in dünyanın çeşitli yerlerinde geniş tarım arazileri edindiği biliniyor; Türkiye’den tarla aldığı iddiaları var.) KKTC’de de satın alınacak fazla bir şey bırakmadılar. Bu gidişle kendi toprağımızda ırgatlığa mahkûm olmayalım; neredeyse içecek suyumuzu bile satın alır hâle geldiler.

Bu arada size olacakları söyleyeyim, iflaslar başladı ya, batmakta olan tesisleri, markaları artık “yerli ve milli” olan yurttaşımız olan Chabat’çılar ve o lobiden birileri  alacaklar. Bu tarımı biz bilmiyoruz (!?), onun için onlardan tohum almıyor muyuz? Artık onlar o hibrit tohumları da ülkemizde üretiyorlar. Yarın onlar daha büyük çiftlikler de kuracaklar buralarda. Bill Gates bile Türkiye’den tarla almadı mı? Zaten KKTC’de satın alacak fazla bir şey bırakmadılar. Kendi toprağımızda ırgatlık yapacağız bu Pedefolik, Satanist, Siyonist efendilere, bu gidişle. Nerede ise bize içecek su bırakmadılar, hepsini satın alıyorlar.

D-8’de yaklaşık 1,2 milyar nüfus var; sekiz ülke: Endonezya, Malezya, Pakistan, Bangladeş, İran, Türkiye, Mısır ve Nijerya. Asya, Avrupa ve Afrika’ya üç kıtaya dağılmış bir topluluktan söz ediyoruz. Ama aramızdaki ilişkiler neredeyse sıfır.

AB’ye giden yolda önce Demir-Çelik ve Kömür Topluluğu vardı; sonra AET, ardından AB oldu. Biz ise Mısır, Sudan ve Özbekistan’la bir “pamuk birliği” bile kuramadık. Türkiye neden Kazakistan’la bir tarım/buğday birliği kurmaz? Bu ülkeler arasında ortak bir yatırım fonu yok; niye? Sekiz ülke arasında bir takas bankası yok, ortak bir kredi kartı yok, ortak bir sosyal ağ yok. Yok işte! Ama iş “İslam Birliği” edebiyatına gelince mangalda kül bırakmıyoruz.

Batılıların LIBOR’u vardı: “London Interbank Offered Rate” yani Londra’daki büyük bankaların birbirine kısa vadeli, teminatsız borç verebileceği tahminî ortalama faiz oranı. Bu orana bağlı bankalar bir politika belirliyor, dünya da onu kabul ediyordu. (LIBOR 2023’te tümüyle kaldırıldı; yerini SOFR gibi oranlar aldı.) Öte yandan rezerv para olarak doları basan ABD merkezli FED, bir IMF, bir Dünya Bankası ve bu sistemi destekleyen sigorta şirketleri var.

Biz ise faiz tartışmaları ve katılım bankacılığıyla oyalanıyoruz. Bazı işleri “yapıyormuş” gibi yapıyoruz. Faiz, devalüasyon ve enflasyon arasındaki ilişkiden bile çoğu zaman habersiziz. Bu arada Citibank da katılım bankacılığına girdi; Bahreyn’den sonra Türkiye’ye de geliyorlar.

İngiltere’nin LIBOR’unun yanında, AB ülkelerinin EURIBOR’u (“Euro Interbank Offered Rate”) vardı  aynı aileden (IBOR) bir referans faiz. Bir de ABD dolarında LIBOR’un yerini alan resmî referans, SOFR (“Secured Overnight Financing Rate” Teminatlı Gecelik Finansman Oranı) var. Peki İslam ülkeleri’nin para birimlerinin birbirine çevrilmesi, ulusal paralarla ticaret, bir takas bankası, ortak kredi fonu, reasürans ve ortak kredi kartı gibi konuları kim, ne zaman konuşacak? Üniversitelerimiz, iş dünyası örgütlerimiz (SİAD’lar) bu konuda ne yapıyor? TÜRKPOL’den söz ediyoruz da, “İSOR”u ne zaman konuşmaya başlayacağız?

Aman aman, derdim çok; hangisine yanayım! Yâ Rab, bize akıl, iman, ilim, irfan, hikmet, ihlas ve cesaret ver. Cahil ve zalim yöneticilerin zulmünden kurtulmamız için, bizi nimet verdiklerinin yoluna ilet; gazaba uğrayanların değil. Gelin bir şeyler yapalım ve Allah’ın gazabından O’nun rahmetine sığınalım. Çok geç kaldık; ama dilerim Hz. Yunus kavminin kurtuluşu bize örnek olur. Değilse, daha fazla gecikirsek Lut kavminin başına gelenler bizim de başımıza gelebilir. Selam ve dua ile.

⚠️ Introducing EchoLink: Enterprise-Grade, Zero-Trace Communications
✔️ EchoLink provides fully encrypted, browser-native communications designed specifically for high-security enterprise environments and confidential operations.
Zero-Server Architecture: Session signaling is used strictly for initial handshakes. All media, voice, video, and file transfers are strictly peer-to-peer (P2P), ensuring no intermediate servers intercept or process your data.
Dynamic Key Rotation: Employs industry-standard DTLS-SRTP (media) and SCTP (data) encryption, automatically rotating encryption keys every 7 seconds and generating unique key sets for every session.

text:
🚨🇬🇧 A fellow IXR shareholder just spent 3.5 hours INSIDE Ionic Technologies' Belfast rare earth recycling plant, and held a sealed bag of separated DYSPROSIUM OXIDE, the heavy rare earth everyone says the West can't make. His first-hand account, with photos approved by the company. 🧵

🔗Full Post on HotCopper Can Be Found Here
https://t.co/Iyw3rBrrJr

📍 The Visit

A long-term shareholder (Koproskilo on HotCopper — report and photos shared with his permission) was hosted at Ionic House, Titanic Quarter, Belfast Harbour by Thomas Kelly and Fergal Coleman, the latter straight from Queen's University Belfast that morning, where the MAIL technology was invented by Prof Peter Nockemann, who still sits on the Ionic Tech board.

🔒 Strictly no photos inside after a previous incident risked IP, Thomas took these at predetermined locations and approved them for sharing

🏢 Corporates, financiers and unnamed major tech manufacturers are now regular visitors to the plant

🧲 The Feedstock Machine

Pallets of magnets on site, sorted into buckets by source: EV motor magnets, hard-drive magnets, MRI magnets.

🤝 EMR has ~25 tonnes warehoused a mile away, with pricing being locked in per magnet type, years of unglamorous collaboration maybe only 1–2 other UK/EU operators can match

🆓 As the company's name grows, feedstock is being OFFERED to them, some of it free

♻️ Visitors were told EV makers scrap up to 10% of e-drive motors on epoxy bonding failures, a potential OEM scrap loop, with return-of-swarf clauses planned in every offtake. A true circular economy

🌍 Even reagents are supply-chain conscious: oxalic acid sourced from Spain, not China

⚗️ The Product In Hand: Dy₂O₃

That sealed, labelled bag is dysprosium oxide — a few percent of a magnet's mass but an outsized share of its value, and one of the rare earths China restricts hardest.

🏭 The demo plant has run 24/7 for 30+ months, producing 10+ tonnes of separated REO at 99.5–99.9% purity

🧪 An unnamed peer stuck at 90% purity sent samples to Belfast, Ionic lifted them to 99%. Epoxy-contaminated feed goes to 99%+ with NO pre-cleaning step, while many newer processes can't reach spec on real, untreated feedstock

🚗 The same Belfast oxides Ford just validated in 100% recycled magnets, 99.87% Nd oxide, 99.56% Dy oxide, 99.75% Tb oxide, on the first attempt

🏗️ Demo to Commercial

🔧 New larger mixing tanks just added to the heavy circuit, the Dy/Tb end is being expanded

⚡ Nth Cycle is sending a demo unit to Belfast for installation into the circuit,  the technologies are proving genuinely complementary

📋 Permitting progressing well; the harbour authority welcomes them as a permanent fixture. Long-lead commercial equipment is being specified and quoted NOW, the demo plant's 30 months of bug-hunting is exactly why the commercial ramp should be faster than peers jumping straight from pilot

🎓 ~25 staff and a QUB PhD pipeline for rollouts flagged in the USA, Brazil and beyond, while competitors rehire 80-year-old retirees, China has banned exporting rare earth IP, equipment AND talent

💰 DFS: US$108.7m capex, 400 tpa commercial plant, post-tax NPV US$502m, IRR 43.6%, £12m UK Government offer in principle, FID targeted this quarter

⚠️ Honest caveats: the capital stack still has to close, and the solar-heavy power plan for a city with ~108 sunny days a year is still being optimised (green grid power /Battery and carbon credits under evaluation). Demo scale is not commercial scale, but all the right ingredients are there.

👀 The Bottom Line

📍While others publish renders, IXR ran a "show me" play with its own shareholders, and a retail investor walked the floor, saw the feedstock buckets, and held separated dysprosium oxide in his hands. His takeaway: the commercial plant feels close to fruition.

📍Grade sets the prize, but feedstock partnerships, magnet liberation logistics which is now being executed through the Drive 35, @theapcuk,  UK funded CirculaREEconomy Project with EMR (Feedstock Logistics) and chemistry proven on real, dirty feed win the game, and Belfast is the rare place where all three are visible in one building.

text:
It gets really dicey.

Here's the issue that both my family and our friend's family one street over had/have:

In the 70s, a farmer decided he'd parcel his land out into a little subdivision. He ran some little roads into his land and offered some plots along it for sale.

People bought them and built houses on them.

Fast forward 40 years, and that farmer is dead. His son is dead. His grandson doesn't even live in town. 

And those "roads" are, legally speaking, still rice paddies owned by the farmer, and no one has paid any taxes on them for decades, and the grandson has no intention of paying for them, because... Why would he? He thought they were roads, too! They don't own any of the plots on the roads, so why would he have to pay taxes on a road???

Add to that the fact that these "roads" are not wide enough for a fire truck to get down (especially the 90-degree turn with a 2m dropoff on the side into... a rice paddy). You're not allowed to build on a road like that because it's a public safety issue.

So how do you fix these?

Our friend, when her folks died (they rebuilt their house only about 20 years prior, before the rules got stricter, so it was worth selling), went up and down the street and got everyone to chip in to buy the road and then "donate" it to the city, so it became a real street. However, their road was wide enough and has no insane turns.

For the next one over, ours, we'd have to do that, but then also convince the people on that corner to give up part of their plot, knock down part of their garden wall, and use that space to make the corner passable. We'd likely also have to get everyone along the road to give up a meter or so to widen the street. Notably... we wouldn't have to, because we're at the end of it. Hard ask.

However, even that "ask" isn't going to go anywhere, because THERE ARE 2 MORE AKIYA ON THE STREET and no one knows who we'd even contact, and can't imagine they'd be interested in the project.

So here's where we are:

1) The property and house can be sold, legally.
2) However, the new owners cannot tear the house down and rebuild. They can only "renovate," which means it has to retain the same footprint. This is likely why on "Before After" (if you watch that, which you should), so many times their "renovation" is to tear the whole thing down but 4 corner pillars sticking out of the ground—they can't change the footprint.
3) We'd have to say, "Oh, BTW, if your house starts on fire, the fire department is going to have to park down the block and hope their hoses are long enough.
4) No matter what, at some point, someone is going to have to deal with the "road" that isn't a road, and someone is going to have to pay the taxes on it or SOMETHING. Right now the guy who clears snow for the city just does the road to be nice, but he always says, "Just so you know... I'm not supposed to do this." He also does it only if he has time, which means that I have literally, by hand, shoveled 1 meter of snow down the block to get to where you can get out. Me and another middle-aged guy who lives there (I was visiting for New Year's).

So there's a cautionary tale. This stuff gets very tricky very quickly, even for what looks like a really nice older house in a little subdivision.

When my FIL dies... we're going to have to figure out what to do with it, and I have a bad feeling about whether we'll be able to do much of anything at all.

text:
THE WEEK OPENS IN SHANGHAI TONIGHT, WITHOUT TOKYO, AND SETTLES NOTHING UNTIL THURSDAY:

The last live stock price anywhere on earth was set at Friday's close in New York. The next one gets set tonight, when Shanghai and Hong Kong open at 9:30pm ET - and Tokyo, the market that normally votes first in Asia, will not trade a share until Thursday. That is the handoff into the American week: a read already two days old, from two continents that disagreed with each other, minus the one exchange whose central bank just moved.

The week is back-loaded. Nothing before Wednesday can settle the argument Friday left open, and Thursday carries nearly all of it in a single morning.

Where Friday left Asia:

- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 65,019, +883 pts / +1.38%
- Shanghai Composite: 3,911.87, +36.27 pts / +0.94%
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 24,751, +146 pts / +0.60%

Europe went the other way:

- DAX (Germany): 25,304, -413 pts / -1.60%
- CAC 40 (France): 8,065.02, -122 pts / -1.49%
- FTSE 100 (UK): 10,659, -157 pts / -1.45%

Two central banks moved inside three days, both the same way. On Wednesday, September 16 the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate a quarter point, to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase in three years, with Chair Kevin Warsh signalling at least one more before the year ends. On Friday the Bank of Japan raised its own policy rate a quarter point, to 1.25%, the highest in Japan since 1995, on a 7-2 vote.

Tokyo rose anyway, which is not how markets usually greet dearer money. Two things explain it. Technology shares followed Wall Street up, and fuel got cheaper: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, settled Friday at $103.87, -0.9% on the day and -1.4% on the week - its first weekly fall in three - as traders grew more confident that Saudi production and export operations would restart. Japan buys nearly all its oil abroad, so that discount lands harder there than in most places. The yen still weakened, past 157 per dollar, because two of the nine board members voted against the increase and Governor Kazuo Ueda promised nothing beyond it.

Europe's decline was narrower than a 1.5% index number suggests. Telecom shares alone fell 3.3%, their worst day since April 2025. A continent marked down on two sectors is not a verdict on the world economy.

The sharpest signal of the week sits outside every index above. Gold pays no interest, so holding it costs you whatever cash would have earned instead - and cash now earns more. The Fed raised rates, the dollar index ended the week at 100.215, +1.1%, and the yield on a 10-year loan to the US government rose 7 basis points on Friday - 0.07 of a percentage point - to 5.00%. Each of those three normally pushes gold down. Gold finished Friday at $4,380.01 an ounce, +0.73% on the week, and silver at $66.35, +3.05%. People paid up for metal in the week money got more expensive. That is a market hedging two outcomes at once, not one that has chosen between them.

The bridge to the American open is US index futures - agreements to buy an index at a set price later, and the nearest thing to a live US quote this weekend. They do not restart until 6pm ET tonight. Friday's figures:

- Nasdaq-100 futures: 29,917.25, +471 pts / +1.60%
- S&P 500 futures: 7,712.50, +72.50 pts / +0.95%
- Dow futures: 52,079.00, +272 pts / +0.53%
- Russell 2000 futures: 2,881.50, +5.60 pts / +0.19%

Two cautions on that board matter more than its direction. September's contracts expired at Friday's quarterly settlement - triple witching, when index futures and options lapse together - so a weekend screen can be measuring the new December contract against a September one that no longer exists; treat the size of those moves as unreliable. And a December contract is meant to sit above the index itself. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,650.50, +12.74 pts / +0.17%. The December future at 7,712.50 is 62 points higher, and most of that gap is the cost of holding the position for three months, not anyone's forecast of a higher market.

What the week actually offers, in order.

Monday: the People's Bank of China sets its loan prime rate, the benchmark banks there price mortgages and business loans against, and it is expected to stay at 3.00% for one year and 3.50% for five. That lands Monday morning in Beijing, which is Sunday evening in New York - the week's first hard number arrives before most Americans wake up. Tokyo is shut Monday through Wednesday for Respect for the Aged Day, a bridge holiday and the Autumnal Equinox.

Wednesday: the first real read on the economy. S&P Global publishes preliminary September purchasing managers' indexes for the US, the UK and the euro area - monthly surveys of the people who buy supplies for companies, where anything above 50 means more firms reporting growth than shrinkage. The euro area's composite figure, factories and services together, was 52.0 last month; the UK's is expected near 52.5, against 52.5 before.

Thursday: everything at once. Tokyo reopens. Four central banks report in one morning - the Swiss National Bank, Sweden's Riksbank, Norges Bank and Mexico's Banxico - and all four are widely expected to hold. And Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit, his first to the White House in 11 years, with a large business delegation. The tariff truce struck after last October's meeting in South Korea expires on November 10, and tariffs between the two countries topped 100% before it. The agenda runs through rare earths and critical minerals, limits on Chinese access to advanced American technology, Boeing aircraft, farm purchases, Taiwan and fentanyl. Few expect a grand bargain; an extension of that truce is the thing being watched.

Friday: mainland China is shut for the Mid-Autumn Festival.

Hold the overnight read loosely, and this weekend more loosely than most. Direction set in thin hours fades before New York opens more often than it carries, and Friday is the proof - Asia about 1% higher, Europe about 1.5% lower, American stocks following neither. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,682.64, -95.40 pts / -0.18%, finishing its worst week since March, while the Nasdaq composite closed at 26,522.55, +104.25 pts / +0.39%.

Monday will produce prices all day. It will not produce much information. Thursday produces both at once.

Not investment advice.
