God does not wait until Babylon has finished falling to start singing the victory song. The song is not a strategy they invented. It is the sound of people who have already been taken out of mankind and set with the Lamb. No one else can learn it because no one else has been bought that way.

Counterfeit religion and worship can copy words. It cannot copy redemption. This is why they follow the Lamb wherever He goes. The choir does not choose the route. Wherever He goes includes Zion and the path that led there. 

Where did they come from?

The very same fields from which all the redeemed are taken. Firstfruits are not a sheltered display case. They are wheat from the same field, offered first, still identified with the One who purchased them.

Why the distinction? Why does the Lord need this kind of disciples?

A choir sent ahead of the army cannot afford a false note. The world of chapter 13 runs on image, slogan, and enforced speech. The firstfruits tell the truth. Their song matches their seal. Their feet match their song. 

God does this because He will not let the counterfeit have the first word or the last. Jehoshaphat did not wait until the coalition had collapsed to send the singers out. He sent them while the enemy was still coming. The praise went first; the ambush followed. Their worship is the battle cry. 

Babylon will fall.

The text will say it twice in a few verses. Fallen, fallen.

But God will not let the fall be the first sound. He puts the victory song in the mouths of those who belong to Jesus before the dust of Babylon has even settled. Babylon does not get to set the timing of the praise.

So the distinction is not that God loves a special crop more than the rest of the field. The distinction is that He will have a people whose mouths and feet already match the Name on their foreheads while the counterfeit is still shouting.

Yeah, you're in love with Jesus. 

Yeah, things are hard. 

Yeah, sometimes God doesn't seem interested in answering your prayers. 

That does not take you out of the choir. The firstfruits were not lifted because the field was easy. They were lifted because they had been purchased and they stayed with the Lamb no matter where He took them. 

Love for Jesus does not cancel the hardness. It keeps you on the path the choir does not get to choose. Unanswered prayer is not proof you were planted in the wrong field. It is often the stretch of ground where the song is learned. 

You came from the same fields as all the redeemed. You were not a display case. You are wheat offered first, still identified with the One who bought you. Things are hard. He is still standing. Stay with the Lamb. The timing of the praise was never Babylon’s, and it was never yours to postpone until the prayers feel answered. The song has already started.

Don't stop singing.

The song is already the sound of the purchased, not the sound of people whose field got easy. Hardness does not dismiss you from the choir. Silence does not mean you were sown in the wrong ground. Follow Him wherever He goes. Keep the Name and the song together. Babylon does not get the first word or the last, and it does not get to tell you when to quit.
Don’t stop singing.

Amen 🙏🏼

text:
The Victory Choir

Revelation 14:1-5
"Then I looked, and behold, the Lamb was standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads. And I heard a voice from heaven, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder, and the voice which I heard was like the sound of harpists playing on their harps. And they sang a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one was able to learn the song except the 144,000 who had been purchased from the earth. These are the ones who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are celibate. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These have been purchased from mankind as first fruits to God and to the Lamb. And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless."

That is the picture of those who belong to Jesus in the hour of the world's greatest pressure. No slogans, no counterfeits, not smoke and mirrors. These are the first fruits of the harvest. 

The world, on the other hand in chapter 13 is all about slogans, images, the mark, and enforced worship. The Lamb on Zion is none of that. He simply stands, and those who belong to Him are with Him. 

These 144,000 are not the entire harvest. They are the first portion lifted up to God and the Lamb; proof that the field belongs to Him and that more is coming. Firstfruits are set apart from the rest of mankind, not because they were better raw material, but because they were purchased. 

Do you understand this?

The farmer planted the entirety of the fields. He cultivated the entirety of the fields. He protected the whole from pests and diseases. And he takes His first fruits from that whole harvest. The farmer did not plant two different fields. He planted the whole. He worked the whole. He guarded the whole from what would ruin it.

When the time comes he does not invent a separate crop; he walks into the same field he has been tending and lifts the first ripe portion to God. That first sheaf is not a different kind of wheat. It is wheat from this field, taken first, set apart, offered to God. This is why Revelation 14 can say they were "purchased from the earth" and "purchased from mankind as first fruits to God and to the Lamb."

Why does God do this?

Do you recall the old testament story about how they sent a choir to go out before the enemy? 

The story is about Jehoshaphat in 2 Chronicles 20. 

A vast enemy coalition is coming against Judah. Jehoshaphat is afraid, and he seeks the Lord, and the Spirit answers through Jahaziel. 

"the battle is not yours but God’s. You will not need to fight in the usual way. Stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord."

The next morning Jehoshaphat does something insane looking to every military mind. He appoints singers to praise the beauty of holiness, and he sends the choir out in front of the army. 

As they begin to sing and praise...

"Give thanks to the Lord, for His steadfast love endures forever"

...the Lord sets ambushes.

The enemies turn on one another, confused by what they are witnessing. 

And Judah arrives to find the work already done.

God puts the song first.

He planted the whole field. He cultivated the whole field. He guarded the whole field. When He lifts the first ripe sheaf, He is not sampling to see if the crop is any good. He is declaring, in public, this field is Mine. The first portion goes to Him because the whole already belongs to Him. Firstfruits are the choir walking out in front of the harvest.

The 144,000 are that first sheaf and that choir. They stand and sing with the Lamb on Zion while the beast is still marking the earth for destruction. The 144,000 sing a new song no one else can learn, before the throne, before the living creatures and the elders, while the slogans and the image and the enforced worship are still loud and proud on the ground.

text:
Let’s talk about BioLongevity Labs and its owner, Jay Campbell.

My issue isn’t with the people buying or using the products. It’s with a company asking customers to pay premium prices while its owner appears incapable of responding to even mild criticism without resorting to personal attacks.

Question the pricing? You’re a “hater.”

Question the evidence? You’re “jealous.”

Question the person selling it? Here comes another insult instead of a substantive answer.

That isn’t confidence. Confident companies welcome scrutiny because they can answer it with transparent sourcing, credible testing, defensible pricing, and evidence proportional to their claims. They don’t need the owner to turn every disagreement into a public tantrum.

BioLongevity Labs seems to rely heavily on Jay’s personal brand and marketing mythology to justify prices that, in my opinion, are wildly inflated. Premium branding does not automatically mean premium science. A loud founder, polished messaging, and an army of loyal supporters do not replace data—and popularity certainly does not make a company immune from criticism.

What makes the whole thing especially ridiculous is Jay calling legitimate criticism “jealousy.” Jealous of what, exactly? Selling expensive products and melting down whenever someone asks an uncomfortable question?

This industry already has enough exaggerated claims, personality cults, and influencers treating basic skepticism like a personal betrayal. Nobody operating in the research or longevity space should be above scrutiny—especially someone charging a premium and presenting himself as an authority.

If BioLongevity Labs offers exceptional value, demonstrate it. Explain the pricing. Publish the relevant evidence. Address specific criticism with specific answers. That is how serious operators behave.

But when the owner’s default response is “you’re jealous,” he isn’t disproving the criticism. He’s demonstrating why more people should be asking questions.

The research space needs fewer untouchable personalities and more transparency, accountability, and evidence. No founder—and no overpriced brand—is exempt.

Today’s commemorated feasts and saints
16th SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST — Tone 7. Afterfeast of the Elevation of the Cross. Sunday after Elevation.  Greatmartyr Eustáthios (Eustace) Placidas, his wife, Martyr Theopistes, and their children, Martyrs Agapius and Theopistus, of Rome (ca. 118). Holy Martyr and Confessor Michael and his councilor, Theodore, Wonderworkers of Chernigov (1245). Rt. Blv. Oleg, Prince of Briansk (ca. 1280). Monastic Martyr Hilarion of St. Anne Skete (Mt. Athos—1804).

Greatmartyr Eustáthios Placidas, with his wife and children, of Rome
Commemorated on September 20 
Before his Baptism, the Holy Great Martyr Eustáthios was named Plakidas (Πλακίδας). He was a Roman General in the reigns of Emperors Titus (79-81) and Trajan (98-117). Even before he came to know Christ, Plakidas devoted himself to charitable endeavors, helping the poor and destitute. Therefore, the Lord did not allow this virtuous pagan to continue in the darkness of idolatry.

One day, while hunting in a forest, he saw a remarkable stag which stopped now and then to stare at him. Plakidas pursued it on horseback, but could not catch up. The stag jumped over a chasm and stood on the other side facing him. Suddenly, Plakidas saw a radiant Cross between its antlers. The General was astonished to hear a voice coming from the Cross saying, “Why do you pursue me, Plakidas?”

“Who are You, Master?” asked Plakidas. The voice replied, “I am Jesus Christ, Whom you do not know, but by your good deeds, you honor me. I have appeared here on this creature for your sake, to draw you into the net of my love for mankind. It is not fitting that one as righteous as you should worship idols and remain ignorant of the truth. It was to save mankind that I came into the world.”

Plakidas cried out, “Lord, I believe that You are the God of Heaven and earth, the Creator of all things. Master, teach me what I should do.” Again the Lord replied, “Go to the bishop of your country and receive Baptism from him, and he will instruct you.”

Plakidas returned home and joyfully recounted everything to his wife Tatiana. She in turn told him of a strange dream she had the evening before, in which she had been told, “Tomorrow you, your husband and your sons shall come to me and know that I am the true God.” The couple then proceeded to do as they had been told.

They hastened to the Christian bishop, who baptized all their family, and then communed them with the Holy Mysteries. Plakidas was renamed Eustáthios, his wife was called Theopistē, and their children, Agapios and Theopistos.

On the following day, Saint Eustáthios went to the place of his miraculous conversion and there he gave thanks to the Lord for having called him to the path of salvation.

Saint Eustáthios received another a miraculous revelation. The Lord Himself predicted his impending tribulations: “Eustáthios, you shall suffer many misfortunes, as did Job, but in the end you will conquer the devil.”

Soon Saint Eustáthios was afflicted with misfortune: all of his servants died of the plague, and his cattle perished. Brought to ruin, but not despairing in spirit, Saint Eustáthios and his family secretly abandoned their home, to live in poverty unknown, humble, and poor.

They went to Egypt to board a ship bound for Jerusalem. During the voyage the Saint experienced more sorrow. Captivated by Theopistē's beauty, the ship owner cruelly set Eustáthios and his children ashore, keeping the wife for himself.

With great sadness the Saint continued on his way, and new calamity befell him. Coming to a tempestuous river, he went to carry his two sons across in turn. When he brought the first one across, the other was seized by a lion and was carried off into the wilderness. As he turned back to shore, a wolf dragged the other child into the forest.

Saint Eustáthios wept bitterly, but he realized that Divine Providence had sent him these misfortunes in order to test his endurance and devotion to God. Saint Eustáthios prepared himself for even more sorrows, knowing that one who endures temptations and has been tested will receive the crown of life which God has promised to those who love Him (James 1:12).

In the village of Badessos he found work and spent five years in ceaseless toil. Saint Eustáthios did not know at the time that by God's mercy, shepherds and farmers had rescued his sons, and they were living near him. He was also unaware that the impudent shipowner had been struck down with a terrible disease and died, leaving Saint Theopistē untouched. She lived in peace and freedom at the place where the ship landed.

During this time it had become difficult for Emperor Trajan to raise an army for Rome to deal with a rebellion, for the soldiers refused to go into battle without Plakidas. They advised Trajan to send men out to all the cities to search for him.

Antiochos and Akakios, who were friends of Plakidas, sought him in various places. Finally, they arrived in the village where Saint Eustáthios lived. The soldiers found him, but they did not recognize him. They began telling him about the person they sought, asking for his help and promising him a large reward. Saint Eustáthios recognized his friends right away, but he did not disclose his identity to them.

Borrowing money from one of his friends, he prepared a meal for his visitors. As they looked at him, they noticed that he resembled their former commander. When they saw a scar on his shoulder from a deep wound made by a sword, they realized that it was their friend who stood before them. They embraced him with tears and told him why they had been looking for him.

Saint Eustáthios returned to Rome with them and was restored to his former rank. Many new recruits were drafted into the army from all over the Empire. He did not know that the two young soldiers who served him, and whom he loved for their skill and daring, were actually his own sons. They did not realize that they were serving under the command of their own father, nor that they were brothers by birth.

While on campaign, the army led by Eustáthios halted at a certain place. One night, the brothers were talking in their tent. The elder spoke about his life, how he had lost his mother and brother, and how he had been parted from his father. The younger brother then realized that the other man was his own brother, and revealed how he had been rescued from the wolf.

A woman overheard their conversation, since their tent was pitched right next to her house, and she realized that these were her sons. Without identifying herself to them, but not wishing to be separated from them, she went to their general, Saint Eustáthios, and asked that he take her to Rome with him. She said she had been a prisoner, and wanted to go home. Then she came to recognize the general as her husband, and with tears she told him about herself, and about the two soldiers who were their sons. Thus, through God's great mercy, the entire family was reunited.

Soon thereafter, the rebellion was crushed, and Saint Eustáthios returned to Rome with honor and glory. Emperor Trajan had died in the meantime, and his successor Hadrian (117-138) wanted to celebrate the victory with a solemn sacrifice to their "gods." To everyone's amazement, Saint Eustáthios did not go to the pagan temple. The Emperor ordered them to find him and bring him to the temple.

“Why don’t you want to worship the gods?” the Emperor inquired. “You, above all others, should offer thanks to them. Not only did they preserve you in war and grant you victory, but they also helped you to find your wife and children.” Saint Eustáthios replied: “I am a Christian and I glorify and give thanks to Christ, and I offer sacrifice to Him. I owe my life to Him. I do not know or believe in any other God.”

Outraged, the Emperor ordered him to remove his military belt and brought Eustáthios and his family before him. They did not succeed in persuading the steadfast confessors of Christ to offer sacrifice to idols. The Saint's family was sentenced to be torn to pieces by wild beasts, but the animals would not touch the holy martyrs.

Then the cruel Emperor ordered that they be thrown alive into a red-hot brass bull, and Saint Eustáthios, his wife Theopistē, and their sons Agapios and Theopistos suffered martyrdom. Before being placed inside the bull, Saint Eustathios prayed, “Grant, O Lord, Thy grace to our relics, and grant a place in Thy Kingdom to all who call upon us, Though they call upon us when in danger on a river, or on the sea, we entreat Thee to come to their aid.”

Three days later, they opened the brass bull, and the bodies of the holy martyrs were found unscathed. Not one hair of their heads was singed, and their faces shone with an unearthly beauty. Many who witnessed this miracle came to believe in Christ. Some pious Christians buried the bodies of the Saints with all honor and reverence.

text:
📚Article on NICAP from the June 1968 issue of Industrial Research

SPECIAL REPORT

UFO study credibility cloud?

“I AM NOT MYSELF A BELIEVER, rather more of an agnostic on the matter of whether these reportings of objects portend more than we have been led to believe.”

The speaker was Rep. J. Edward Roush (D-Ind.), commenting on the controversy developing around the University of Colorado project investigating unidentified flying objects.

Noting that it “raises great doubts as to the scientific profundity and objectivity of the project,” the member of the House Science & Astronautics Committee has called for a congressional investigation, an evaluation by the Comptroller General of the United States, and comments by the Secretary of the Air Force.

It appears the controversy surrounding the discharge of two of the Colorado study staff members, resignation of a third, publication of a memo allegedly “stolen” from project files, and press statements attributed to the project’s director have enveloped the effort in a credibility cloud, which may jeopardize public acceptance of the study conclusions.

Industrial Research has managed to penetrate the secrecy that the university has wrapped around the project and obtained two documents generated by its management, which offer insight into the subjects to be treated in the final 800- to 1,100-page report expected in late September. As a result, these conclusions emerge:

■ The project does not “stress investigation of the people doing the observing, rather than of physical phenomena, as proposed in the notorious memo.

■ There appears to be no effort in the study directed at a serious evaluation of extraterrestrial hypotheses.

■ A follow-on investigation apparently will be proposed in the final report, in a chapter that treats future government handling of UFOs.

The rhubarb that caught Roush’s attention flared with publication of an article in Look magazine, authored by John G. Fuller, who reported a “near-mutiny by several staff members,” and labeled the study a “$500,000 trick.” Fuller wrote “Incident at Exeter,” the book that attempted to link the Northeast blackout to flying saucers.

Another UFO buff, Maj. Donald E. Keyhoe, director of the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP), Washington, cited “evidence of grave deficiencies” in a letter to President Johnson, and tagged the project a “failure.”

Keyhoe, who had cooperated with Colorado for 17 months before severing relations, quoted Robert J. Low, project coordinator, as noting that if Dr. Edward U. Condon, scientific director of the study, “were to write a report today, the conclusion would be negative.” However, Low acknowledged that this was not the view of all the project’s scientists.

Key element in the controversy is a memo prepared by Low two months before the contract was awarded to the university and before Low heard the story presented by Air Force people to the university.

What were the words that launched the critics into orbit?

“Our study would be conducted almost exclusively by nonbelievers who, although they couldn’t possibly prove a negative result, could and probably would add an impressive body of evidence that there is no reality to the observations. The trick would be, I think, to describe the project so that, to the public, it would appear a totally objective study, but to the scientific community, would present the image of a group of nonbelievers trying their best to be objective but having an almost zero expectation of finding a saucer.

“One way to do this would be to stress investigation, not of the physical phenomena, but rather of the people doing the observing. . . . If the emphasis were placed here, rather than on an examination of the old question of the physical reality of the saucer, I think the scientific community would quickly get the message.”

Low also examined some of the arguments for and against taking on the study, the problems of finding “prestigious” journals willing to publish results, and the admittedly premature nature of his views.

In Keyhoe’s letter to the President, Low’s seemingly biased attitude is compared to the contract’s requirements that an objective study was to be conducted by “investigators who, as carefully as can be determined, have no predictions or preconceived positions on the UFO question.”

Besides challenging Low’s objectivity, the critics also assail Condon for his failure to participate in field investigations and the “strongly biased” tone of remarks attributed to him in the lay press. One example: “My attitude right now is that there’s nothing to it, . . . but I’m not supposed to reach a conclusion for another year.” (Elmira, N.Y., Star-Gazette, Jan. 26, 1967.)

Thus, on the surface, what started out as a calm, objective scientific study of UFO phenomena has become ensnarled in controversy. Is all the heat justified? Is there a Colorado side to the issue? What is the reaction of the Air Force, which is funding the contract?

The official statement of the Air Force says: “The report on the UFO study being conducted by the University of Colorado has not yet been completed, reviewed by the National Academy of Sciences, or submitted to the Air Force; and we believe it would be inappropriate and premature for the Air Force to comment at this time.”

Thomas Ratchford, project scientist, Air Force Office of Scientific Research, is monitoring the contract. He told Industrial Research that the study is “an independent one,” given the same degree of freedom granted any basic research contractor. He apparently was not impressed by Fuller’s credentials and noted that similar articles “have appeared in many magazines in the past.”

Surprisingly, nine days after the article had appeared, Ratchford had not seen the Low memorandum. But his own reaction, based on what he had heard, was that “it’s a quite reasonable document for generation in the context of when it was generated.”

He also was unimpressed by the charges that Condon had not carried out field investigations. “The function of a productive scientist is to come up with ideas, not necessarily to go out and read the dials—this analogy applies to Condon.

“My personal observations have been that Dr. Condon is an outstandingly open-minded person. . . . I have not seen any evidence which indicates that he’s biased.” Ratchford realizes, however, that such an opinion will be discounted as coming from an Air Force source.

When Industrial Research contacted Condon, he declined to comment on the Look article, other than noting he had dispatched a telegram to Gardner Cowles, the magazine’s publisher, suggesting he “ought to review the situation with me personally in the interests of truth and responsibility in publishing.”

Condon confirms the Low memo was authentic, charging: “It was stolen from our files!”

When asked whether the study was biased toward an examination of the observers, Condon replied, “No, certainly not. It is an excellent study and it’s going forward and it will be finished. Our report will be ready toward the end of September.”

He declined to explain why the two staff members were discharged, beyond noting it was “for cause.”

Just what is the investigation doing?

“We’re not talking about the study until the report is in,” he replied. “We’re telling that consistently to everybody, so people are just going to have to wait until we get it done. . . .

“The stuff you see on it is based on no facts on it whatsoever—speculation and guesses by other people. Anything you see that purports to describe what we’re doing is without any foundation in fact.”

However, Industrial Research has obtained copies of documents already generated by the Condon group which provide considerable insight into the nature of the study and the topics to be covered in the final report.

Ratchford was asked if any reports had been prepared during the course of the study. He said there were two, but they didn’t say very much, and no more were expected because of the approaching final report. The two reports were available for public viewing in a Pentagon office, he stated.

But the Air Force press people who handle UFO queries seemed unaware the documents existed and were surprised when they were requested. A call was placed to Ratchford, who told them what the titles were and where to look for them. Within minutes, a copy of each document was supplied to Industrial Research.

One was a progress report for the period between Nov. 1, 1966 through Mar. 31, 1967. The second was a proposal for extending the contract beyond its originally scheduled expiration date. This latter document—dated July 1967—offers the greatest insight into the project’s activities.

It requested an eight-month extension and an additional $259,146 in funds. (The original contract was $313,000.) But the cost figure was an overestimate on Colorado’s part, and it later was reduced to $183,146, without change in the planned program.

Both documents make it clear that whereas the Low memo suggested investigation “not of the physical phenomena, but rather of the people who do the observing,” the study has a heavy effort centered on examination of possible physical explanations of UFO phenomena. The people studies, however, are not neglected.

There is no evidence that the extraterrestrial hypothesis is receiving attention. It is not on the list of 12 tasks spelled out in the progress report, unless it falls under the category entitled: “Search for further hypotheses, not now known, that might be advanced to explain UFOs.”

The progress report noted early activities were directed to familiarization with known data and literature on the UFO phenomenon and “arriving at a reasonable, defensible methodology.”

Pointing out that development of a methodology had taken “twice as long as anticipated,” the proposal detailed the roles of the study team members and contractors. Success of the study was seen linked to whether or not the methodology solution was solved “imaginatively and effectively.”

Of particular interest is the role of Dr. David R. Saunders, a Dept. of Psychology professor who was one of the two staff members discharged by Condon. Saunders was responsible for:

■ Directing acquisition, cataloging, and organization of the sightings file, using raw material primarily from Air Force and NICAP sources.

■ Developing the interview and sighting report forms.

■ Handling statistical analyses of the 1,200 sighting reports coded for machine study.

Saunders also was given responsibility, says the proposal, for “decision making leading to the signal to send investigating teams into the field to study reports of sightings.” Low was to make that decision in his absence.

Fuller’s Look article, however, states that “it seemed to some of the staff that several potentially interesting cases were turned down for investigation by Low for what were apparently specious reasons.” On another occasion, according to Fuller, Saunders “reminded Low that he had blocked the investigation of one particularly startling case. Low protested that the investigation on this was completed. No mention was made of any dissatisfaction with Saunders’s work.”

This choice-of-sightings problem was discussed in the proposal.

“It is our intention to investigate only those sightings that show promise of yielding additional (italics added) information about the nature of the UFO phenomenon. Criteria are needed for determining which sightings, if investigated, would be most likely to contribute to that end. We now have those criteria.”

Other details of the Colorado project efforts are summarized in the accompanying table. The study’s conclusions, obviously, were not part of the proposal and must await publication of the final report.—ALFRED J. COTE JR., WASHINGTON EDITOR.

Key features of UFO study

Search for an Answer

A $50,000 Stanford Research Institute contract to catalog knowledge of optical mirages, atmospheric scintillation and extinction, and known phenomena that produce false radar echoes.

A $5,000 study of the lack of sonic booms associated with sightings, and implications about the solidity of observed phenomena.

A $15,000 contract for photoanalysis and photogrammetric studies of five sets of pictures.

A $5,000 examination of the link between UFO sightings and power blackouts.

Chemical and radioisotope tests of a limited number of artifacts alleged to be associated with UFO sightings.

Examination of hypotheses that “blobs of solar plasma that reach the earth with magnetic fields of the order of several thousand gauss” might produce UFO reports.

Evaluation of radar sightings in light of present radar technology.

Aids to Investigation

Two field teams, equipped and ready on “instant notice.”

Manual of instructions for future UFO investigations.

Instrumentation for investigation teams.

Interview and sighting report forms.

Instrumentation cost effectiveness study related to possible future observational programs.

Criteria for selection of sightings promising additional information about the nature of the phenomena.

Case book of the most interesting sightings, prepared by a law student, to maximize objectivity and neutrality of the presentation.

Statistical analysis of data from more than 1,200 sightings.

Questions of evidence as viewed by a lawyer.

Catalog of the whole field of photographs, with appropriate critical comment.

And a Look at the People Problem

A “cultural history” of UFO phenomena from biblical times to 1946 to reveal the extent to which reports reflect cultures of the times or man’s tendency to see “that which at the moment is at the forward edge of technical advance.”

Relationship between press reports and frequency and character of sightings.

Assessment of how closely reports of sightings correspond with actual physical events.

Problems in visual perception and cognition.

‘Conflict has potential to escalate rapidly’: US issues Mideast warnings as Trump leaves Camp David early

Alert follows Houthi missile attack on Riyadh as Iran sets conditions for talks, threatens Hormuz closure and warns it is ready for ‘decisive war’

Lior Ben Ari, Daniel Edelson, New York

U.S. President Donald Trump returned to the White House earlier than expected from Camp David on Saturday as fighting in Yemen escalated following a Houthi ballistic missile attack targeting the Saudi capital, Riyadh.

The White House gave no explanation for Trump’s early return from the presidential retreat in Maryland, a day before he had originally been scheduled to leave. His return came as the United States issued another series of warnings about tensions in the Middle East, this time specifically citing the Houthis alongside Iran.

“Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation,” the U.S. warning said, urging Americans in the region to remain vigilant and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.

The warning said the Iran-backed Houthis were engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks affecting civilian airports, and cautioned that the conflict could escalate rapidly.
The State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to or through the Middle East.

It also reiterated that U.S. diplomatic facilities, including those outside the region, have previously been targeted and warned that Iran and Iran-aligned groups could target other U.S. interests, businesses, institutions and citizens overseas.

Warnings were issued by U.S. embassies across the region, including in Israel, Oman, Lebanon, Iraq, Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

Saudi Arabia said the Houthi attack on Riyadh involved a ballistic missile that was intercepted. Residents reported hearing explosions, and flames and thick smoke were seen near the airport. Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage from the missile itself.

The Saudi-led coalition also said the Houthis attempted to strike civilian infrastructure in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, as well as Taif, Baysh and Farasan, but that those attacks were thwarted. Yanbu is a crucial outlet for Saudi oil exports.

The Houthis offered a different account, saying they had attacked “sensitive sites” in Riyadh and facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in Yanbu. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the strikes caused major fires. The claims were not independently verified.

Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, meanwhile, said Tehran would not return to the previous terms for negotiations with Washington or allow normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz until Iran’s demands were met and the United States honored its commitments.

Iran lays out its conditions

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told Qatar’s Al Jazeera on Saturday that Tehran was prepared for what he called a “decisive war” while saying Iran had presented the Trump administration with seven conditions for reopening negotiations.

Rezaei also said Iran’s current nuclear doctrine remained unchanged and that Tehran continued to abide by a religious decree prohibiting nuclear weapons, though he suggested future developments could affect its position.

“Trump’s threats will not achieve any results,” Rezaei told Al Jazeera. “We are prepared for a decisive war.”

Rezaei said Iran was in contact with mediators Qatar and Pakistan and that Doha had relayed Tehran’s conditions to Washington. He said Iran was awaiting Trump’s response.

The publicly disclosed conditions include ending the war on all fronts, releasing frozen Iranian funds and lifting the U.S. naval blockade restricting Iranian oil exports. Tehran has not publicly detailed all seven demands.

The demands resemble conditions Iran previously raised in connection with restrictions on passage through the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway through which a significant share of the world’s oil trade normally passes.

The United States has been conducting operations aimed at protecting shipping and maintaining the flow of oil through the region as the conflict has disrupted energy markets and kept crude prices elevated.

The escalation has increasingly drawn the Houthis into the wider regional confrontation.

The group has launched missile and one-way attack drone strikes against Saudi oil and energy infrastructure, while Saudi Arabia has carried out waves of airstrikes against Houthi-controlled areas in Yemen as it supports forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

Saree confirmed that the Houthis launched their first attack on Riyadh since the latest escalation overnight Friday into Saturday.

He said the group struck “sensitive sites” in the Saudi capital and an Aramco facility in Yanbu.

Yanbu has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia as an alternative outlet for oil exports amid severe disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi energy infrastructure has also faced attacks elsewhere during the regional conflict, adding to concerns over the reliability of alternative export routes.

The Houthis said their attacks were retaliation for continuing Saudi airstrikes in Yemen.

Saree claimed Saudi Arabia had carried out 732 airstrikes since the latest escalation, a figure that could not be independently verified.

The Houthi spokesman also rejected Saudi allegations that the group had launched a drone toward Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, calling the accusation false.

Saudi Arabia had accused the Houthis of targeting the city earlier in the week, an allegation the group denied.

Saree said the Houthis would continue what he described as a policy of “blockade for blockade” and “escalation for escalation” until Saudi attacks ended and restrictions imposed on Houthi-controlled Yemen were lifted.

The Houthis have long accused Saudi Arabia of imposing an air and sea blockade on areas under their control.

Even before the latest escalation, the group had announced what it called a naval blockade targeting Saudi shipping.

It remains unclear how the renewed Saudi-Houthi fighting will affect the broader confrontation involving Iran and the United States.

The Houthis, who are aligned with Tehran but maintain their own leadership and decision-making structure, have made rapid territorial gains in Yemen in recent weeks and expanded their position along the Red Sea coast.

The escalation has heightened concerns over both Saudi oil exports and shipping through the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandab, one of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints.

Former U.S. diplomat Joey Hood told CNN that Houthi advances in the Red Sea could strengthen Iran’s position in its broader confrontation with Washington and complicate attempts to negotiate with Tehran.

“Iran is now in an existential struggle and is mobilizing all its proxies to fight,” Hood said, according to CNN.

He added that while the Houthis are not remotely controlled by Tehran, they rely on Iranian support, meaning their stated reasons for launching the current offensive may not fully explain the timing of the escalation.

Series of great articles from the May 1969 issue of American Engineer, with frequent mentions of NICAP. 

UFO’s And The Technological Community

Unidentified flying objects have been with us now for at least two decades. The phenomena have passed through the hands of a generation of assorted cultists, cranks, and visionaries. The time has come, claims this consulting engineer, to enlist the full resources of the technological community in an examination of these persistent and as yet unexplained sighting reports.

By Robert F. Morse, P.E.
Brandt & Morse
Consulting Engineers
Richmond, Virginia

On June 24, 1947, Kenneth Arnold, a Boise, Idaho, businessman, was piloting his light plane in the vicinity of Mt. Rainier, Washington, when he was astonished to see nine objects in a row flying from north to south at 9500 feet altitude. The five-mile-long chain of unidentifieds dipped and changed course slightly every few seconds, swerving in and out amongst mountain peaks. Arnold later stated that they “flew like a saucer would if you skipped it across the water.” Hence, Mr. Arnold had the dubious distinction of originating the phrase “flying saucer.” Since Arnold’s famed 1947 sighting, the United States, in fact the entire world, has been consciously subjected to the puzzling and fascinating enigma of unidentified flying objects. Yet today, some 20 years later, we truly seem no nearer to positive identification than we were at the commencement of this mystery.
Certainly we should be asking the obvious “why?”; why is it that with the greatest assemblage of scientific minds and technological equipment since the dawn of history, the simple “whys and wherefores” of this elusive “will-o’-the-wisp” cannot be ascertained? It would logically appear that a society that has the intelligence to unlock the tightly held secrets of the atom, to transport close-up images of distant heavenly bodies to receiving equipment on earth, and to transplant various human organs should have the capability to determine the nature of these persistent sightings. In the minds of many is the firm conviction that we do have that capability.
Proceeding on the assumption that we do have the native intelligence, and that through the years we have honed our scientific and engineering abilities to a fine edge, we must irrevocably arrive at the conclusion that the scientific community is disinterested, and that it much prefers to dwell in its “ivory towers” of conservatism and conventionalism. Yet this is an enigma unto itself as the scientific mind is supposedly primed with vast quantities of curiosity. In fact, is not our purported natural curiosity the basic key to great advance on numerous scientific fronts? Still, it must be admitted that the “hands off” attitude of the community may be largely defensible, as few self-respecting scientists, or engineers, would care to associate with, or unwittingly be the tool of, some of the charlatans drawn into the UFO fray. Also, it generally is not construed as a wise business practice for that relatively large percentage of the community that earns its livelihood in the direct or indirect employ of the Federal government to discount the preachments of the Air Force, which, for 20 years has indoctrinated the public with the fallacy that there is no evidence that the UFO exists, and if indeed it does, there has been absolutely no indication of any activity to our detriment.
Therefore, must we deduce that moving counter to certain postulates from the Air Force and the stigma attached to the investigation of a phenomenon attractive to the practitioners of chicanery are the sole deterrents against employing the scientific method for the purpose of unraveling UFO facts? Of course not! Upon careful examination, other factors come into focus. For example, there are considerations such as the ridicule and indignity experienced by certain well-meaning citizens who thought it vital to their country’s security to report sightings, the tremendous divergence in the details of eyewitness descriptions, and the rather laborious treatises of a small number of apparently sincere scientists who seem to believe that they have a moral obligation to castigate any phenomenon which does not fit into an acceptable pattern of established criteria.

Undoubtedly, there are other valid reasons, but the aforementioned, when displayed against a background of incredulous public opinion, have had the effect of nullifying the scientific method of investigation in reference to UFO questions.

Be that as it may, in spite of a record of apathy relating to any concerted scientific detection efforts to resolve the UFO intrigue, there are now becoming apparent some encouraging signs recognizable to those of us who have spent much time in personal investigative research. We are now noticing that in the course of lecture presentations to various organizations, public opinion is markedly changing from one characterized by disbelief to a mixture of views ranging from open-mindedness to credibility concerning the phenomenon. We are also finding that scientists and engineers are beginning to shed their timidity and are stepping forward to be counted, likely as a result of the respectability precipitated by the University of Colorado’s Research Grant awarded from the Air Force; this grant most probably being attributable to congressional and National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP) pressure for scientific investigation. We are finding scholarly rebuttals appearing in prominent scientific journals in response to the UFO “debunkers,” a group seemingly led by Dr. Donald H. Menzel, former director of Harvard Observatory, and Mr. William Markowitz, professor of physics at Marquette University. These gentlemen have, for publication, repeatedly and unconvincingly tried to identify the UFO with known phenomena. Professor Markowitz has further espoused that all investigations should be stopped on the proposition that the UFO, as a manifestation of extraterrestrial investigation, is untenable. One cannot help but ponder why such illustrious men of science appear to have lost touch with the methodical and unprejudiced approach to the unknown that their vocation demands.

Those of us concerned with the study of UFO’s detect hopeful signs in the very fact that certain institutions of higher learning are becoming increasingly involved and interested, with a filter center having been established at a northeastern college for the purpose of receiving UFO reports, and a course in UFO study having been organized at a prominent western university. It is also noteworthy to state that Dr. J. Allen Hynek, the renowned astrophysicist and chief scientific consultant for the Air Force on the subject of UFO’s, has indicated there is a definite need for serious investigation far in excess of the twenty-year, somewhat less than spectacular, effort by the Air Force.

Perhaps it would seem to some who read this article that we are attempting to enlarge and emphasize a mundane matter. Actually, UFO’s have not evidenced any hostility and have seemingly not affected our life and times one iota, either for good or for bad. Yet to draw a parallel, although the citizens of our country have, fortunately, never felt the effects of a nuclear holocaust, this fact alone does not mean that we have not taken reasonable precautions for that possibility. Likewise, it would seem that we must prepare ourselves to cope rationally with a phenomenon of such probable import as the UFO. There is no attempt here to even hint that the UFO constitutes a hostile force, but the simple fact remains that we do not know this for certain. Hence, by neglecting a total and serious investigation from the standpoint of science and engineering, we are faced with the uncertainty of the nature of the UFO without preparedness. Is this not analogous to behaving as the proverbial ostrich with its head buried in the sand? However, let me stress that readiness on our part must not be calculated only in terms of resistance to hostile acts. Rather, this readiness must be presented as a carefully considered attitude of rational, perhaps even worldwide, posture should we suddenly find thrust into our midst a profoundly intelligent culture which would leave us pale by comparison. Should the UFO be found to be a manifestation of stellar visitation, then quite obviously our intelligentsia would be no match.

Although I have formulated personal conclusions as to the nature of UFO’s, the admission must be made that even after 20 years of investigative effort I can present no concrete evidence documenting my conclusions, any more so than can the skeptics support their theories. Since a conclusion is, in such an instance, merely a personally satisfying resolution of the problem presenting itself to an individual’s mind, in terms of available data, there still remains to be garnered the irrefutable documentary evidence whereby the masses will know the nature of the UFO, in terms of facts. Such evidence is, of necessity, costly and time-consuming to accumulate, and is thus beyond the reach of the individual, or for that matter, of any small organizational group. The solution will be forthcoming only as the result of concerted national, or even global, effort. The resources and equipment required will be enormous, unless some unusual stroke of luck should place the evidence in hand, and this seems highly doubtful in view of past experience. The task is difficult, but I have high hopes that my fellow constituents will apply the logical mind and sound approach characteristic of their professions toward the pursuance of substantiating evidence. However, unless the scientific community warms to the task with inspirational interest and curiosity, the end will not be in sight. Each scientist and engineer should begin to search, with some diligence, his personal convictions as to the true character of the UFO. In fact, should this occur, I can only foresee a considerable portion of the community expressing boundless interest and concern. Such increasing attention, referenced against the backdrop of the University of Colorado’s grant, and the recently stated pronouncements of a number of the world’s foremost scientists, could well be the catalyst necessary to snowball public opinion into demanding a properly conducted, sufficiently resourceful, and adequately financed international investigation.

Perhaps you may consider it unnecessary to push for a large-scale undertaking when the University of Colorado appears to be conducting serious work, exactly along the lines advocated. Also, you are almost certain to ask why we should expend money for such an investigation when our economy is already drained by the effects of a war in Asia and the social-economic programs here at home.

First of all, the Colorado project should be placed in proper perspective. It is an important effort, but cannot be likened to more than the bottom rung of a ladder, which must be painstakingly ascended in order to reach the top, or in essence, to acquire the ultimate answer. There is an overwhelming amount of data to sift through, and much of it is of a questionable nature. Without a considerably more permanent effort than the short-term project mentioned, it is hard to conceive of results amounting to more than mere unproved conclusions. In fact, Dr. Hynek, who is apparently greatly concerned about the effectiveness of the project, responded recently to a question posed by a reporter from the Richmond News Leader, that in the event the Colorado project report was completely negative in its findings, some very interesting things would happen; he would make use of his personal file of good sightings. Certainly a statement of this nature, coming from this particular man who commenced his investigations as an avowed skeptic, should be noted for its courage and conviction.

Whether we sufficiently stimulate man’s innate gnawing curiosity to push investigation ahead, or whether we move in that direction out of fear for what answer the skies may hold, the motive no longer is paramount. Only the finalized answer attains importance as it may conceivably be the key that will stimulate and mold man’s aspirations for the future. Furthermore, if we should eventually find that the UFO has been the tangible sign of amicable explorers from afar, then the intellect can only grope at the benefits that can accrue to mankind by association with phenomenally advanced and useful technology. Such benefits would likely be sociological as well as scientific, and I would view as most unlikely any civilization having matured to a highly advanced state in its manipulation of the physical sciences without having obtained great maturity from a sociological standpoint. Certainly, we on earth could benefit from the latter, as we know that social ills have time and again proven to be self-destructive.

Regardless, should the UFO’s definitely prove to be extraterrestrial, we must face the certainty that they will either be peaceful or hostile. It would behoove us to take steps to be in the position to avail ourselves of potential friendship, and in kind, we must be prepared to contribute however we can. Conversely, should the visitors prove to be hostile, we must be ready and willing to defend ourselves.

In summary, it is tantamount that we commence investigation. It is the opinion of many scientific and engineering minds that the ability, resources, and technical equipment are available. The challenge is indeed unmistakable, and in order to allow us to adequately plan our actions, the scientific and technological community must not be found lacking in providing the facts. It is a personal conviction that we, as a civilized society, must be ready for the challenge when presented.—End.

Four small holes, lower left, about ¾ inches deep and ½ inch wide were found in the road. The burned spot, lower right, is at the center of an X formed by straight lines from the four holes. Engineer Involvement In UFO Investigations

The Massachusetts Investigating Subcommittee of the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena is an example of engineering organization at the state level. During 1967, approximately 100 unidentified sightings were investigated in Massachusetts under engineer supervision.

By Raymond E. Fowler
Project Administrative Engineer
Sylvania Minuteman Program Office

Engineers are basically problem solvers. This is true whether they are involved in research and development or in the improvement by modification of already existing equipments, systems, and processes. Therefore, it should not be surprising that a variety of engineering talent has been called upon to assist in solving what some scientists are calling the “greatest scientific problem of our times”—the UFO problem.

NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, directed by retired Marine Major Donald Keyhoe, has been a pioneer in the investigation of the UFO problem since 1956. Early members of its Board of Governors included Vice Admiral Roscoe Hillenkoetter, former CIA chief, and Admiral Delmar Fahrney, former chief of the Navy Guided Missile Division. A broad range of scientific and engineering talent is found within NICAP’s panel of special advisers, affiliates, subcommittees, and overall associate membership. NICAP’s three basic objectives have been to instigate a more open governmental public information policy on UFO’s; to encourage an interest in the UFO problem on the part of the civilian scientific community; and, to investigate, substantiate, and document UFO sighting reports for dissemination to researchers and the interested public. To carry out these objectives, NICAP has set up voluntary investigating subcommittees throughout sections of the United States. Presently, I am serving as chairman of the NICAP Massachusetts Investigating Subcommittee.

The purpose of this article is to describe our activities in Massachusetts. In order to accomplish this we shall ask ourselves: Who is serving on the Subcommittee? What are their technical fields and job titles? What is the function of the subcommittee, how is it organized, and what is our method of operation? Lastly, have we who are serving on the NICAP Massachusetts Subcommittee been able to make a worthwhile contribution to carrying out NICAP’s three-fold objective?

Presently, there are 17 members serving on the Massachusetts Subcommittee. Their names, technical titles, and/or fields are as follows: Walter Webb, chief lecturer in astronomy, Hayden Planetarium, Boston; Francis Pechulis, logistics coordinator, Minuteman Ground Electrical System Repair and Recycle Program; Edward Argerake, engineering design specialist; Lee Comly, aeronautical engineer; Herbert Eismann, computer engineer; Richard Fowler, chemical engineer; Nathan Gold, electrical engineer; Dr. Bryce Hand, assistant professor of geology; George Kaiser, training director, missile tracking; Robert Jackson, materials administrator, refrigeration; John O’Neill, project administration, Satellite Communications Program; Ernest Reid, detective and electronics specialist; Robert Salvatore, engineering psychologist; John Spencer, radio station manager and former USAF public information officer; Gary Storey, electronics technician; and myself, a project administrative engineer in the Sylvania Minuteman Program Office, Needham, Massachusetts, specializing as a schedule analyst in the areas of program planning, scheduling, and PERT.

The primary function of the NICAP subcommittee is that of data gathering by a local investigation unit comprised of people with scientific, technical, or special training who are willing to use their time and talents in conducting field investigations of UFO sightings on behalf of NICAP. Depending upon facilities available to the unit, this would include the obtaining of firsthand signed reports from witnesses through the use of specially prepared UFO report questionnaires based upon government forms; obtaining character evaluations; checking possible natural or man-made explanations and preliminary evaluation of physical or photographic evidence obtained. After an investigation, a complete typewritten report is prepared and submitted with signed questionnaires, maps, sketches, etc., to NICAP, the USAF, and the government-sponsored University of Colorado UFO Project for research purposes.
Organization of a NICAP subcommittee consists of the candidate chairman submitting a list of potential subcommittee members to NICAP. This list includes signed application forms, professional resumes, and a list of equipment which can be made available by the members for subcommittee use. There must be at least one professional scientist on each team either in an active or advisory capacity. Exceptions are made only when NICAP believes that the collective experience of the team justifies it. Upon receipt of this information, NICAP, in turn, examines each team for approval and issues ID card credentials and necessary supplies to those subcommittees which are approved. The chairman must sign an agreement form concerning supervision of and personal responsibility for both the use of NICAP ID cards and the activities of subcommittee members as related to UFO investigation. A NICAP subcommittee handbook is issued to the chairman which contains the basic guidelines for subcommittee operation.
The method of operating a NICAP subcommittee is flexible and is usually dependent upon the drive, resources, and imagination of the chairman and members. In order to operate efficiently, there is the matter of finances. Dues may be collected or each member may volunteer to pay for personal investigating expenses. Our subcommittee derives much of its financial needs from a percentage of my earnings from UFO lectures. Each member is allowed to claim some reimbursement for gasoline and telephone expenses incurred during an investigation. To keep abreast of UFO sightings in Massachusetts we subscribe to a newsclip service which supplies a complete coverage of newspaper UFO reports on a daily reading-mailing basis. Contacts are made periodically with police stations, key installations, and organizations asking them to refer UFO report witnesses to the chairman. Arrangements have also been made with pertinent sources to obtain balloon-launching information, astronomical and satellite transit data, night advertising plane schedules, radar data, etc., on an as-required basis. All investigations are coordinated by the chairman and his appointed assistant. When a UFO sighting is brought to our attention, the witnesses are asked to supply basic data by telephone. The chairman checks such data against possible explanations before assigning field investigators to the case.

Due to the use of technical and special talent from a number of fields, the NICAP Massachusetts Investigating Subcommittee has been able to make a substantial contribution to the three-fold objective of NICAP in the form of objective investigations and carefully prepared detailed reports. Our report on the classical Exeter, New Hampshire, UFO sighting was voted unanimously into the Congressional Record by the House Armed Services Committee during the first open congressional hearings on UFO’s on April 5, 1966. These hearings, in turn, helped instigate a government-funded civilian scientific study of the UFO problem through the auspices of the University of Colorado. On May 31, 1967, I was asked to serve as an “early warning coordinator” for the Colorado University UFO Project. This has directly involved our subcommittee in joint UFO sighting investigations with scientists from this project. The NICAP Massachusetts Subcommittee UFO report files were examined by visiting Colorado University scientists, and later the complete files were requested and reproduced by the Colorado Project. We were told that “the accumulation of sightings in Massachusetts was about as impressive as the UFO business offers,” and that the Colorado Project “would like to build a case around the whole series of sightings in the vicinity.” In a further effort to make a contribution to official UFO research, I am now conducting a complete statistical analysis of the NICAP subcommittee UFO reports on file from 1964 onwards in a search for consistent UFO characteristics and patterns. An analysis for 1967 has recently been accomplished and amounts to 84 pages of charts, graphs, maps, and overlays which reflect statistics on UFO configurations; behaviors; side-effects; sighting locale; weather conditions; sighting proximity to power lines, power stations, and areas of technical interest; and report evaluations. Another project soon to be initiated is a UFO-witness profile report which will be a compilation of witness-background statistics. All such statistical reports will be provided to governmental and civilian UFO researchers for comparison and evaluation purposes.—End.

Their economy is suffocating. Their oil is blockaded. The navy dredged an alternate straight for an alternate shipping line. The navy regularly successfully escorts commercial ships through Hormuz without incident. 

However, high-level Iranian leadership are a procession of ideologues with forced-loyalty and the govt and military structure is highly fragmented/compartmentalized by design; so the only way the war will definitively come to an end without a peace agreement, with force alone, is by a heavy barrage of airstrikes taking out the remaining 10% of defense structure, followed by a likely years-long intel/contractors/special ops campaign converting at least some of the regime and populace to friendly.

But Iran just submitted a peace offer to Washington yesterday.  I think Trump will accept the offer.

The rising inflation and of cost of living resulting from this is war is un-fucking-believable, and this low-intensity prolonged bombing campaign is mind-boggling. The grinding, moderate pressure seems be working though. Cooler heads prevail, but that takes patience.

I think Trump will accept Iran’s offer.

If he doesn’t, and he launches a new wave of heavy strikes, the war will effectively be over within a few days, and special ops will be able to go in and orchestrate new regime. 

If he doesn’t accept the offer, and he also doesn’t launch a new wave of heavy strikes, but instead continues the low-intensity strikes, then that would seem to tell us that the military-industrial complex won, a long-term regional posture was deemed preferable, gas prices aren’t going anywhere and the “war” (effectively an economic war at this point with occasional dick-measuring contests) won’t end anytime soon.

Israel, US DOD and intel seem to want a long-term U.S. presence. Understandable. But I don’t think Trump will allow his legacy to be tarnished with an unfinished war he initiated. Pretty sure he’s gonna accept the offer.

𝐅𝐀𝐑𝐆𝐎 𝐃𝐄𝐓𝐄𝐂𝐓𝐈𝐕𝐄 𝐊𝐍𝐄𝐖 𝐒𝐇𝐄 𝐃𝐈𝐃𝐍'𝐓 𝐌𝐀𝐓𝐂𝐇 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐒𝐔𝐒𝐏𝐄𝐂𝐓 — 𝐉𝐀𝐈𝐋𝐄𝐃 𝐇𝐄𝐑 𝐒𝐈𝐗 𝐌𝐎𝐍𝐓𝐇𝐒 𝐀𝐍𝐘𝐖𝐀𝐘

U.S. Marshals arrested Angela Lipps at gunpoint in July 2025 while the 50-year-old Tennessee grandmother was watching her neighbor's kids — all because an AI facial recognition program decided her Facebook photo matched a bank fraud suspect a thousand miles away in Fargo, North Dakota. 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘬𝘯𝘦𝘸 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘈𝘐 𝘧𝘢𝘤𝘪𝘢𝘭 𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘨𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘦𝘤𝘩𝘯𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘺 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘣𝘦 𝘶𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘭𝘦 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘦𝘹𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘵𝘦 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘨𝘦 𝘢 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯, her lawsuit states. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐲𝐰𝐚𝐲.

Lipps had never set foot in North Dakota. She'd never even boarded a commercial flight. Bank surveillance video of the real suspect showed a different build and different facial features entirely — but Fargo detective Lucas Heck pushed the arrest warrant through regardless, according to the lawsuit. She was booked as a fugitive, extradited a thousand miles from her grandchildren, and told she was facing eight years in prison for a crime committed by a stranger she'd never met.

𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘶𝘨𝘨𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘰𝘧 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘣𝘦 𝘳𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘳 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘶𝘱 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨𝘭𝘺 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘷𝘪𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘪𝘮𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴, the suit alleges. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘤𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥, 𝘴𝘦𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘴, 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘛𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘬𝘴𝘨𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘊𝘩𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘮𝘢𝘴. 𝘞𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘤𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘥𝘺, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘪𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘤 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘦, 𝘴𝘶𝘤𝘩 𝘢𝘴 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘮𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘦𝘴. By the time she walked free on Christmas Eve, she'd lost her house, her car and her belongings.

Her attorney did what Fargo police never bothered to do — pulled her bank records and proved she was buying groceries in Tennessee the same day she was supposedly robbing a North Dakota bank. Charges dropped instantly. 𝘚𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘴 𝘪𝘯 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘦 𝘢𝘣𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘨𝘢𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘭𝘦𝘧𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘭𝘦𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘨𝘩 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘪𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘴𝘢𝘧𝘦, the complaint states.

The department's own then-chief admitted afterward that 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦𝘴 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘢𝘥𝘦, telling reporters, 𝘕𝘰 𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘦𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘥𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘦𝘥, 𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘶𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘭𝘺, 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵? He retired weeks later. Fargo itself has offered nothing — a city spokesperson says it 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴𝘯'𝘵 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘯 𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘨𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯, and has 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐳𝐞 to the woman its own detective jailed for six months on a hunch from a computer. Lipps is now suing the city and Detective Heck for $𝟏𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧.

𝐀𝐧 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞, 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐢𝐱 𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐥𝐠𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐦 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞-𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 — 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐨 𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐜𝐚𝐧'𝐭 𝐬𝐚𝐲 𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐲.

text:
Famous 1959 Gibson Les Paul Bursts - Owners and Sale Prices

Celebrity-owned 1959 Bursts rarely reach auction, so many prices are private reports, asking prices or rejected offers.

Peter Green / Gary Moore / Kirk Hammett - “Greeny”

Green sold his Fleetwood Mac Burst to Gary Moore for ~£100-£110. Moore sold it in 2006, reportedly for $750,000-$1.2 million, though unconfirmed. Kirk Hammett acquired Greeny in 2014 and says he paid under $500,000. Reports of a $2 million purchase confuse an asking price with the sale.

Sales: Green-Moore ~£100-£110; Moore reportedly $750,000-$1.2 million; Hammett under $500,000.

Mark Knopfler - 1959 Les Paul Standard

Knopfler owned this Burst for 20+ years and used it recording and touring. Christie’s sold it in 2024 for £693,000 including premium, ~$880,000, setting its world auction record for a 1959 Les Paul.

Verified sale: £693,000 (~$880,000), Christie’s, 2024.

Keith Richards / Mick Taylor - “Keith Burst”

Richards acquired this Bigsby-equipped Burst around 1964 and used it during the Stones’ early rise. It later passed to Mick Taylor. A $1 million-plus private sale is reported but unverified, and later provenance is disputed.

Reported sale: ~$1 million-plus, unverified.

Neal Schon - 1959 Les Paul Standards

Two 1959 Standards from Neal Schon sold through Heritage in 2021 for $350,000 and $300,000.

Verified sales: $350,000 and $300,000, Heritage, 2021.

Jimmy Page - “Number One”

Joe Walsh sold Page the 1959 Les Paul that became his principal Led Zeppelin guitar around 1969 for ~$500 plus expenses. Walsh recalled Page’s total with delivery may have reached $1,200.

Historical sale: ~$500-$1,200.

Modern sale: None.

Billy Gibbons - “Pearly Gates”

Gibbons bought Pearly Gates from a Texas rancher for ~$250. It became his signature ZZ Top Burst and remains with him.

Historical purchase: ~$250.

Modern sale: None.

Paul Kossoff - “Stripped Top”

Kossoff’s Free-era Burst is associated with “All Right Now.” Christie’s offered it in 1994 for £14,000. After failing at auction, it sold privately for £12,000.

Sale: £12,000, 1994.

Mike Bloomfield - 1959 Les Paul Standard

Bloomfield’s Burst was later acquired by Chris Okey for $980. In 2016 a reported $1.5 million offer failed when its owner declined to sell.

Historical purchase: $980.

Later offer: $1.5 million - rejected.

Bernie Marsden - “The Beast”

Marsden acquired The Beast in 1974 and used it with Whitesnake. ATB offered it in 2023 for £999,995 (~$1.3 million), but Marsden withdrew it.

Asking price: £999,995 (~$1.3 million).

Sale: None.

Eric Clapton - “Beano”

Clapton’s Blues Breakers Burst’s exact year is uncertain, often identified as 1959/1960. He bought it around 1965 for reportedly 105 guineas (£110.25). It was stolen in 1966 and remains missing.

Historical purchase: ~£110.25.

Modern sale: None.

Public-Sale Benchmarks

Mark Knopfler - £693,000 (~$880,000), Christie’s, 2024.

Neal Schon - $350,000, Heritage, 2021.

Neal Schon - $300,000, Heritage, 2021.

Greeny’s reported $750,000-$1.2 million and Keith Burst’s $1 million-plus transactions were private and lack comparable documentation.

Not actual sales:

Mike Bloomfield - $1.5 million offer, rejected.

Bernie Marsden “The Beast” - ~$1.3 million asking price, withdrawn.
