text:
The Zodiac Killer
View @FBI  Records on Hunt for Clues
03/02/07

The seemingly random brutal murders of five people in California’s Bay Area in 1968 and 1969 and a series of taunting cryptic notes sent by their killer terrorized Northern California for years.
The self-proclaimed “Zodiac Killer” sent local newspapers a three-part coded message explaining his motive for the killings in 1969 and in a separate letter to the editor suggested his identity was buried within an elaborate cipher message. The decoded message did indeed reveal the killer’s twisted motive, but his identity remains a mystery.

The unsolved nature of the murders and the Zodiac Killer’s elaborate methods of communicating with the public and his pursuers still captures the imaginations of screenwriters, authors, true-crime buffs, forensic scientists, and, of course, law enforcement.

The murders did not fall under federal jurisdiction, so the FBI never opened an investigation. But a glance through the FBI’s public records on the case shows how local law enforcement agencies called on the FBI’s expertise in handwriting analysis, cryptanalysis, and fingerprints to aid their investigations.

The FBI’s role in 1969, much as it is today, was to support local law enforcement in their investigations. In the Zodiac Killer case, correspondence between law enforcement agencies in Northern California and forensic experts at the FBI’s Laboratory—in what was then called the Technical Evaluation Unit—shows our efforts to analyze handwriting samples and lift latent fingerprints from the letters and envelopes sent by the purported killer. FBI cryptanalysts, or code-breakers, were also enlisted to unravel a complex cipher that used more than 50 shapes and symbols to represent the 26 letters of the alphabet. Ultimately the code was made public and broken by two university professors.

But then, as now, the case illustrates the extent of partnerships between the FBI and other law enforcement agencies. Here’s a look at just some of the ways we support our partners in investigations:

Behavioral analysis: Local police call on the FBI profilers, or behavioral analysts, at the FBI Laboratory for help and advice when leads in their criminal cases turn cold or fray into infinite possibilities. Read more about it.

Fingerprint analysis: Our Integrated Automated Fingerprint Identification System is the largest biometric database in the world, containing the fingerprints and corresponding criminal history information for more than 47 million subjects. Read more about it.
Criminal Background Checks: More than 90,000 agencies are connected to the FBI’s massive computerized database of fingerprints, mugshots, crime records, and parole and probation information. We run the “host computer” at our Criminal Justice Information Services facility in West Virginia. Read more about it.
Cryptanalysis: Code-breakers at the FBI Laboratory analyze and decipher codes used in used in the commission of crimes, including kidnappings, gang communications, espionage, and terrorism. Read more about it.
The records in the Zodiac case, meanwhile, are just a sample of what is available for your review in our Electronic Reading Room, which contains thousands of records, including our probes of famous persons, available through the Freedom of Information Act.
https://t.co/gV9F550QBn

Zodiac is a 2007 American crime thriller film directed by David Fincher and written by James Vanderbilt, based on the non-fiction books by Robert Graysmith: Zodiac (1986) and Zodiac Unmasked (2002). It stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, and Robert Downey Jr., with Anthony Edwards, Brian Cox, Elias Koteas, Donal Logue, John Carroll Lynch, Chloë Sevigny, Philip Baker Hall, and Dermot Mulroney in supporting roles.[6][7]

The film tells the story of the manhunt for the Zodiac Killer, a serial killer who terrorized the San Francisco Bay Area during the late 1960s and early 1970s, taunting police with letters, bloodstained clothing, and ciphers mailed to newspapers. The case remains one of the United States' most infamous unsolved crimes. Fincher, Vanderbilt, and producer Bradley J. Fischer spent 18 months conducting their own investigation and research into the Zodiac murders. Fincher employed the digital Thomson Viper FilmStream Camera to photograph most of the film and used traditional high-speed film cameras for slow-motion murder sequences.

Zodiac was released by Paramount Pictures in the United States and Canada and by Warner Bros. Pictures in international markets on March 2, 2007. It received largely positive reviews, with praise for its writing, directing, acting, and historical accuracy. The film was nominated for several awards, including the Saturn Award for Best Action, Adventure or Thriller Film. It grossed over $84.7 million worldwide on a production budget of $65 million. In a 2016 critics' poll conducted by the BBC, Zodiac was voted the 12th greatest film of the 21st century.

In the years since its release, the film has garnered a large cult following, with many claiming it to be David Fincher's magnum opus. Most of the film's followers praise its direction, acting, writing, cinematography, production design, soundtrack, attention to detail, and accuracy to both the real life investigation and the obsession that gripped some of those who were either directly involved with or close to the investigation itself.

Plot
On July 4, 1969, an unknown man attacks Darlene Ferrin and Mike Mageau with a handgun at a lovers' lane in Vallejo, California. Only Mike survives and later disappears from the public eye. One month later, the San Francisco Chronicle receives encrypted letters written by the killer, calling himself "Zodiac", who threatens to kill a dozen people, unless his coded message containing his identity is published.

Political cartoonist Robert Graysmith, who correctly guesses that his identity is not in the message, is not taken seriously by crime reporter Paul Avery or the editors and is excluded from the initial details about the killings. When the newspaper publishes the letters, a married couple deciphers one, revealing it indeed did not contain the killer's name. On September 27, the killer stabs law student, Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shepard at Lake Berryessa in Napa County; Cecelia dies two days later.

At the office, Avery makes fun of Graysmith before they discuss the coded letters. Graysmith interprets the letter, which Avery finds helpful, and he begins sharing information. One of Graysmith's insights about the letters is that Zodiac's reference to man as, "the most dangerous animal of them all," is a reference to the 1932 film The Most Dangerous Game, which features the villainous Count Zaroff, a man who hunts live human prey.

On October 11, San Francisco taxicab driver Paul Stine is shot and killed in the city's Presidio Heights district. The Zodiac killer mails pieces of Stine's bloodstained shirt to the Chronicle along with a taunting letter. San Francisco police inspectors Dave Toschi and his partner, Bill Armstrong, are assigned to the case by Captain Marty Lee, and work closely with Vallejo's Jack Mulanax and Captain Ken Narlow in Napa. Someone claiming to be Zodiac continues to send taunting letters and speaks on the phone with lawyer, Melvin Belli, on the KGO-TV morning talk show, hosted by Jim Dunbar.

On August 4, 1971, Detectives Toschi, Armstrong, and Mulanax question Arthur Leigh Allen, a suspect in the Vallejo case. They notice that he wears a Zodiac wristwatch, with the same logo used by the killer, and Toschi thinks he is the killer. However, a handwriting expert Sherwood insists that Allen did not write the Zodiac letters, even though Allen is said to be ambidextrous.

Avery receives a letter threatening his life; becoming paranoid, he turns to drugs and alcohol. He shares information with the Riverside Police Department that the killer might have been active before the initial killings, angering Toschi and Armstrong. The case's notoriety weighs on Toschi, who cannot sit through a Hollywood film, Dirty Harry, loosely based on the Zodiac case.

In 1976, Avery moves to the Sacramento Bee. Graysmith persistently contacts Toschi about the Zodiac murders, and eventually impresses him with his knowledge of the case. While Toschi cannot directly give Graysmith access to the evidence, he provides names in other police departments where Zodiac murders occurred. Armstrong transfers from the San Francisco Police homicide division, and Toschi is demoted for supposedly forging a Zodiac letter in 1978.

Graysmith continues his own investigation, profiled in the Chronicle, and gives a television interview about the book he is writing on the case. He begins receiving phone calls from someone breathing heavily. As his obsession deepens, Graysmith loses his job, and his wife Melanie leaves him, taking their children. Graysmith learns that Allen lived close to Ferrin, and his birthday matches the one Zodiac gave when he spoke to one of Melvin Belli's maids. While circumstantial evidence seems to indicate his guilt, the physical evidence, such as fingerprints and handwriting samples, does not implicate him.

On December 20, 1983, Graysmith tracks Allen to a Vallejo Ace Hardware store, where he is employed as a sales clerk; they stare at each other before Graysmith leaves. On August 16, 1991, after Graysmith's book, Zodiac, has become a bestseller, Mike Mageau resurfaces after years of drug use, and identifies Allen from a police mugshot.

A textual epilogue says that Allen died of a heart attack in 1992 before police could question him; and though a 2002 DNA test did not match Allen's, the police refused to rule him out as a suspect. Allen remains the prime and only suspect in the counties of Napa and Solano and the city of Vallejo, and to this day, the case remains open.

In 1754, near Paris, Chevalier de Bonneville established the Chapter of Clermont. The Chapter resided in the College of Jesuits of Clermont, hence the name. It is said to have been created to honor the Duc de Clermont, then Grand Master of the English Grand Lodge of France.

The Chapter of Clermont was a “Chapter of the Advanced Degrees” and initially entailed six degrees and was later extended to 25 known degrees. The six initial degrees were 1˚, 2˚ and 3˚ St John’s Masonry, 4˚ Knight of the Eagle, 5˚ Illustrious Knight or Templar, 6˚ Sublime Illustrious Knight.

Interestingly enough historically, prior to the time of the Rite’s creation, James II had been in residence at Clermont in exile from Britain from 1688 to his death in 1701. As noted by German Masonic historian, Lenning… “whilst in exile, James II residing at the Jesuit College of Clermont in France, allowed his closest associates to fabricate certain degrees in order to extend their political views.” Lenning believed this to have been an attempt on the part of James and his associates to regain control of the British throne for the House of Stuart. If Lenning is right, this places the origins of the “Rite of Perfection” in the hands of James II and the Jacobite (Stuart) Freemasons who at the time were in exile from Great Britain throughout France and Italy. Lenning also contends that these degrees were introduced into French Freemasonry under the name of the Clermont System.

The Archer Who Came from the East
Then word came from the capital. Yao — the emperor, the Son of Heaven — had heard of the suffering in Sanglin. And he had sent someone to end it.

His name was Yi. The divine archer. The man who had already shot nine suns from the sky to save the world from burning. If anyone could stop Fengxi, it was him.

The people of Sanglin gathered at the edge of the village to watch him arrive. They expected a giant, a demigod, a figure of legend. What they saw was a man — lean, weathered, carrying a bow that seemed too simple for the weight of what it had done. He walked through the village without speaking, past the burned fields, past the empty pens, past the faces of people who had forgotten what hope looked like.

He stopped at the edge of the marsh. He looked at the dark water, the tangled reeds, the place where the beast made its home.

Then he nocked an arrow.

The Hunt
The battle between Yi and Fengxi was not a duel. It was a hunt — the oldest kind of hunt, the kind where one creature pursues another across a landscape that neither of them can fully control.

Yi entered the marsh alone. He moved through the reeds with the patience of a man who had hunted gods before. He did not rush. He did not call out. He simply followed the trail — the broken reeds, the massive footprints in the mud, the faint smell of rot that hung in the air wherever Fengxi had been.

And then he found it.

Fengxi burst from the water with a sound that was half roar, half scream — a noise that flattened the reeds and sent birds scattering for miles. It charged. The ground shook. The mud sprayed in every direction.

Yi did not run. He stood his ground and loosed an arrow. It struck Fengxi's flank and bounced off — a spark, a scratch, nothing more. The boar's hide was too thick, too ancient, too armored by years of rage and hunger. Yi loosed a second arrow. Then a third. Each one found its mark, and each one failed to stop the beast.

Fengxi was still coming.

The Shot That Changed Everything
Yi moved. He was faster than he looked, faster than any man had a right to be. He dodged Fengxi's charge, rolled through the mud, came up with another arrow already nocked. The people watching from the edge of the marsh saw only flashes — the glint of Yi's bow, the massive shape of the boar, the spray of water and mud where the beast's tusks tore into the earth.

Yi had learned something in those first moments. Fengxi's hide was too thick to pierce anywhere except one place: the leg. The joint. The spot where the armor was thin and the muscle vulnerable.

He waited. The beast charged again. Yi dropped low, loosed the arrow at the exact moment Fengxi's front leg came down, and the shaft drove deep into the soft tissue behind the knee.

Fengxi screamed. The sound was terrible — not just pain, but something that sounded almost like surprise. The boar crashed to the ground, its massive body sending shockwaves through the marsh.

Yi did not kill it. He walked up to the fallen beast, placed his foot on its neck, and looked it in the eye.

Then he bound its legs and dragged it out of the marsh.

The Capture
The people of Sanglin watched in silence as Yi emerged from the reeds, the beast behind him, bound and broken. They could not believe what they were seeing. The creature that had terrorized them for years, the nightmare that had taken their crops and their children and their hope — it was on the ground. It was defeated. It was captured.

The Huainanzi records the moment simply: "Yi captured Fengxi in the Mulberry Grove. The people were overjoyed and acclaimed Yao as their ruler."

The celebration lasted for days. The people of Sanglin sang songs. They rebuilt their homes. They planted new crops. And they told the story of the archer who came from the east and faced the beast that no one else could face.

Yi did not stay. He had other beasts to hunt — the great serpent in the lake, the nine-headed monster in the north, the demon who devoured the sun. He left Sanglin the same way he had arrived: alone, silent, with his bow across his back.

But he left one thing behind.

He left the proof that even the most unstoppable terror can be brought down. He left the knowledge that there is always someone who will stand where others cannot. He left the story.

Why This Legend Still Matters Today
The Pig is the twelfth sign of the Chinese zodiac — the final position, the last hour before midnight, the moment when the year prepares to end and begin again. It is a sign of abundance, of warmth, of the quiet contentment of a life well lived.

But abundance is not something that comes easily. It is something that is protected. Something that is fought for. Something that, once won, must never be taken for granted.

Fengxi is the shadow side of abundance — the greed that consumes without gratitude, the hunger that never stops, the power that exists only to destroy. It is the warning that lives beneath the sign of the Pig. The Pig is not lazy. It is not indulgent. It is the creature that has seen the darkness and chosen, again and again, to find joy in the light.

If you were born in the Year of the PIG, Fengxi is not your enemy. It is your counterweight. You carry a deep knowledge of what it means to lose everything — and an even deeper gratitude for what it means to have enough. You were not made for the battlefield. You were made for the harvest.

But you will never forget that the harvest must be protected.

Abundance is not about having more. It is about being grateful for what you already have — and never letting the darkness take it away.

The Art of War is an ancient Chinese military treatise dating from the late Spring and Autumn period (roughly 5th century BC). The work, which is attributed to the ancient Chinese military strategist Sun Tzu ("Master Sun"), is composed of 13 chapters. Each one is devoted to a different set of skills or art related to warfare and how it applies to military strategy and tactics. For almost 1,500 years, it was the lead text in an anthology that was formalized as the Seven Military Classics by Emperor Shenzong of Song in 1080. The Art of War remains the most influential strategy text in East Asian warfare,[1] has influenced both East Asian and Western military theory and thinking, and has found a variety of applications in myriad competitive non-military endeavors across the modern world including espionage,[2] culture, politics, business, and sports.[3][4][5][6]

The book contains a detailed explanation and analysis of the 5th-century BC Chinese military, from weapons, environmental conditions, and strategy to rank and discipline. Sun also stressed the importance of intelligence operatives and espionage to the war effort. Considered one of history's finest military tacticians and analysts, his teachings and strategies formed the basis of advanced military training throughout the world.

The book was translated into French and published in 1772 by the French priest Jesuit Jean Joseph Marie Amiot; it was re-published in 1782. A partial translation into English was attempted by British officer Everard Ferguson Calthrop in 1905 under the title The Book of War. The first annotated English translation was completed and published by Lionel Giles in 1910.[7] Military and political leaders such as the Chinese communist revolutionary Mao Zedong, Japanese daimyō Takeda Shingen, Vietnamese general Võ Nguyên Giáp, is cited along with American military generals Douglas MacArthur and Norman Schwarzkopf Jr. as having drawn inspiration from the book.[8]

Outside of military use, The Art of War has also become a source of inspiration in business, politics, sports and esports, and its usage has extended to film and television.

History
Text and commentaries
The Art of War is traditionally attributed to an ancient Chinese military general known as Sun Tzu (pinyin: Sūnzǐ), meaning 'Master Sun'. Sun Tzu is said to have lived in the 6th century BC, but the earliest parts of The Art of War probably date to at least 100 years later.[9]

Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, the first of China's 24 dynastic histories, records an early Chinese tradition that a text on military matters was written by one "Sun Wu" (孫武) from the State of Qi, and that this text had been read and studied by King Helü of Wu (r. 514–495 BC).[10] This text was traditionally identified with the received Master Sun's Art of War. The conventional view was that Sun Wu was a military theorist from the end of the Spring and Autumn period (776–471 BC) who fled his home state of Qi to the southeastern Kingdom of Wu, where he is said to have impressed the king with his ability to quickly train even court women in military discipline and to have made Wu's armies powerful enough to challenge their western rivals in the state of Chu. This view is still widely held in China.[11]

The strategist, poet, and warlord Cao Cao in the early 3rd century AD authored the earliest known commentary to the Art of War.[10] Cao's preface makes clear that he edited the text and removed certain passages, but the extent of his changes were unclear historically.[10] The Art of War appears throughout the bibliographical catalogs of the Chinese dynastic histories, but listings of its divisions and size varied widely.[10]

text:
THE CHINESE SHOP NEXT DOOR: Trade Fair and the Death of the Nigerian Middleman

The world is waking up. On May 19 in Kansas City, Vice President J.D. Vance told factory workers what America denied for thirty years: America borrows from Chinese peasants to buy what Chinese peasants make. America, with 25 trillion-dollar GDP, is angry it funded its own de-industrialization. In Europe, France and Italy import near-finished Chinese goods but add local content to claim Made in France, Made in Italy. Everyone protects long term interest. Everyone except Nigeria.

In 2025, Nigeria imported 19.79 trillion naira from China and exported only 2.78 trillion. Deficit: 17.01 trillion. China supplies 39% of all imports. In H1 2026, for every 1 naira we sold to China, we bought 10.11 naira. That one-sidedness has left the port and entered the shop.

To understand it, we must start with the Spider Web Doctrine. Look at Jews, Indians, Lebanese. They are spiders. They spin a web. That web is their bank, their insurance, their lawyer, their wholesaler, their shipper. The web is designed to trap money inside and not let it escape. When a Jew makes one dollar in America, that dollar circulates thirteen times inside the Jewish web before it leaves. The spider spins to feed his family. Deliberate economic patriotism. Chika Onyeani's warning was simple: the Black man refuses to spin his own web. He makes money in Lagos and rushes to buy a Chinese container. Money made inside escapes same day. No closed loop. So, he remains consumer, never spider.

Before we blame the Chinese shop in Trade Fair, understand his web and why he can afford to be cheap. One, cheap credit. China EXIM Bank gives 2 to 3% for five years plus 13% export rebate. Two, cheap power. Shenzhen pays 7 cents per kilowatt-hour, 24-hour power, port clears in two days. Three, scale. Making ten million chargers drops cost to thirty cents. Four, state protection. You cannot open retail in Yiwu as a Nigerian. China fences retail at home yet pushes its traders to do retail abroad. Zero reciprocity. Five, stable currency. He plans one year with same cost in Renminbi.

Now the Nigerian trader. No power. Diesel at 1,300 naira. A shop in Trade Fair burns 150,000 weekly just to test electronics. No cheap credit. Nigerian bank offers 33 to 38% for ninety days. No infrastructure. Apapa takes twenty-one days with demurrage, Customs, SON. Chinese port: two days. No stable currency. Dollar moves from 1,600 to 1,800 while goods are on sea. Multiple taxation, no subsidy. Government that found 15.6 trillion for coastal highway cannot create 500 billion Industrial Transition Fund at 5% for Trade Fair and Computer Village to move from import to assembly. He comes from a system designed to make him win. We come from a system designed to make us fail.

For forty years our web, though weak, had a structure: Chinese manufacturer to Nigerian importer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer. Each layer funded Nwa Boy apprenticeship - seven years to become master. That apprenticeship was our web school. Now there are two competing webs in one market. The Chinese have spun their own web inside Nigeria: China EXIM Bank to Chinese shipping line to Chinese warehouse in Ojo to Chinese retail shop in Ojo to Chinese underground banking back to China. Money made in Trade Fair circulates inside the Chinese web and returns to China to feed their family. Our web is torn because we refused to spin. On September 15, 2026, ASPMDA in Trade Fair shut shops. Placards read Chinese Must Go. Many happen to be Igbo, but pain is Nigerian. Same cry in Computer Village, Alaba, Kano. The effects are clear. Price elasticity - electronics is elastic, cheaper wins. Waybill cloning - staff copy customer numbers and call your customers directly. Profit repatriation - Nigerian profit builds house and settles apprentice; Chinese profit leaves. In 2025, CBN recorded Chinese FDI as 38 million dollars, Beijing recorded 390 million. Value chain collapse - kill importer, you kill 30% duty, VAT, PAYE, transporters. Temu threat - if we cannot regulate physical shops in Ojo, how do we regulate digital shops selling below cost straight to Nigerian phones? What China does is spinning its web on our soil to trap our wealth. Imagine fifty thousand Nigerian boys landing in Shenzhen, renting shops, copying customers, sending profit to Onitsha. China would jail them in one week.

On X, Do2dtun called it selective outrage. Lere Olayinka, aide to FCT Minister Wike, wrote Nigerians came to Lagos to trade, Chinese also came. Their point works for today, ignores tomorrow. It exposes our disease: supporting unfair means to cure emotional hangups. In 2019, President Buhari removed Chief Justice Walter Onnoghen. The Constitution says only NJC recommends removal, Senate confirms. Many cheered the illegality because they disliked Onnoghen. That became template for invading judges' homes. Today we repeat it. Some celebrate Chinese web because it harms Igbo. They forget. Doctrine of One Strand: allow one strand of your own web to be eaten because you hate who stands on it, you teach the other spider that your web is weak. Today Igbo in Trade Fair, tomorrow Yoruba in Computer Village, next Hausa in Kantin Kwari. Comprador collapse: Walter Rodney in How Europe Underdeveloped Africa called them collaborators. Landlord collecting ten million from Chinese when Nigerian can pay four million is not spinning his web, he is helping the other spider spin its own. Apprenticeship death: Nwa Boy is the most successful web school in Black Africa. Kill master margin, you kill seven future traders.

Traders protesting happen to be mostly Igbo, but they are a dyke protecting Nigeria. They could pool ten billion via town unions and become sole distributors for the Chinese and become richer compradors. They refused. They said do not do our business. By protecting his shop, the Nigerian trader protects Yoruba transporter, Hausa retailer, Federal Government collecting duty.

Ghana understood. GIPC Act 865, Section 27 reserves retail, petty trading, hawking for Ghanaians. Foreigner must invest one million dollars, employ twenty Ghanaians, cannot trade inside a market. Nigeria: CAMA allows one hundred percent foreign ownership for one hundred million naira. No law reserves retail. It is law vacuum.

Protectionism is now normal. This is the Trump Doctrine. To protect America, President Trump in 2025-2026 imposed 145% tariff on Chinese EVs, steel, batteries, plus 10 to 20% universal tariffs and transshipment penalties. He said cheap today means dead tomorrow. America chose to protect its web over cheap goods. If America with 25 trillion GDP protects its middle class with tariffs, why should Nigeria with less than one trillion celebrate another spider spinning inside its market as healthy competition?

This is not anti-China. It is pro-Nigeria. First, government may consider amending CAMA and trade laws to reserve retail in designated markets for Nigerians, as Ghana did. Government may consider allowing foreigners to own warehouses and distribution hubs, but not retail shops inside Trade Fair, Computer Village, Alaba, Kantin Kwari. Second, government may consider creating a 500 billion naira Industrial Transition Fund at 5% for Trade Fair and Computer Village to move from import to assembly, and encouraging traders to pool funds via town unions for industrial clusters in Ogun and Abia, with tax holidays and stable power. This is how we spin our own web - capital circulates inside before going out. Third, government may consider sanctioning landlords who rent shops to foreigners for retail in prohibited markets, and sanctioning officials who clear retail containers as raw materials. Market associations may consider internal clean-up - no member should sublet to factory-to-shop operators.

Africa does not need cheap foreign retail webs. Africa needs its own spiders spinning its own webs to trap its own wealth and feed its own family. If we clap because their spider is eating the Igbo strand of our web today, tomorrow their web will cover the whole market. And because we refused to spin our own, there will be no food left for our own family.

text:
My neighbor's AC repairman charged him $800 for a new capacitor that was still in the original plastic wrapper.

Air conditioning died in July. Called a company with good online reviews. Tech comes out, diagnoses a bad capacitor.

"Gonna need to replace this. $800 with labor."

Seems expensive for a small part, but it's 95 degrees. My neighbor agrees.

Tech goes to his van, comes back fifteen minutes later. Says it's all fixed.

My neighbor asks to see the old part. "Already in my truck. But you're good to go!"

Something feels off. After the tech leaves, my neighbor opens the AC unit to look.

The capacitor has a tiny manufacturer's sticker on it. Serial number, date code. He takes a photo.

Hour later, his buddy who's an electrician stops by. Looks at the photo.

"That date code is from last week. And see that residue on the terminal? That's from the protective plastic they ship with. This part was installed like ten minutes ago, still had the wrapper on."

My neighbor pulls the unit open again. There's the plastic wrapper, tucked behind the housing. Tech must've dropped it and missed it.

He calls the company. "Your tech charged me $800 for a part that wasn't broken."

Dispatcher says that's impossible, their techs are trained and honest.

"Then why is the old capacitor still in my unit with this week's date code and the plastic wrapper still inside?"

Long silence. "Let me have a supervisor call you."

Supervisor offers a refund "as a courtesy." My neighbor demands full refund plus the service call fee, or he's reporting them to the state contractor's board and posting the evidence online.

Got his money back same day.

Checked online. Three other recent reviews mentioned the same scam with capacitors.

Company's not in business anymore.

text:
💛 ZM @Zcash community!

Tomorrow is a big day! A lot of hyped projects like @zaddrnet, @zecfrogs, @BITFOOTS_, @ZeckersNFT and others will launch their mints.

Zcash is built around privacy. Shielded transactions encrypt transaction data, hiding addresses, amounts and memos from public view.

NFTs on Zcash can be issued as ZSA — Zcash Shielded Assets. The asset exists at the protocol level, while ownership and transfers can remain private through shielded notes.

Amazing tech, but it also introduces some interesting risks:

• Fake NFTs — selling an image/database entry that isn’t a real protocol-level asset.

• Fake collections — impersonating a legitimate project or creating a lookalike collection.

• Fake ownership — a marketplace claims you own an NFT while the actual ownership model is purely off-chain.

• Metadata rug — the NFT exists, but its image/metadata can later be changed, deleted or become inaccessible.

• Fake scarcity — claiming a limited supply while the issuer can actually create more.

• Wash trading — trading NFTs between controlled wallets to manufacture volume and price history.

• Fake floor — creating artificial high-priced listings to make a collection look more valuable.

• Self-buying — buying your own NFT at an inflated price to create a fake “last sale” price.

• Fake volume/activity — manipulating marketplace statistics to make a collection look active.

• Fake liquidity — showing attractive listings/offers that aren’t backed by genuine demand.

• Creator dump — minting/accumulating a large amount, generating hype, then dumping on buyers.

• Fake burns — claiming NFTs were permanently burned when they were only removed from a marketplace/database.

• Fake sales — displaying “SOLD” in a centralized UI without independently verifiable settlement.

• Marketplace custody risk — buyers send real ZEC through infrastructure controlled by the marketplace, creating a trusted intermediary.

• Settlement risk — NFT and payment don’t move atomically; one side can potentially be completed while the other is delayed or requires operator intervention.

• Double-listing / race conditions — the same NFT can potentially be offered through multiple marketplaces if listings aren’t enforced at the protocol level.

• Migration scams — “upgrade/migrate your NFT” requests that actually transfer the asset to an attacker.

• Bridge scams — fake bridges or wrapped versions of NFTs.

• Issuer risk — the entity creating the asset can potentially control important properties of the collection, depending on how the asset was issued.

• Indexer/UI censorship — the NFT still exists on-chain, but a marketplace can hide, delist or misrepresent it.

• Phishing — fake Zcash NFT marketplaces, fake mint pages, fake offers and wallet-draining transactions.

The key question isn’t:

“Is this NFT on Zcash?”

The real question is:

What exactly exists on-chain?

ZSA asset → protocol-level asset.

Off-chain database entry → you’re trusting the marketplace.

And even a genuine ZSA doesn’t automatically make the entire marketplace trustless.

You still need to examine:

Asset → Ownership → Metadata → Listing → Settlement → Marketplace custody.

Also, always double check which transaction you want to sign AND use only trusted swap/bridge services!

Stay safe!

Excerpt-Chapter 6: Mandatory Palestine, 1927

Gazing into the Mediterranean horizon, Alexandra sought her escape. She had spent a healthy part of the last six weeks frolicking the salty seas—from the beaches of the Portuguese Algarve to those of the Greek Islands—exercising a type of Polynesian ocean worship she had sampled in Hawaii. The waves had been middling, but time in the sun had left her skin nicely bronzed. Haifa provided ideal conditions for bodysurfing. The ankle waders found interest in her antics. Some offered applause, while others gawked as if she were a rumbustious sea creature that kept washing ashore.
--There was one dogged frowner: a thickset woman with golden curls spilling out of her bathing cap, who, if raised in Japan, would have been trained in the art of the Sumo. Now she stood waiting with two police officers, pointing.
--Alexandra was unsure of her offense, awash in a strange land and knowing few of its rules. Her Jantzen swimsuit clung to her lithe frame modestly. Perhaps it struck blasphemously to display wet hair in the ancient Holy Land. She jumped bashful waves that broke close to shore and ducked under the churning lather of those so forceful they collapsed under their weight out to sea. Having the patience to corral the ideal wave proved key, and likely her only chance, short of swimming for Cyprus, to avoid arrest.

running google ads the vanilla way stopped working and most brands haven't caught up

keywords, bids, match types, a product page at the end. the setup carried the industry for a decade and dies in 2026 for a reason nobody wants to say out loud

google keeps automating the exact skills media buyers used to charge for

smart bidding replaced manual CPC. PMax replaced campaign structure decisions, broad match plus AI Max replaced keyword research, and asset generation writes the headlines now

every update makes the BUYING part easier

so deep platform knowledge, the thing separating a good account from a bad one for years, matters less every quarter

meanwhile CPCs climbed and the market saturated. the same pressure everyone feels on meta hit google eighteen months later and nobody announced the shift

running good ads no longer makes you profitable. good ads are the entry fee

the accounts printing today belong to operators who understand ecom first and google second

people who know what an advertorial does to cold traffic, when a quiz funnel beats a comparison page, and why problem-aware search traffic hitting a product page is the most expensive mistake in the account

funnel builders, not button clickers

google will happily deliver a thousand qualified clicks. what google will never decide is where those clicks land, what the page says, what offer sits behind the page, or how to frame the mechanism so a stranger trusts you in 90 seconds

the human work sits there, and almost nobody is doing the human work on google

meta operators solved this years ago. advertorials, quiz funnels, listicles, VSLs, comparison pages, all standard over there

on google the same stack is rare enough to be an edge

the platform is becoming a delivery system. the funnel is the product

DM me "FUNNEL" if you want to see one built out properly

SUNDAY MORNING DISPATCH ROUNDUP
September 20, 2026

Here’s a look at overnight and early morning calls across the Denver metro area. Information below is based on preliminary dispatch traffic and may change as agencies investigate.

LAKEWOOD / JEFFERSON COUNTY / GOLDEN

• 4:43 AM — I-70, Lakewood/Wheat Ridge area: Dispatch traffic reported a closure of I-70 between Kipling Street and Ward Road.

• 3:55 AM — Sheridan Boulevard & West Florida Avenue, Lakewood: Officers were requested for a reported disturbance involving a man and a woman. Details were still being gathered.

• 3:45 AM — Kipling Street near West 44th Avenue, Arvada: Medical crews were dispatched to a reported assault.

• 3:42 AM — West Bowles Avenue: Officers responded to a single-vehicle crash near Bell’s. The vehicle was disabled and possible fence damage was reported. No transports were reported.

• 12:54 AM — South Sheridan Boulevard, Lakewood: Officers were dispatched to a report of a fight possibly involving a gun.

• 12:38 AM — St. Anthony Hospital, Lakewood: Fire crews were dispatched emergently to a reported incident involving a hospital room. The preliminary automated dispatch summary characterized the call as a possible fire, but the exact circumstances were unclear.

• 12:29 AM — I-70 westbound near mile marker 248, Golden: Dispatch reported a loose golden-colored dog in the roadway. A unit was sent to check the area.

• 12:28 AM — US 6 westbound west of Sheridan Boulevard: Responders were reported on scene of a three-vehicle crash.

• 11:14 PM — Lakewood/Jefferson County: Law enforcement units tracked a silver vehicle across I-70, I-76, Pecos and other roads. Dispatch traffic described coordinated surveillance of the vehicle and its occupants, but did not state the underlying reason.

• 11:07 PM — I-70/I-76, Jefferson County: A silver Mitsubishi Outlander was followed for reported erratic driving, including brief wrong-way travel. Dispatch traffic reported sparks after the vehicle apparently struck an object.

• 11:01 PM — Washington Avenue/Highway 93, Golden: Officers followed a vehicle reported to be driving recklessly, including passing vehicles and nearly striking a median.

• 10:48 PM — Lakewood/Golden: Dispatch traffic described a black BMW with no license plates fleeing westbound on US 6 after reportedly running a red light. Multiple occupants and a firearm inside the vehicle were mentioned over the radio.

• 10:46 PM — Wadsworth Boulevard near Bowles Avenue: Dispatch received a report of a black BMW without license plates driving recklessly northbound, including reportedly running red lights.

• 10:41 PM — Kipling Street & Morrison Road, Lakewood: Officers reported vehicles possibly connected to street racing heading east on Morrison Road. Marked police vehicles were following, and another agency asked about the availability of a Grappler device.

• 10:18 PM — Golden: Radio traffic referenced a possible DUI-related crash, a summons for resistance and a blood kit being taken to the Golden office after a hospital visit.

DENVER

• 6:48 AM — Francis Heights, West 26th Avenue: Officers were sent emergently to a reported assault at an apartment. Dispatch indicated the reported assailant had left and was reportedly not armed.

• 6:11 AM — Union Station: Officers responded to a report of a woman exposing herself and repeatedly dressing and undressing near the B2 platform area. Later updates placed her near the B3 and B4 platforms.

• 5:51 AM — 16th Street Mall near Tremont Place: Officers were sent to a report of a person lying in front of buses and refusing to allow them to move.

• 5:31 AM — Colfax Avenue & Broadway: Dispatch traffic indicated a possible overdose at a bus stop. The person was reportedly transported to Denver Health.

• 5:23 AM — Colfax Avenue & Lincoln Street: A person initially reported unresponsive was revived and later awake and talking before being transported to a hospital for evaluation.

• 5:03 AM — East Colfax Avenue: Dispatch traffic reported a major crash affecting eastbound Colfax, with transit operators being rerouted around the scene.

• 4:40 AM — Colfax Avenue: Police were reported blocking part of the roadway following a crash, with buses detouring around the closure.

• 4:33 AM — 7 North: Dispatch traffic reported a possible four-car collision involving train 35.

• 4:06 AM — 6000 block of Washington Street: Emergency crews responded to a property-damage crash near a railroad crossing where fuel was reportedly leaking from a vehicle into a storm drain.

• 4:02 AM — Union Station: Transit police were requested to meet two A Line passengers over a reported fare issue. A later update indicated the passengers were fare-compliant and the police contact was cleared.

• 3:23 AM — Park Avenue near Henderson Street: Dispatch reported a possible DUI-related crash with significant debris in the roadway.

• 3:07 AM — Washington Street & East 58th Avenue: Dispatch reported a possible hit-and-run after a vehicle struck railroad crossing arms. The occupants reportedly fled on foot and the vehicle remained on the tracks.

• 2:18 AM — North Federal Boulevard: Emergency crews responded to a reported possible fentanyl overdose in a motel parking lot. A 20-year-old man was reportedly conscious and breathing after receiving one dose of Narcan. Responders later had difficulty locating the patient and reporting party.

• 2:13 AM — West 58th Avenue near the I-25 northbound on-ramp: Officers responded to a reported possible hit-and-run involving a red Volkswagen Atlas. Dispatch reported the vehicle’s registration as valid.

• 1:58 AM — Larimer Street: Officers were dispatched to a report of a fight involving a person reportedly armed with a weapon.

• 1:55 AM — East 56th Avenue & Quebec Street: Dispatch reported a possible injury crash involving a black or gray pickup and a white van. Radio traffic included conflicting reports about the vehicles’ directions of travel and mentioned a possible red-light violation.

• 1:55 AM — East 6th Avenue & Quebec Street: Dispatch traffic reported a possible two-vehicle injury crash, with a possible red-light violation mentioned.

• 1:38 AM — North Pecos Street: A deputy was requested to assist a trooper with reported street racers at a warehouse facility.

• 1:16 AM — West Mississippi Avenue: Officers were dispatched to a reported family disturbance involving a knife in a parking lot.

• 12:55 AM — East Evans Avenue: Officers were dispatched to a report of a fight involving guns and knives near the Cross Apartments.

text:
Who is @EugeneDaniels2 really?

AI: One point in your premise needs a major correction: he did not actually win an election for @WHCA president. That job came to him through an unusual succession after Kaitlan Collins resigned to bring back Trump.

Where Daniels actually came from

Daniels is a Texas native who played high-school football and says he had 10 Division I offers. He went to Colorado State University as a defensive end, but a shoulder injury ended his playing career. He graduated in 2012 with a bachelor’s degree in journalism and technical communication. At CSU he worked across student media and even hosted a late-night show called Daniels After Dark. 

He joined Politico⁠ in 2018, initially covering the midterms. He covered Andrew Yang in 2020 and subsequently became a White House correspondent, a Politico Playbook author and, importantly, Politico’s principal reporter following Vice President Kamala Harris. 

Then came television. He became an MSNBC contributor in 2021, was elevated into a larger Morning Joe role in 2022, and in 2025 left Politico to become a full-time MSNBC host and senior Washington correspondent.

That is a remarkably fast trajectory: Politico in 2018 → MSNBC contributor in 2021 → major Playbook/White House presence → WHCA president in 2024 → MSNBC host/senior Washington correspondent in 2025.

The WHCA story is stranger than “he got elected president”

In the 2022 WHCA election, Daniels ran for the organization’s New Media seat, not president. He absolutely crushed that election: 398 votes out of 449 ballots, with 43 abstentions and only eight write-ins. 

Kaitlan Collins separately won the at-large seat with 247 votes and was supposed to become the 2024–25 WHCA president. But after CNN moved Collins to New York for CNN This Morning, she resigned from the WHCA board in September 2022. 

Then the bylaws kicked in.

Because Daniels had received the most votes among the remaining board members, he was scheduled to become treasurer. The bylaws specified that if the president-elect couldn’t serve, the incoming treasurer became president.

WHCA counsel explicitly concluded:

“The bylaws are unequivocal”

that Daniels would become president. 

So the precise version is:

The WHCA membership overwhelmingly elected Eugene Daniels to its board. It did not elect Eugene Daniels president. Kaitlan Collins was the intended president. Her resignation automatically elevated Daniels under the bylaws.

That distinction actually makes the chronology more interesting, not less.

And the language you’re remembering is real. When the succession was announced, Daniels said he was “humbled and full of excitement” for “all that we will do together.”

Where the access/influence question gets interesting

Daniels became unusually closely identified professionally with Kamala Harris coverage.

During the 2024 campaign, he described his relationship with the Harris operation as contentious at times—“we tussle”—but also said her people were accessible and forthright with him. 

That’s legitimate source cultivation in political journalism, but it’s also exactly the sort of reporter-source proximity where examining access, coverage and subsequent career opportunities is reasonable.

There is one explosive allegation — but it remains an allegation

In February 2025, Breitbart reported, citing unnamed sources, that Daniels had interviewed twice for employment with Harris’s presidential campaign during 2024. Daniels denied it.

In January 2022, Politico Playbook reported that Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor had been spotted dining at Washington’s Le Diplomate with Senator Chuck Schumer.

She hadn’t.

The woman was Schumer’s wife, Iris Weinshall.

Politico had to correct the fact multiple times. The Daily Beast reported that Daniels wrote the fact incorrectly but declined to comment through a spokesperson.

text:
You do not need a bill number to read a speech. You need a spine.

Give the narrow point its due. “Greatest assault on free speech of the 21st century” is a headline, not a statute. No Online Harms Act 2.0 is on the Order Paper this week. Calling a man dangerous because he used the word “disinformation” in Alsace is not the same as reading a clause. Fine. That is not the file.

The file is what the Prime Minister actually said, in public, to the European Parliament, on 17 September. Tech platforms “aspire to sovereignty.” They want to set the terms of access, dictate the rules, circumvent them, control data, “spread disinformation” and “steal our children’s childhoods.” Then he offered the cure: Canada and Europe “join forces” on AI safety protocols, common standards and transparency, plus youth who can live, work and study on either side of the Atlantic. That is not a rumour. That is the PMO text. Reuters printed the same lines. So did CBC.

A speech that names the platforms as a storm and Brussels as the forest is a policy direction. Waiting for a bill so you can pretend the direction does not exist is how process people keep the argument in the nursery.

The Charter paragraph is the other tell. The Liberal Party of 1982 is not a permanent injunction against the Liberal Party of 2026. Section 2(b) did not stop C-11, C-18, the last Online Harms run, or a cabinet that invoked the Emergencies Act and froze accounts. Two courts later said the national-security test failed. This government is still appealing. The same man now wants common standards with a Union that already runs the Digital Services Act as a speech architecture. Associate member is a noun the treaties do not contain. Dynamic alignment is how rules arrive without a vote. You do not get to wave 1982 at that and call the objection “fearmongering.”

Roman can overclaim. You underclaim. The honest test is dull and public. Publish the exclusions page before Montreal: no automatic alignment with Brussels content rules, no European last word on a Canadian platform, Parliament keeps the statute. Put the rejected August trade text on the same table. Score a corridor financed twice before 1 January 2027.

Until those papers exist, “wait for the bill” is not fact-checking. It is a permission slip for the room to write the next rule in another capital and call the Charter the alibi. Numbers do not lie. Speeches are numbers too, once you print them.

text:
How to Make Money With Google Maps (No Money Down, No Risk)

Everything I did to go from zero to my first paying clients, before I ever ran an ad.

Google Maps is one of the most underrated ways to start making money online.

It won't scale you to hundreds of thousands a month by itself. But to get your foot in the door with no risk and no money down, nothing beats it.

Quick disclaimer: no income guarantees. I don't know if you'll make money. I'm just showing you what I did.

What I actually did

For 8 to 10 hours a day, I sat down and called local businesses off Google Maps to sell them:

A website
More Google reviews
Missed-call text-back

That's it. I kept doing it until I hit $3-4K a month, and only then did I start running ads. Once you have money for ads, that's how you scale.

Small businesses have no automation and don't understand AI. I ran everything through the  AI, which holds websites, reviews, SEO, Google Business and Voice AI in one piece of software for about $300 a month. You resell it to local businesses and they think you're a magician.

Product is commoditized. Sales is the skill.

AI has changed the game. Anyone can build a website or an automation now, and there are free snapshots of the software setup everywhere. Everyone is selling the same thing.

The technical barrier is gone. It's all about sales now, meaning how well you can sell, scale and acquire customers, whether you charge $100 or $400 a month.

At $550K a month, 95% of what we do doesn't apply to you. What applies to you is how to land your first few customers, and the way to get good at sales is cold calling.

Step 1: Find the businesses

Pick a city and a service business, like "handyman Reno, Nevada." Scroll Google Maps until you find businesses with:

No website
Few reviews (0 to 20)
Maybe a bad review or two

These are perfect targets. Once I could afford it, I had a virtual assistant scrape lists of home service businesses with 0-20 reviews and no website. You can also use a scraping tool.

And when people say this is saturated, look at the map. You can find four in a row with nothing.

Step 2: Sell the outcome, not the feature

Nobody cares that you'll "build a website." They care about what it does for them.

The outcome always comes down to one of two things: saving them time or getting them more business.

Here's the kind of conversation I'd have:

"I noticed you don't have a website and your competitors do. Any reason for that?""Do you have a lot of happy customers?" (They'll always say yes.)"I only see 11 Google reviews, and one negative one."

The owner almost always knows exactly who left that review, and it bothers them. From there, you pitch the outcome:

More and better reviews mean you rank higher on Google

Ranking higher means you can charge more

A better website means more leads
Step 3: Sell ONE thing

When I started, I only talked about the website. That was all I knew how to do.
If you pitch reviews, a voice AI agent, automations, missed-call text-back and social media management in the same call, it's too much to take in. Clarity creates the sale. As a beginner, you can't explain five features when you've never sold one.

Pick one offer and get really good at selling it. Sell it a few times, even on a free trial, to collect testimonials. Then keep going.

Step 4: Don't sell on the first call

Your only goal on the phone is to book a Zoom meeting. That's where you close.

Business owners want to talk about themselves, their business and their competitors. So say you'll:

Analyze their competitors

Look at their bad reviews

Audit their website
Hit those pain points, get them on the call, and close them there.
Why cold calling works (and why people quit)

Cold calling is scary. Most people make 10 calls and stop, or never make one.

But 500 to 1,000 cold calls will teach you more than most people ever learn. You'll get better at talking about your offer, you'll hear the real struggles of local businesses, and you'll learn the questions they ask. That puts you ahead of 99% of people trying this.

And 99% of people quit before they hit $5K a month. If you get past that first sticking point, you have enough cash for ads and proof that it works. That's where things speed up.

No excuses on time

Have a 9-to-5? Call on Saturdays.

On the East Coast? Call the West Coast after work.
On the West Coast? Wake up early and call the East Coast.
I did this for about two and a half years with no expenses. I lived with my mom and cold called 10 hours a day. I got really, really good at sales.
The bottom line

Find local businesses with no website and few reviews

Sell one offer, focused on the outcome
Call to book a meeting, not to close
Repeat until you can afford ads
It's simple, but it isn't easy. Most people won't do it, and that's your edge.

I'll explain with an example:

Let's say OpenAI builds an OSS 1T-50B multimodal model that is extremely good at communicating and coordinating with their closed frontier model (because they can co train them), and is also much better at using their harnesses and scaffolding than other models (cause they can build terrific environments to help the model learn their scaffoldings & harnesses). 

They also host it on Jalapeno v4 in 2031, which is co-designed with both the open model and their closed models. Additionally, they offer legal CoT distillation from their closed models exclusively for their open models. And they do all this at a dirt-cheap price on the Pareto frontier.

I don't understand why, despite seeing the success of Apple and Nvidia—driven by co-design, vertical and horizontal integration, and an iron grip on the supply chain—people discount similar approaches taken by OpenAI and Anthropic.

The model is the product, distribution is the moat, and infrastructure is the flywheel. This is the cardinal rule that has been proven over at least the past three years for AI industry and past 3 decades for the semiconductor and internet era.

text:
At 29, I had a good job, a small apartment, and plans for the future.

I thought I was finally getting somewhere.

Then, within three months, everything changed.

The company I worked for downsized, and I was among the people laid off.

At first, I wasn't worried.

“I'll find another job,” I told myself.

But weeks became months.

My savings slowly disappeared.

I stopped eating out.

Then I stopped buying things I didn't need.

Eventually, I started calculating whether I could afford transportation before leaving the house.

One evening, I checked my account.

₦2,000.

That was all I had left.

I sat quietly on my bed, staring at the balance on my phone.

I had never felt so helpless.

Then my younger sister called.

“Have you eaten?”

I lied.

“Yes.”

She laughed.

“Okay. I'll call you tomorrow.”

After the call ended, I broke down.

Not because of the money.

Because I was tired of pretending that I was okay.

The next morning, I woke up early and decided to stop waiting for the perfect opportunity.

I printed a few copies of my CV and started walking from one business to another.

Some rejected me.

Some promised to call.

Some didn't even look at my CV.

On the fourth day, a small company offered me temporary work.

The salary wasn't what I used to earn.

But I accepted immediately.

For the first few months, I did everything they asked.

I arrived early.

I stayed late.

I learned new skills.

And I saved whatever I could.

A year later, I was offered a permanent position.

It wasn't the life I had imagined.

It was actually better.

Because now I knew what it felt like to lose everything.

And I knew I could still rebuild.

Sometimes life doesn't give you a warning before changing your plans.

You just wake up one morning and realize you're starting again.

But starting again isn't the same as starting from nothing.

You still have your experience.

You still have your lessons.

You still have the strength you gained from surviving what almost broke you.

Sometimes, the chapter that feels like the end is simply the chapter where you learn how to begin again.

The process for selecting the American Expedtionary Force soldier that would be reinterred on November 11, 1921 as President Harding dedicated The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is detailed in @combathistorian 's incredibly well researched book, The Unknowns: The Untold Story of America’s Unknown Soldier and WWI’s Most Decorated Heroes Who Brought Him Home.

I helped many families, VFW posts, and counties research  their World War I service members during the years of the World War I Centennial. World War I was the first U.S. conflict that Graves Registration Teams follow the fighting, recording the name, rank, Army serial number, unit, location of the casualty occurring, date and circumstances of death, and date and place of burial. Indicators of any grave markers was noted as was disposition of ID tags. 

That information was eventually  transferred onto Burial Cards. Card Register of Burials of Deceased American Soldiers, 1917–1922 (National Archives AID 6943087, Records Group 92): Summary cards (digitized before or during the WWI Centennial and available online via the National Archives Catalog, Fold3, and related genealogy websites) documenting death/burial details for the over 78,000 American soldiers who died overseas during WWI, the intervention in Russia, and occupation of Germany.

The more detailed Burial Files are retained at the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis, MO. They can be viewed by appointment at the archive in St. Louis. The WWI Burial Files were NOT impacted by the 1973 Records fire that burned approximately 80% of personnel files of Army veterans who served during the period November 1912 to January 1960 and US Air Force veterans with names alphabetical after Hubb... who served September 1947 through January 1964.

Many people do not realize the WWI dead were, in many cases, exhumed and reburied three or four times before arriving at their final resting place. The first time they were exhumed was to relocate them to a more centralized collecting cemetery in in preparation for construction of the original eight American Cemeteries to be completed:
Aisne-Marne American Cemetery (France)
Brookwood American Cemetery (United Kingdom)
Flanders Field American Cemetery (Belgium)
Meuse-Argonne American Cemetery (France)
Oise-Aisne American Cemetery (France)
Somme American Cemetery (France)
St. Mihiel American Cemetery (France)
Suresnes American Cemetery (France)

As work progressed on developing these cemeteries,  the men were exhumed from the temporary collecting cemeteries and reinterred at the eight American Cemeteries. The families of the deceased were sent letters asking them to return their preference of having their loved one's remains returned to the United States for burial or their preference for the remains to remain at the overseas American Cemeteries  with their fallen comrades. About 31,000 families chose permanent overseas burial. The British thought the Americans foolish and refused to offer bringing the remains of British fallen home. A senior British official noted, "We don't need the roads of Europe clogged with convoys of the dead."

text:
Students discuss social and technical implications of worldwide sightings in an experimental course given at the Davis Campus.

By Dr. P. S. Moller
Assistant Professor, Mechanical Engineering
University of California, Davis

Intelligent curiosity and interest about UFO sightings are showing up in the college world. A course offered at the University of California, Davis Campus, for the winter quarter 1967-68, attempted to bring the knowledge of the physical scientists, the sociological interests of the political scientist, and the curiosity of the students together. The course was taught by the writer, assisted by Dr. Dennis Livingston, the political scientist, and attended by 30 students, with majors evenly divided among the natural sciences, physical sciences, and liberal arts.

The course, entitled Flying Saucers: The Social and Technological Implications, is exactly that. The requirement—an open mind to all phenomena. An open mind is a very difficult requirement since the barrier of superstition has closed off effective evaluation of the subject. Until 1951 it could be said that the public in general and the Air Force (the official governmental agency responsible for deciphering UFO activity) in particular held a less biased attitude towards the existence of alien spacecraft. After 1951 when the Air Force reversed the opinion it had previously offered to the public and began selecting the information it released, nearly everyone’s objectivity was affected.

Today, a tentative idea, such as this course, faces tremendous prejudice in all areas that might possibly be concerned with UFO’s—from the scientist to the cultist who claims to believe Venus has chosen him as a prophet. Now almost everyone justifiably is wary of the religious fanatics and the claims made in a thousand hoaxes, so the students were not surprised at the three men who showed up during one course discussion to sit back and scoff at every point. This was an expected show of disbelief. However, the course tried to examine more unexpected negative attitudes held in the other areas where open minds are taken for granted. It is far more detrimental to the objective study of UFO’s when Dr. Hugh Dryden, previous director, National Advisory Committee on Aeronautics, said, “There are no such things as flying saucers—nothing to them at all!”

A two-part danger arises from this refusal to deal with UFO’s. First, the scientific world excuses its lack of objectivity and serious exploration into the subject because it is “obviously” an area reserved for crackpots and overly vivid imaginations. Secondly, the Air Force investigative apparatus uses these same hoaxes and fanatics as a smoke screen for their own very serious investigations and conclusions—mostly kept secret from the public. For example, there are many cases of UFO eyewitnesses questioned by the Air Force. The tactics prove to the witness he was hallucinating. Nonetheless, the interviewers write down every detail of the “hallucination” and even go as far as showing the witness photographs (many not available to the public) and asking him if he can identify any one of them as the craft he has just seen.

Creating doubts is a way of achieving skepticism. This is as false as the form of skepticism which makes itself the science with egocentricity the gauge, a gauge that is limited to measuring our life as the apex of all life. Today most of the scientific world accepts the existence of life elsewhere in the universe. Thus, the question becomes one of commutation, i.e., how do they get here. The main reasons scientists discount the existence of flying saucers is still our own boundaries of knowledge concerning the physics of matter at speeds approaching the speed of light. Of course, for us traveling through the universe seems impossible because our physics states that we can travel only at speeds no faster than the speed of light. History is filled with examples of our unwillingness to look beyond the currently accepted theories. Some engineers may recall that the initial studies regarding the speed of sound led us to believe that the sound barrier represented a theoretical upper limit to that speed in the atmosphere.

It is necessary, however, to state that some skepticism is important. To say that it is not is just another unfair extreme. For instance, the students as a whole were very skeptical which provided sharp questions for the lecturers and themselves alike. This kept the course from being just a comparatively high-level cult of its own.

The scientific hypotheses form the bulk of this paper, and as it turned out, the course. Some interesting sociological implications, however, concerned the realization that history is filled with the eventual collapse of civilizations through the terror and loss of self-confidence in the face of a superior civilization. Our own American Indian is a familiar example. Would it affect us to know for certain someone is much more advanced, causing us to look like barbarians in comparison?

Another implication—religious cults formed because of UFO’s have similar behavior patterns that in many ways take on man’s ageless desire to attach higher meaning to the unexplained. A third idea—what might be “their” point of view? Could it be they feel we are much like the aborigines are to us, to be studied and observed undisturbed in their natural habitat? The sociological, then, attempted to broaden perspective, to use the knowledge gained from history to prepare for any future reality.
As curiosity increased about the technical implications of flying saucers, the writer approached outside sources to help correlate the rapidly increasing data in preparation for further exploration. To prevent the usual negative interpretations, the questions were presented as part of the writer’s studies related to the physiological effects surrounding a state-of-the-art propulsion system to be designed. Only at the conclusion of the discussions were the questions revealed to be about UFO’s. The reaction was always the same, shock at the amount of correlation between the reported environmental effects surrounding the UFO’s and our own technological knowledge of the effects of magnetic fields, plasmas, etc. It was a very effective way of insuring objectivity on the subject and at the same time convincing the scientist to look further into the subject.
The exciting technical areas studied in the course related to propulsion systems that might duplicate the reported performance and environmental effects of UFO’s. The physical evidence of reported performance was gathered by the writer and extrapolated into our own state-of-the-art. One potentially useful propulsion system was designed by the writer which employs very large alternating magnetic fields > 100 kilogauss that might be obtained through the use of super conductors. Unfortunately, due to the proprietary nature of the propulsion system, the writer can only hint at its characteristics.

A large magnetic field, > 10 kilogauss, is capable of setting up eddy currents within the body. If one makes any movement an EMF will be developed which will give the effect of shock and tend to terminate the motion made, causing a temporary paralysis. By moving a hand or arm a subject will also experience a prickling sensation. A third magnetic field effect causes subjects to see “stars” when their heads are put into even weak magnetic fields. In an extremely large alternating magnetic field one would not have to move to experience paralysis and the prickling sensation. The exciting correlations here are the number of reliable cases brought out by such reports as UFO evidence by the National Investigation Committee on Aerial Phenomena where witnesses have reported this same temporary paralysis and prickling sensation when near a UFO. These same people could not have known about the magnetic effects since very few scientists are aware of them.

Another piece of relative technical evidence—when certain materials such as tungsten are placed in magnetic fields, their measured electrical resistance undergoes a large increase. There are literally hundreds of reported cases where automobile and house lights have dimmed or gone out when in the vicinity of a UFO. An interesting case is that of an airplane flying over South America with a full load of passengers. The cabin lights dimmed for over an hour, the exact length of time the plane was paced by a UFO witnessed by a large number of the passengers. This piston engine airplane had tungsten filament cabin lights, while modern aircraft employ fluorescent lighting and are not affected. The aircraft’s magnetic compass was also reported to be totally inoperative during the time it was being paced.

In another case a house located near a hovering UFO underwent a dimming and brightening of its lights at the same frequency as the light intensity changes of the UFO (≈ 1 c.p.s.). This frequency is near the optimum theoretical frequency for pulsing the superconductor in the writer’s aforementioned design.

A further question arises—why do so many of the reported UFO’s hover near high-voltage lines. This cannot be answered for certain, but it is possible to charge an electric power supply by induction from a high-voltage alternating current power source without being in contact with it. The explanation that some scientists give, however, is that what appears to be a UFO near a power line is actually ball lightning or plasmas. In the writer’s opinion, this is a case of trying to explain something taboo that we know little about by something we know even less about but is not taboo.

A propulsion system employing a large magnetic field could use it in conjunction with a plasma (possibly ionized air). If such a system is designed the circular shape would be near optimum and the plasma would probably be generated near the edge of the machine to maximize both thrust and control. If such a plasma were employed it would glow in the dark and change color with the degree of ionization (power level, or speed) and the altitude of operation of the vehicle. Those familiar with reports of UFO sightings will recognize this behavior as characteristic of many of the good UFO reports.

In addition to the above-mentioned correlations between our technical knowledge and the reported performance of UFO’s; the lack of sound at high and low speeds; the heat sometimes reported; and the failure of automotive ignition systems in the proximity of UFO’s can also be accounted for fairly well technically. Thus the technology available provides reasonable answers to most of the questions concerning the performance of those reported UFO’s within our atmosphere.

In conclusion, the writer feels that the time devoted to such an experimental course was small in proportion to the value gained both from the questions brought out and the beginnings made in utilizing any technical correlations. There was an overall feeling by the students—the more knowledge shared, the less fear and absurdities surrounded the UFO’s. But above all, if such courses can just help to bring the scientific world closer to objective investigation, the vicious cycle of superstition could be stopped—a cycle that enables scientists to excuse UFO’s as too ridiculous for thought, which in turn allows the clutter of superstition and fear to feed on itself with little denial. More disciplined thought and exploration is needed to correlate the large amount of relevant technical information. If this is done, the disturbing UFO could very well become the more useful and didactic identified flying object.—End.

Photo caption

Photo of UFO taken through truck window with a model 101 Polaroid camera by Rex E. Heflin, an Orange County, California, highway inspector, near Santa Ana on August 3, 1965.

THE CURRENT UFO SITUATION IN RUSSIA

In May, 1967, a sponsoring group of scientists, the military, writers, and public figures met to form an unofficial body whose purpose it would be to conduct a preliminary scientific investigation of UFO’s. Those present included Professor Heinrich Ludwig; Doctors of Science Nikolai Zhirov and Igor Bestuzhev-Lada; chief navigator of Soviet polar aviation Valentine Akkuratov; Generals Porfiri Stolyarov, Leonid Reino, Georgi Uger and Georgi Zevalkin; twice Hero of the Soviet Union Grigori Sivkov, Master of Science (engineering); Heroes of the Soviet Union docent Yekaterina-Ryabova and Natalia Kravtsova.

The organization, set up October, 1967, is called the UFO Section of the All-Union Cosmonautics Committee, with headquarters at the Central House of Aviation and Cosmonautics in Moscow. Air Force Major General Porfiri Stolyarov was elected chairman of the section. Those of us who are participating in this new and exciting undertaking have an ambitious program of work ahead. The first step will be to organize the collection of reliable information on UFO’s. That will be done at the outset by the existing systems of astronomical, meteorological, and geophysical observatories, satellite and space-rocket tracking stations, and the radar installations of civilian airports, and the hydrometeorological service. All these organizations can make UFO observations with equipment now available.

In the design stage are special devices for photographing UFO’s and recording the radiation and magnetic disturbances which they may be responsible for. The recorded observations will serve to check hypotheses. These hypotheses should not, in my opinion, attempt to explain the nature of UFO’s in terms of familiar phenomena. Judging by other surprises, nature has some in store for us here too, and we must be ready for perhaps a radical “reassessment of values.” The hypothesis that UFO’s originate in other worlds, that they are flying craft from planets other than earth, merits the most serious examination.

… From an article in the February, 1968, issue of Soviet Life by Felix Zigel, Doctor of Science (Technology), Assistant Professor, Moscow Aviation Institute.

text:
I still find the last few minutes of Maura Murray’s known story difficult to understand.

Not because we know what happened to her. We don’t.

It is because, for a few minutes on February 9, 2004, people actually knew where she was. They could see her. Someone spoke to her. Police were on their way.

And then, somehow, she was gone.

Maura was 21 years old and studying nursing at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. On that Monday, she left campus and drove north into New Hampshire. She had not told the people around her exactly where she was going. The reason for the trip has never been fully established. (FBI⁠)

That evening, around 7:27 p.m., a resident along Route 112 in Haverhill, New Hampshire, reported seeing a car that had gone off the road. It was Maura’s black Saturn.

A local school-bus driver, Butch Atwood, stopped when he came across the crashed vehicle. He saw a young woman standing outside the car. She appeared cold and was shivering, but he did not see obvious injuries. He offered to call the police.

She asked him not to.

According to his account, she told him she had already called AAA for assistance. Atwood was concerned because the area had little or no reliable cellphone reception, so he continued home and called police himself. His call was received at about 7:43 p.m.

This is where the story becomes almost impossible to comprehend.

When police arrived at the crash scene, Maura was no longer there.

Her Saturn remained. It was damaged and locked. Inside were some of her belongings. But Maura herself had disappeared.

There was no clear explanation for where she had gone.

She had been seen beside that car only minutes earlier. Now there was an empty road, a damaged vehicle, and a young woman who seemed to have simply stepped out of the story.

Searches followed. Her family waited for answers. Investigators pursued leads, but no confirmed sighting of Maura after that night has established what happened to her. The FBI still lists her as missing.
