text:
I grew up hearing that America was the most powerful country in the world.

But as I got older, I started asking a different question:

How did America get there?

Because America wasn’t born as the country that dominates global finance, technology, entertainment, military alliances, and international politics.

In 1776, it was a new nation fighting for independence.

Today, decisions made in Washington, New York, Silicon Valley, Houston, and other American cities can affect markets, technology, security, and businesses far beyond America’s borders.

So how did we get here?

The answer isn’t one thing.

It is a story of geography, immigration, industrialization, war, technology, finance, institutions, military power, and alliances.

And, like almost every country’s history, it is also a story containing achievements and serious contradictions.

America’s geography gave it an extraordinary starting point.

Two enormous oceans separated the country from Europe and Asia. The territory contained vast agricultural land, forests, minerals, rivers, and eventually enormous industrial resources.

Then came something even more important:

People.

Generations of immigrants arrived from different parts of the world, bringing labor, skills, languages, businesses, ideas, and cultures.

America’s population became extraordinarily diverse.

Then industrialization transformed the country.

Factories expanded.

Railroads connected distant regions.

Oil became increasingly important.

American companies learned how to produce goods on a massive scale.

By the early twentieth century, the United States had become one of the world’s major industrial and economic powers.

Then came the wars that changed the international system.

World War I weakened the European powers.

World War II changed the balance even more dramatically.

By the end of World War II, much of Europe and Asia had suffered enormous destruction, while the United States possessed a huge industrial economy and emerged as the leading economic and military power of the Western world.

The dollar’s international role grew enormously.

The Bretton Woods system established the dollar as the anchor currency of the postwar monetary system, helping create the foundations for its continuing global importance.

But America didn’t simply build power by keeping its resources at home.

It helped construct institutions and alliances that shaped the postwar world.

The United States participated in the creation of institutions such as the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

It became a central member of NATO.

It helped finance European recovery through the Marshall Plan.

And American alliances eventually stretched across Europe and into the Indo-Pacific.

That alliance network became one of America’s most important sources of influence.

Instead of standing alone, America built relationships with countries that shared security or economic interests.

NATO, for example, eventually became a military alliance connecting the United States with numerous European and North American countries. The alliance currently provides security cooperation involving roughly one billion people.

But there was another American advantage that was perhaps even more powerful than military strength.

Strengthening Assam’s Rural Economy Through Better Finance, Markets and Value Creation.

The strength of Assam’s rural economy lies not only in what our farmers produce, but in the value and opportunities we create around that production.

For a State where a large section of the population depends on agriculture and allied activities, strengthening rural incomes requires better access to finance, stronger markets, local processing, infrastructure and entrepreneurship.

This was the larger concern I highlighted at the two-day conference on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” in New Delhi, where I called for region-specific financial mechanisms and stronger end-to-end value chains for Assam.

Agriculture and allied activities engage around 40–46% of India’s workforce while contributing around 18% to GDP. Improving farm incomes, therefore, is not merely an agricultural objective; it is essential for strengthening employment, purchasing power and economic resilience in rural communities.

Good production alone cannot guarantee prosperity. Without reliable markets, storage and processing facilities, farmers may be forced to sell at low prices, particularly in the case of perishable produce.

This is why Assam needs stronger rural value chains.

Along with cold storage, warehouses and transportation, we need processing, packaging and branding closer to production centres. When value addition happens within Assam, it creates employment beyond the farm and allows a greater share of the economic value to remain in our villages and towns.

Finance is equally important.

While agricultural credit has expanded nationally, regional disparities remain. The southern region accounts for around 48% of agricultural credit, compared with approximately 8% for the eastern region, with the North-East receiving an even smaller share.

Uniform financial frameworks cannot always address different regional realities. Assam requires mechanisms suited to its production patterns, landholding structures and local conditions.

Institutional credit must also become more accessible to tenant farmers, leasehold cultivators, forest-rights beneficiaries, small tea growers and those cultivating public land. The rollout of Farmer IDs in Assam under the leadership of Hon’ble Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma can help create a more targeted system of support.

Assam also possesses several high-value products capable of transforming rural incomes.

Agarwood is one such opportunity. With regulatory facilitation, quality-testing facilities, processing infrastructure and stronger export channels, we can build the entire value chain—from cultivation and processing to quality assurance and exports—within Assam.

Our premium ginger and turmeric from the hills, Assam Lemon, Bhut Jolokia and indigenous rice varieties similarly offer tremendous potential through branding, processing and better market linkages. Improved international air-cargo connectivity can further connect these products directly with global markets.

The objective must be to create an ecosystem where farmers are not merely producers of raw materials but increasingly become participants in processing, enterprise and value creation. This can also generate opportunities for our youth and women in logistics, packaging, food processing, marketing and technology.

At the same time, our rural economy must become more resilient to floods, droughts and pest outbreaks through timely intervention and responsive financial support.

The vision is simple: production must lead to processing, processing to enterprise, and enterprise to employment and higher incomes.

Our villages should not merely produce raw materials. They should become centres of value creation.

A stronger rural economy will ultimately mean a stronger Assam.

text:
In 2025 the United States imported $309 billion of goods from China, down from $539 billion in 2018. #China's share of #American imports fell from 21.2 percent to 13.4 percent by 2024.

Freund, Mattoo, Mulabdic and Ruta traced ten-digit import lines from 2017 to 2022 for the World Bank. The countries replacing China tended to be deeply integrated with China. "To displace #China on the export side, countries must embrace China's supply chains." Schulze and Xin at the IMF, June 2025, value-added tables to 2022. "Chinese value added has been increasingly exported to the #US through other countries".

The one place decoupling looks real is Vietnam. Its domestic value added in strategic exports to #America ran 10 and 12 percentage points above the counterfactual by 2022, Chinese value added fell, and the authors call it reallocation, not rerouting. Real factories.

And who built them. It counts eight more greenfield projects committing #Chinese capital to Vietnam's electrical and machinery sector than the counterfactual by 2022, and offers that "Chinese firms relocate their production to #Vietnam through greenfield FDI". Then what it cannot see. "Due to the lack of information on the ultimate ownership of these FDI projects, we caution that the effects on FDI could include those from Chinese firms and non-Chinese firms in China."

American origin rules cannot see it either. Under 19 CFR 134.1 another country becomes the country of origin only if work there effects a "substantial transformation". Ownership is not in the definition.

So the two instruments that would tell a government whether decoupling worked, the customs rule and the value-added table, both record place. Neither records command. A tariff can move a production line across a border. It cannot move the line out of anyone's reach, and the accounts that certify success cannot ask.

Sovereignty is a relation to territory. Coercion is a relation to command. A backup supplier is a backup only if no one can order both lines to stop at once, and that is the one variable the ledgers do not carry. A state can decouple its map and keep its exposure, and cannot know which it has done.

Two counterweights. Over 80 percent of American industrial inputs are sourced at home, and American, Japanese and Korean investment into Vietnam rose alongside Chinese.

If an ownership-resolved series shows the Chinese-controlled share of Vietnam's strategic exports to America falling, the claim dies.

text:
Start here.

A war-band can take a peninsula and still not own its own story. Muhammad died in Medina in June 632. Within a generation his men were not reciting one fixed text. According to the Sunni canon itself—Sahih al-Bukhari 4987 and 5102—Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, campaigning in Armenia and Azerbaijan under the third caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (r. 644–656), heard Syrian and Iraqi soldiers accusing one another over variant readings of the Qur’an and feared schism. Uthman ordered Zayd ibn Thabit and a small committee to produce one official recension from the sheets already gathered under Abu Bakr after the battle of Yamamah (c. 632–633), sent copies to the main garrison cities, and commanded that other written collections be burned. That is not how a father handles truth. That is how a commander handles a riot in camp. The man of the raid had offered fighting men what fighting men already priced—women, spoil, rank, a paradise with the smell of victory on it—and he got his army: Hijrah 622, Badr 624, the taking of Mecca in 630, a community armed enough that, after 632, it walked out of Arabia and broke the near frontiers of Byzantium and Ctesiphon. He did not get control of the wording. The sword can gather a host. It cannot keep ten mouths from rewriting the banner. When the banner starts a fight, the caliph does not repent. He lights a fire under the other pages (Bukhari 4987).

That is the method. Feed the pack. Win the ground. When the story cracks, burn the variants. A hunter plates the hunger. He does not remake it.

Now the other table.

The gospel is still the worst product in the shop. No one designing customers writes it. Someone who wants sons writes it. Soft men swollen with appetite will always walk to the louder stall. That walk is not evidence. It is the x-ray. And it leaves Jesus where He stands: above the stall, the legion, and every cheap replacement—worthy, because He refused to purchase us with our vice. He paid in blood.

God is not recruiting buyers. He is calling children home.

Jesus does not bait Jew or Greek with their favorite dish. He orders both to drop the plate.

The Jew wanted a war-crown: Rome thrown off, Zion armed, a Messiah who wins like Caesar. Jesus answers with timber and nails, under Pontius Pilate, c. 30–33. “My kingdom is not of this world” (John 18:36). Come back to the Father. Receive a name. “To all who received Him, He gave the right to become children of God” (John 1:12).

The Gentile wanted the old night: the body as shrine, the feast that never closes, the rot Paul names in the streets around the churches (Romans 1; 1 Corinthians 5–6). Jesus answers with a cut. Stop staring. Tear out the eye (Matthew 5:27–32). One covenant bed. Rule the flesh. Then live as a son, not as a stomach.

He does not toss steak to the wolf. He puts bread in a mouth that only knew raw meat—and then dies and rises so the mouth can say Abba. No harem as wages. Adoption. The Lamb dies for the enemy. The stone rolls.

Muhammad runs the opposite shop. He wanted a host and he bought one with the inventory the host already priced: raids for caravan wealth after 622, plural marriage written into law, captives as a lawful yield of war. That raises banners. It does not raise sons of God. And when the inventory of words would not sit still, Uthman, about 650–653, burned the extras. Army first. Canon by bonfire second.

Look at what grows, without perfume. Where Christ’s gospel actually entered—not the costume of Christ, the command of Christ—even under crooked kings, a strange orchard appeared: the weak life counts, the child is not a clan chip only, the woman is not a share of loot, letters and universities sprout because a soul is addressed by God and must learn to answer. Cathedral schools and the medieval universitas—Bologna (1088), Paris (c. 1150), Oxford (c. 1096)—did not grow from a tent of captives. They grew from a Cross and from “let the little children come to Me” (Mark 10:14).

A creed built to please the raider will not pause and see woman and child as the image of God. It will see them as cargo—flesh, hush, wall. Useful falsehood, sanctified war, the killing of the holdout, poverty called fate: that is not bad weather on the map. That is what you plant when desire wears a scabbard.

If truth were the average male wish, heaven would be unemployed. We already know the wish: more body, more force, more alibi. That wish is the clay of this century—in the old paganism that still rides under a prophet’s name, and in the new ideologies that spit on the church. Both want a homemade god. One names it caliphate. One names it State. Both say the vote of man is the verdict of right. That sentence is not faith. It is apostasy with a flag.

The hunter blesses the pulse. The Father breaks it and names it child. That is why the gospel still will not sell to synagogue or forum. And that is why Jesus still has no rival: He would rather lose the crowd than nurse the fever. He lost the crowd. He kept the empty tomb. He kept the way back to the Father.

text:
It’s not every day I read something that physically chokes me up. But today is that day.  @TheIronGod2 sent me a message explaining the other side of the foster care system. The people who actually want to make a difference.  He read my posts and told a story of his own, as a foster parent.

To say it is bittersweet is an understatement. And anyone who makes it to the end will hardly have a dry eye.  But he and his family are the best of what the human condition has to offer. 👇

“Hey Sir. I just wanted to reach out and say thank you for sharing you story about the foster care system and your families struggles. 

I come from the opposite side of things with foster care, but I fully understand your experience.

I dropped out of high school and joined the Australian army at 17. As the son of a boat builder it seemed a weird choice, but it was something I had wanted to do since I was a young teen.

It wasn't until I finished basic that my father told me that my grandfather (who had died before I was born) was a SGT in the NZ Army and fought in Korea. He came home with some demons, and after a stint in jail, drank himself to death.

I was a Rifleman for the first 2 years of my service, transferred a couple of times to other rolls, and now after 30 years in, I'm a WO2 running a workshop in a Calvary Regiment.

The foster care bit started 23 years ago. My wife had spent some time in care when she was early teens, and even though we had 3 kids of our own, she wanted to become a carer. I was hesitant at first, but then it was like Isaiah 6:8. A voice said "who will I send to care for them?" and we answered. 

So, we have cared for and loved every child that has come into our home. 

Nine years ago, we had a young girl by the name of Thamey come into our care. She had Cerebral palsy alongwhen a host of other medical challenges that meant she would never be able to care for herself. 

It was that her family didn't want her or had abused her, they simply didn't have the ability to meet her care needs.

When she turned 18, she was no longer a ward of the state.  We were told they would find a nursing home for her to live in and that our job in caring and loving her was over. 

We fought this and went to court to become her legal adult guardians, and she remained with us as our daughter.

In February, we found out that Thamey was in early stages of heart failure. Unfortunately due to her disability there wasn't anything that could be done.

She was in hospital for her 21st birthday. We snuck in some champagne for her to taste.

She passed away on Friday night. 

Of all the things I have done in my life, being a father to children in care has been the most challenging, but also the most rewarding thing I will ever do. 

People still ask me why I'm raising other people's kids. My response is "Someone has to do it, and if not me than who?"”

***I hope the world sees this, far and wide. Please share to honor these people, and the late Thamey who as of Friday night, is no longer with us***

text:
The Darkness of Massachusetts: Another Personal Story

I’ve been thinking about this a lot lately. And maybe how violence against children in MA isn’t anything new. And perhaps the state taking kids away is a knee jerk from a larger issue.

You people keep asking about me and this situation, it goes deeper. And I guess I’ll share it. But it’s not for the weak.

The Lindsey Clancy case captured national attention with her killing her 3 kids. Well, both of my parents had THEIR parents try to kill them as well.

When my Dad was 6, his father came home drunk one day and tried throwing him off the third story of a triple decker outside Boston. The reason? Because he thought my dad was defective because he had cerebral palsy. My aunts interdicted and saved my dad. That’s when the state took him away and put him in foster care.

My mom was just a baby when her mother desperately asked the woman who I refer to as “Nana” to take her in. She was clearly on drugs and not well, but at least had the good sense to give my mom away to someone safer.

Anyway, my Nana knew this woman was not well. But she apparently cleaned her act up and came by the house everyday for a few weeks. The woman wanted to just hold my mom one time. She made it seem like she was being genuine.

Finally my Nana relented and let her hold her for a sec.  The woman immediately tried taking my tiny 9 month old mom and smashing her to death against the wall.  Obviously my Nana intervened and stopped her before any serious damage was done.

So yea, both my parents were almost killed by their parents, in Massachusetts.  Out of my mom, dad, and sister, I’m the only one that wasn’t taken away from my family by the state or whoever.

I consider myself blessed and lucky. But I’ve been thinking about it alot lately. Perhaps more of an insight into why I am the way that I am.

I am grateful we are all still here. I love my family.  I am however, deeply horrified about what the state of Massachusetts actually is. What lurks beneath it in terms of energy.

text:
On November 29, 2000, Iowa residents David Winkelman and his stepson Richard Goddard heard a radio DJ promise $150,000 to anyone willing to permanently tattoo the station’s logo across their forehead.

They took him seriously.

The DJ at KORB’s “93 Rock” had offered $30,000 a year for five years to anyone who went through with it.

Winkelman and Goddard called the station to make sure the offer was real.

According to their later lawsuit, they were told it was.

A station representative even accompanied them to a tattoo parlour and paid for the tattoos.

Both men emerged with “93 Rock” and “Quad City Rocker” permanently inked across their foreheads.

The station photographed them and posted the pictures on its website.

Then came the truth.

The $150,000 offer had been a joke.

There was no prize.

Winkelman and Goddard sued the station and its DJ for breach of contract, fraud and negligence.

But neither case ever reached a decision on whether the station actually owed them the money.

Winkelman voluntarily dropped his lawsuit within months.

Goddard continued his case, but a judge eventually dismissed it after he repeatedly failed to appear in court.

Years later, the radio station changed its name and format.

The tattoos remained.

text:
Ultrasound Treatment Leads to Rapid Improvements in Parkinson’s | Knowridge

A treatment that uses concentrated sound waves inside the brain has produced rapid improvements in two people with severe Parkinson’s disease.

Doctors at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus treated two tiny brain pathways during one session, helping reduce shaking, stiffness, and slow movement.

The two pathways are separated by only about 6 to 9 millimeters. The procedures were the first dual-target focused ultrasound treatments of their kind performed in the Rocky Mountain region.

Parkinson’s disease develops when brain systems that control movement stop working normally. The condition becomes worse over time and can make everyday tasks such as dressing, eating, writing, walking, and getting out of a chair increasingly difficult.

Shaking is perhaps its most recognizable symptom, but Parkinson’s is much more than a tremor disorder. Many patients experience rigid muscles, slowed movement, balance difficulties, and involuntary movements, especially in later stages.

Doctors have several ways to manage these symptoms, but there is no treatment that cures Parkinson’s. Medicines can replace or support brain chemicals involved in movement, although their benefits may become harder to manage after years of disease.

Some people with advanced symptoms receive deep brain stimulation. In this treatment, surgeons place electrodes in specific brain areas and connect them to a device that sends controlled electrical signals.

Deep brain stimulation can provide major benefits, but it requires surgery and implanted hardware. Some patients cannot receive it because of infection concerns, other health problems, or factors that make brain surgery less suitable.

High-intensity focused ultrasound offers a different approach. Instead of opening the skull or implanting an electrode, doctors send many ultrasound beams through the skull and focus their combined energy on a very small brain target.

Each individual beam carries limited energy as it passes through surrounding tissue. Where the beams meet, however, enough energy is concentrated to create a precise permanent change that interrupts troublesome brain circuits.

MRI guidance allows doctors to locate the target and monitor the patient during treatment. Because the effect can appear quickly, clinicians can observe changes in symptoms while the patient is still undergoing the procedure.

Focused ultrasound was first approved in the United States for a pathway used to control severe tremor in certain people with Parkinson’s disease. That pathway is known as the dentatorubral thalamic tract.

A second pathway, called the pallidothalamic tract, has also become a treatment target. It is connected with several major Parkinson’s movement problems, including stiffness and the unusually slow movements that can make ordinary activities exhausting.

The University of Colorado team decided to treat both pathways during the same outpatient session. The procedure took around 90 minutes.

In one woman, treatment of the tremor pathway alone reduced her resting shaking by an estimated 60% to 70%. It did not provide much relief from her stiffness or slow movements.

Doctors then moved the ultrasound target by only a few millimeters and treated the second pathway. Neurologist Dr. Drew Kern said her tremor disappeared, while stiffness and movement speed improved by about 70%.

Her walking also became more fluid. The improvement appeared immediately, allowing the medical team to see the result while she was still on the MRI table.

The doctors later considered the same approach for a man with advanced Parkinson’s disease who was not suitable for deep brain stimulation. After treatment, the team reported that his rigidity disappeared, his movements became much less slow, and his tremor was greatly reduced.

The changes also affected simple daily activities. His wife reported that he slept particularly well because the tremor was no longer disturbing him, and he was able to eat breakfast with utensils without the difficulty he had experienced before.

These examples illustrate why doctors are interested in treating more than one brain pathway. Tremor is only one part of advanced Parkinson’s, and reducing shaking without improving stiffness or slowness may leave a patient with major disability.

By combining two targets, clinicians hope to address several movement symptoms in one treatment. This could be particularly useful for patients who have few other treatment choices.

There are important reasons for caution, however. Focused ultrasound creates a permanent change in brain tissue, and the long-term effects of the newer target and the dual-target approach are still being studied.

Researchers need to know whether the improvements remain months and years later. They must also carefully study possible changes in thinking, speech, balance, and other brain functions.

Another unanswered question involves treating both sides of the brain. Parkinson’s often affects both sides of the body, but the Colorado program has so far used focused ultrasound on only one side at a time.

U.S. regulators require at least six months between procedures when treatment is performed on the opposite side. Researchers are studying whether staged treatment of both sides can provide additional benefits without creating unacceptable risks.

The immediate improvements in these two patients are impressive, but they should be interpreted as early clinical experience rather than definitive evidence. Two cases cannot tell doctors how often the treatment will work, how long the benefit will last, or how frequently complications may occur.

The next step is careful follow-up and larger studies comparing outcomes across more patients. Those studies will help determine whether targeting both pathways offers a meaningful advantage over treating one target alone.

If the results hold up, focused ultrasound could broaden the choices available to people with advanced Parkinson’s disease who cannot receive deep brain stimulation. For patients whose movement problems have resisted medicines, that possibility could eventually translate into greater independence in basic parts of daily life.

text:
In the truest sense, Shakti is never obtained through consecration, idols, temple images, ritual procedures, or pran-pratishtha. Such images may serve as sacred supports for worship, but Shakti is not acquired or activated through rituals. Shakti is obtained and operates only through a living human body.
The awakened Ugra Shakti is attained by a Sadhaka through Sadhana and Siddhi, and made accessible to others through the living presence of a Siddha Guru. Through siddhi, Shakti may choose a living human body as Her seat and instrument of grace.
This is where the objection—“How can Devata exist within a human body?”—becomes difficult to reconcile with the very idea of avatara. If divine principles such as Vishu, Lakshmi, Shiva and others can manifest through embodied existence, the possibility of Shakti manifesting through a Siddha cannot simply be dismissed.
And there is an important distinction:
The body is not Shakti, but Shakti may choose the body as Her medium.
Therefore, one cannot claim to revere Shakti while disrespecting the body through which She has chosen to manifest. The respect offered to that body is not the worship of flesh—it is reverence for the Shakti residing and operating through it.
The Sadhaka must therefore learn not merely to look at the Siddha, but to look through the Siddha and recognise the Shakti.
The body is the medium.
Siddhi is the attainment.
The Siddha is the living channel.
Shakti is the reality.
To see only the human form is to stop at the doorway.
To recognise Shakti through that form is to enter.

“There are in our lives reservoirs of many kinds. Some reservoirs are to store water. Some are to store food, as we do in our family welfare program and as Joseph did in the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty. 

There should also be reservoirs of knowledge to meet the future needs; reservoirs of courage to overcome the floods of fear that put uncertainty in lives; reservoirs of physical strength to help us meet the frequent burdens of work and illness; reservoirs of goodness; reservoirs of stamina; reservoirs of FAITH. 

Yes, ESPECIALLY reservoirs of faith so that when the world presses in upon us, we stand firm and strong; 

When the temptations of a decaying world about us draw on our energies, sap our spiritual vitality, and seek to pull us down, we need a storage of faith that can carry youth and later adults over the dull, the difficult, the terrifying moments, disappointments, disillusionments, and years of adversity, want, confusion, and frustration.

I am grateful to my parents, for they made reservoirs for my brothers, my sisters, and me. The reservoirs were filled with prayer habits, study, activities, positive services, and truth and righteousness. 

Constant training, constant vigilance, companionship, and being watchmen of our own children are necessary in order to keep our homes intact and to bless our children in the Lord’s own way.

The Church auxiliaries are very important, and we should all partake of the blessings they offer. But we should NEVER, never allow them to replace parents, to relieve parents of the responsibility to teach their children the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Only by properly planning and charting our family life can we guide our children and keep them free from the pitfalls that lead to sin and destruction, and put them on the pathway to happiness and exaltation. 

In this, nothing is more powerful than the example of their own parents and the influence of their home life. 

The child will carry into his own life much that he sees in his family home life. 

If he sees his parents going to the temple frequently, he will begin to plan a temple life. If he is taught to pray for the missionaries, he will gradually gravitate toward the missionary program. Now, this is very simple, but it is the way of life.

Fathers and mothers, your foremost responsibility is your family. 

By working together you can have the kind of home the Lord expects you to have. By showing love and consideration for one another and for your children, you can build a reservoir of spiritual strength that will NEVER run dry.

(Kimball; Teachings of the Presidents, Chapter 19)

Home CENTERED.
Church supported. 

Every day we are showing our children and grandchildren what is important to us! 

As we make God the top priority in our lives— if they see us giving our time and attention to the things of eternity— we are not only building a strong foundation for ourselves, but for them as well. 

And over time, even if they leave for a while (or even a long time) that foundation will hold!

God’s promised ARE sure.

No. All flu shots are not now mRNA, and traditional options remain the bulk of what’s available. ￼
For the 2026–2027 U.S. season, most licensed flu vaccines still use the same long-standing platforms:
•  Egg-based inactivated shots (Afluria, Fluarix, FluLaval, Fluzone, etc.)
•  Cell-based inactivated (Flucelvax)
•  Recombinant protein (Flublok)
•  Live attenuated nasal spray (FluMist)
•  High-dose (Fluzone High-Dose) and adjuvanted (Fluad) products, which are preferred for many people 65+
Those platforms do not use mRNA. They remain widely available across ages, including children and people under 50. ￼
What did change
In August 2026 the FDA approved one mRNA flu vaccine: Moderna’s mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010). It is authorized for adults 50 and older (traditional approval for 50–64; accelerated approval for 65+ with a required confirmatory study). It is expected to be available this season at some retailers as an additional option, not a replacement for everything else. ￼
It uses the same general mRNA-LNP idea as the COVID mRNA shots, but encodes influenza hemagglutinin rather than SARS-CoV-2 spike. Manufacturing can be faster than egg-based production, which is the main practical advantage.
“Lightly tested” and long-term effects
The flu mRNA product itself is new, so multi-year follow-up on this specific shot is limited—that is true of any newly approved vaccine.
What exists so far:
•  A large phase 3 trial (~40,000 adults 50+) showed about 27% relative efficacy against lab-confirmed flu compared with a standard-dose traditional shot. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in both arms. Short-term reactions (sore arm, fatigue, headache, muscle aches) were more common with the mRNA shot and usually lasted 1–2 days. ￼
•  Approval for ages 65+ is accelerated and tied to more data versus high-dose comparators.
•  The broader mRNA-LNP platform has years of real-world use from COVID vaccines (hundreds of millions of doses) plus ongoing safety monitoring. That is not the same as decades of data on this exact flu formulation.
Traditional flu vaccines have far longer track records (egg-based production goes back many decades). You can still request those.
No public-health body has replaced the entire flu-vaccine supply with mRNA. If a clinic or pharmacy only offers the new product, you can ask for a conventional one or go elsewhere. Coverage and supply for the mRNA option may also lag because ACIP recommendation timing has been messy this year. ￼
If you have a specific age group, medical history, or preference (egg-free, high-dose, nasal, etc.), that determines which products actually apply to you.

U.S. Marshals arrested Angela Lipps at gunpoint in July 2025 while the 50-year-old Tennessee grandmother was watching her neighbor's kids — all because an AI facial recognition program decided her Facebook photo matched a bank fraud suspect a thousand miles away in Fargo, North Dakota. 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘬𝘯𝘦𝘸 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘈𝘐 𝘧𝘢𝘤𝘪𝘢𝘭 𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘨𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘦𝘤𝘩𝘯𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘺 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘣𝘦 𝘶𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘭𝘦 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘦𝘹𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘵𝘦 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘨𝘦 𝘢 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯, her lawsuit states. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐲𝐰𝐚𝐲.

Lipps had never set foot in North Dakota. She'd never even boarded a commercial flight. Bank surveillance video of the real suspect showed a different build and different facial features entirely — but Fargo detective Lucas Heck pushed the arrest warrant through regardless, according to the lawsuit. She was booked as a fugitive, extradited a thousand miles from her grandchildren, and told she was facing eight years in prison for a crime committed by a stranger she'd never met.

𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘶𝘨𝘨𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘰𝘧 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘣𝘦 𝘳𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘳 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘶𝘱 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨𝘭𝘺 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘷𝘪𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘪𝘮𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴, the suit alleges. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘤𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥, 𝘴𝘦𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘴, 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘛𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘬𝘴𝘨𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘊𝘩𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘮𝘢𝘴. 𝘞𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘤𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘥𝘺, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘪𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘤 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘦, 𝘴𝘶𝘤𝘩 𝘢𝘴 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘮𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘦𝘴. By the time she walked free on Christmas Eve, she'd lost her house, her car and her belongings.

Her attorney did what Fargo police never bothered to do — pulled her bank records and proved she was buying groceries in Tennessee the same day she was supposedly robbing a North Dakota bank. Charges dropped instantly. 𝘚𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘴 𝘪𝘯 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘦 𝘢𝘣𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘨𝘢𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘭𝘦𝘧𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘭𝘦𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘨𝘩 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘪𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘴𝘢𝘧𝘦, the complaint states.

The department's own then-chief admitted afterward that 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦𝘴 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘢𝘥𝘦, telling reporters, 𝘕𝘰 𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘦𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘥𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘦𝘥, 𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘶𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘭𝘺, 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵? He retired weeks later. Fargo itself has offered nothing — a city spokesperson says it 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴𝘯'𝘵 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘯 𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘨𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯, and has 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐳𝐞 to the woman its own detective jailed for six months on a hunch from a computer. Lipps is now suing the city and Detective Heck for $𝟏𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧.

U.S. Marshals arrested Angela Lipps at gunpoint in July 2025 while the 50-year-old Tennessee grandmother was watching her neighbor's kids — all because an AI facial recognition program decided her Facebook photo matched a bank fraud suspect a thousand miles away in Fargo, North Dakota. 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘬𝘯𝘦𝘸 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘈𝘐 𝘧𝘢𝘤𝘪𝘢𝘭 𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘨𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘦𝘤𝘩𝘯𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘺 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘣𝘦 𝘶𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘭𝘦 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘦𝘹𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘵𝘦 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘨𝘦 𝘢 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯, her lawsuit states. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐲𝐰𝐚𝐲.

Lipps had never set foot in North Dakota. She'd never even boarded a commercial flight. Bank surveillance video of the real suspect showed a different build and different facial features entirely — but Fargo detective Lucas Heck pushed the arrest warrant through regardless, according to the lawsuit. She was booked as a fugitive, extradited a thousand miles from her grandchildren, and told she was facing eight years in prison for a crime committed by a stranger she'd never met.

𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘶𝘨𝘨𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘰𝘧 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘣𝘦 𝘳𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘳 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘶𝘱 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨𝘭𝘺 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘷𝘪𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘪𝘮𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴, the suit alleges. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘣𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘩𝘥𝘢𝘺 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘤𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥, 𝘴𝘦𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺. 𝘚𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘥𝘢𝘺𝘴 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘥 𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘴, 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘛𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘬𝘴𝘨𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘊𝘩𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘮𝘢𝘴. 𝘞𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘤𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘥𝘺, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘪𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘤 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘦, 𝘴𝘶𝘤𝘩 𝘢𝘴 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘮𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘦𝘴. By the time she walked free on Christmas Eve, she'd lost her house, her car and her belongings.

Her attorney did what Fargo police never bothered to do — pulled her bank records and proved she was buying groceries in Tennessee the same day she was supposedly robbing a North Dakota bank. Charges dropped instantly. 𝘚𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘴 𝘪𝘯 𝘧𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘦 𝘢𝘣𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘨𝘢𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘭𝘦𝘧𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘭𝘦𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘨𝘩 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘪𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵, 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘪𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘴𝘢𝘧𝘦, the complaint states.

The department's own then-chief admitted afterward that 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦𝘴 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘢𝘥𝘦, telling reporters, 𝘕𝘰 𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘦𝘦 𝘴𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘥𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘦𝘥, 𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘶𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘭𝘺, 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵? He retired weeks later. Fargo itself has offered nothing — a city spokesperson says it 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴𝘯'𝘵 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘯 𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘨𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯, and has 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐳𝐞 to the woman its own detective jailed for six months on a hunch from a computer. Lipps is now suing the city and Detective Heck for $𝟏𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧.

𝐀𝐧 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞, 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐢𝐱 𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐥𝐠𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐦 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞-𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 — 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐨 𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐜𝐚𝐧'𝐭 𝐬𝐚𝐲 𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐲.

text:
My ancestors are Tejanos, having come up from the Mayan peninsula and settled Texas when it was Mexico. The border crossed us. Having experienced what happens when a wave of foreigners w/ a drastically different way of life settle in an area, my family and those like mine are naturally skeptical. 

But it’s nuanced. 

Our heritage and way of life is very much tied to the land itself. We own property and land that has passed through generations is because of the settlers - not Mexico. Mexico offered land grants to these new comers, and the land in many cases was already occupied by Tejanos. Then when these new settlers fought for independence, they offered its own soldiers land bounties and grants as incentives to fight against Mexico. Many people including my ancestors would help Texas achieve its independence. 

There is a lesson here: Mexico ceded its land, land already occupied by those of Mexican descent, willingly to newcomers, and those new comers waged war to claim it as their own. What a nation does willingly in the name of expedience and economics may ultimately be its own undoing by force and determination.

2/91/9

Dear Mr. President,

We live in extraordinarily difficult and divided times. Many Americans, including many Republicans, strongly support what you are trying to accomplish and understand the urgency with which you believe change must occur.

2/9

But I believe something critically important must never be forgotten:

You are not just my President. You are not just the President of the people who voted for you.

You are the President of every American.

3/9

Some Americans understand your sense of urgency. Others do not. Some believe the changes you are attempting are desperately needed. Others see things very differently.

Whether we agree politically or not, we remain Americans together.

4/9

I recently listened to remarks by Mr. Pat Boone, and much of what he said caused me to think seriously about the moment our country is facing.

Mr. President, I would respectfully offer you a suggestion:

Talk directly to the American people.

5/9

Consider addressing the nation on television, not primarily to list accomplishments, defend policies, attack opponents, or celebrate victories.

Instead, simply talk to us.

Explain why you believe this moment demands such urgency and why you believe it is necessary to move so quickly.

6/9

Perhaps acknowledge something Americans sometimes forget: the President is also a human being.

A President can become tired, frustrated, angry, and impatient under the enormous burden of that office.

And please speak directly to Americans who do not support you.

7/9

They are Americans too.

You do not need to persuade every citizen to agree with you. Perhaps the greater opportunity is helping them understand why you believe you are doing what you are doing.

The presidency belongs to the entire country.

8/9

I also believe we should examine the culture of every institution entrusted with protecting this country, including our military.

After 28 years in the Navy, including service with Marines and in the submarine community, I remain deeply concerned about critical thinking and respectful disagreement.

9/9

You have undertaken what you clearly believe is a Herculean task. I hope you remember that leadership sometimes requires speaking most directly to those who understand you the least.

I wish you strength, wisdom, good health, and success serving all Americans.

Respectfully,
John William Pate
Lieutenant, Nurse Corps, USN (Ret.)

WORLD THIS WEEK

14–20 SEPTEMBER 2026
MY READ OF THE WEEK

The biggest change was not a new conflict.
It was the way pressure started moving between systems.... from war into shipping, from sanctions into buyers, from technology into security, and from geography into strategy.

1 - THE GULF - A WAR STARTED TRAVELLING

Houthi attacks spread toward Saudi Arabia while Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb remained under pressure, pushing security, shipping and energy into the same story. Saudi Arabia began adapting oil flows, while Turkey moved closer to supporting Riyadh.

WHY I PUT IT #1:
This is no longer confined to the battlefield. If the disruption persists, the next effects travel through freight, fuel and inflation.

2 - RUSSIA- THE SANCTIONS TARGET IS GETTING WIDER
Trump signed new Russia sanctions legislation, giving Washington broader tools to pressure Russia's energy trade and countries that continue doing business with it.

WHY #2:
The pressure is shifting from “Russia must pay” to “Russia's customers may have to choose.”
That makes this an India, China, Europe and global-energy story.

3 - US–CHINA -THE BARGAINING TABLE GOT BIGGER
Washington and Beijing have moved into talks covering trade, AI, rare earths and energy ahead of the Trump–Xi meeting.

WHY #3:
The relationship is increasingly being negotiated as one system: chips + minerals + energy + trade.

4 - RUSSIA–UKRAINE -THE WAR IS MOVING DEEPER INTO THE SYSTEM
Ukraine carried out its largest reported drone attack on the Moscow region as Russia held parliamentary elections; an oil-refinery facility was damaged.

WHY #4:
The important shift is not simply another drone attack. War, domestic politics, cyber activity and energy infrastructure are increasingly overlapping.

5 - GREENLAND - THE ARCTIC BECAME A SOVEREIGNTY QUESTION

The U.S., Denmark and Greenland reached a security agreement involving expanded U.S. military presence, while Denmark and Greenland stressed that sovereignty remains intact. The detailed terms are still important.

WHY #5:
The Arctic is becoming a meeting point for military access, NATO security, resources and great-power competition.

ON THE RADAR

NORTH KOREA - Pyongyang fired two ballistic missiles on Sunday, its second missile-launch episode in about a week. South Korea and Japan protested.

AI SECURITY - Google's Gemini autonomously breached three company systems during a cybersecurity test. The significance is bigger than the individual incident: AI agents are gaining the ability to act, not simply generate information.

EU–CANADA - Brussels' offer of an “associate member” relationship to Canada is opening another debate about how closely Europe and Canada can align amid tensions with Washington.

THE THREAD

This week, the battlefield became only one part of the story, the pressure moved into shipping lanes, energy supplies, technology, trade rules and alliances.

That is the reason the Gulf story ranks first... it shows most clearly how a regional event can move through systems that millions of people depend on.

BlackRock's August geopolitical framework identifies the same broader mechanism: geopolitical shocks are pushing countries and companies toward greater redundancy, alternative routes and resilience - but at higher cost.

text:
Early Voting Has Begun for the 2026 Midterms. 

Cast Your Ballot.

Early voting for the November 3, 2026, midterm elections is now underway in several states. 

Virginia opened in-person early voting on September 18. Minnesota and South Dakota made ballots available the same day for in-person absentee voting at local election offices. Additional early-voting periods will open across the country in the coming weeks. 

Virginia’s 45-day early-voting window runs through October 31. Registered voters can appear at their locality’s designated early-voting site, present acceptable identification, and cast a ballot without an excuse. Weekend hours are available on October 18, 24, 25, and 31. The deadline to register or update registration for a regular ballot is October 23; same-day registration with a provisional ballot is available after that date. Mail-ballot applications must also be received by October 23. 

Minnesota made absentee ballots available for in-person voting beginning September 18. Official early voting—where ballots go directly into a tabulator—starts October 16 and continues through November 2. South Dakota offers in-person absentee voting from September 18 until the day before Election Day. Idaho’s in-person early or absentee period generally begins later, around October 13 in participating counties. Voters should confirm exact locations and hours with their county election office, as rules and availability.

Most other states begin early in-person voting in mid-October. Illinois opens September 24. California, Arizona, Ohio, and others follow in early October. Forty-seven states plus Washington, D.C., offer some form of no-excuse early or in-person absentee voting. A handful of states still require an excuse or rely primarily on Election Day and mail options. Check your state’s official election website or https://t.co/IJTgH1UDEe for registration status, polling locations, ID requirements, and deadlines. Do not rely on unofficial lists.

Why It Matters
The right to vote is the practical expression of self-government. 

It is how free citizens choose representatives, approve or reject policies that affect their communities, and hold officeholders accountable. Midterm elections decide control of the House and Senate, dozens of governorships, state legislatures, and countless local offices that set tax rates, school policy, public safety priorities, and infrastructure. Those decisions shape daily life whether turnout is high or low.
Early voting exists to make participation easier. Work schedules, family obligations, weather, and travel should not determine whether a citizen’s voice is heard. Casting a ballot weeks before Election Day is not a lesser form of civic duty; it is the same duty performed with greater convenience. The process is designed to be accessible, secure, and verifiable under state law.

A republic depends on citizens who show up. Low turnout does not make the outcomes illegitimate, but it does mean a smaller group of people decide for everyone else. High turnout across communities of every background strengthens the legitimacy of the result and reminds elected officials that they serve the whole public, not just the most motivated faction. 

Voting is not a partisan act. It is the act of a citizen.

Confirm your registration now. 

Review the candidates and measures on your ballot. If early voting is available in your state, use it. If it is not, plan for Election Day. 

The machinery of self-government only works when people operate it. This is the moment to do so.

Saudi mBridge Withdrawal: SAMA Exits China-Led CBDC Platform Amid Geopolitical Scrutiny - This assessment examines the Saudi Central Bank’s withdrawal from the mBridge multi-CBDC platform following its May 2025 proof-of-concept, evaluating the implications for alternative cross-border payment architectures, US-dollar primacy, and the platform’s operational trajectory without BIS oversight.

The Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) has formally withdrawn from the China-led mBridge wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC) platform, confirming to the Financial Times that it ceased participation after completing its planned proof-of-concept on 13 May 2025 Saudi Arabia exits China-led mBridge digital currency platform — Moneycontrol — Sep 2026. While Riyadh maintains the exit was programmatic and unrelated to US pressure, the withdrawal aligns with the Bank for International Settlements’ (BIS) October 2024 departure, which occurred amid Washington’s concerns regarding Chinese influence over platform governance and sanctions enforcement Saudi Arabia exits China-led mBridge digital currency platform — Moneycontrol — Sep 2026. SAMA’s exit deprives mBridge of a major petro-currency anchor, yet the platform continues to expand operationally under the sole stewardship of Asian and Middle Eastern monetary authorities, evidenced by the Monetary Authority of Macao activating live commercial transactions in June 2026 Saudi Arabia exits mBridge: Can China-led platform still challenge US dollar — Livemint — Sep 2026. The principal uncertainty remains whether mBridge can achieve sufficient liquidity and interoperability to function as a systemic alternative to SWIFT without the institutional credibility previously provided by the BIS and the prospective volume of Saudi rial settlements Saudi Arabia exits mBridge: Can China-led platform still challenge US dollar — Livemint — Sep 2026.

Saudi Arabia’s mBridge exit exposes a yuan corridor masquerading as a multilateral bridge
The Saudi Central Bank’s confirmation that it ceased participation in the mBridge cross-border payment platform after completing its proof-of-concept on 13 May 2025 is not a technical footnote. It is the clearest public signal yet that the project, originally designed by the Bank for International Settlements as a multilateral alternative to dollar-clearing infrastructure, has narrowed into a Chinese monetary instrument that no major energy exporter can afford to be seen operating. With 95 percent of the platform’s cumulative $55.5 billion in settled volume denominated in the renminbi, mBridge no longer functions as the neutral multi-currency bridge its founders advertised. The fiscal, diplomatic and security costs of continued association now exceed the technical benefits for any jurisdiction still exposed to US secondary sanctions enforcement.

A planned exit that reveals an unplanned trajectory

SAMA joined mBridge as an observer in 2023 and elevated to full participant status in June 2024, joining the Minimum Viable Product platform alongside the People’s Bank of China, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Bank of Thailand and the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates. The Saudi central bank stated it “successfully completed” its proof-of-concept on 13 May 2025 and ceased to be a participating member thereafter. Riyadh insists the withdrawal was programmatic. A separate source told the Financial Times that SAMA “continues to engage discreetly,” a formulation that preserves optionality while eliminating public association with a platform now governed exclusively by Asian monetary authorities. The distinction matters: SAMA retains technical access to the ledger architecture without exposing the Kingdom’s $55.5 billion energy export corridor to the secondary sanctions framework codified in Executive Order 14114, which authorises the US Treasury to sever foreign financial institutions from dollar-clearing for facilitating transactions with designated adversaries.

$55.5 billion in volume, 95 percent in one currency

The operational data dismantles the multilateral premise. By the second quarter of 2026, mBridge had processed approximately $55.5 billion across more than 4,000 cross-border transactions. According to figures reported by the People’s Bank of China and cited in Forbes’ May 2026 analysis of the project’s trajectory, approximately 95 percent of that volume settled in the digital yuan. This is not a multi-currency bridge. It is a renminbi internationalisation corridor operating under distributed-ledger packaging. In January 2026, the PBoC formally repositioned the e-CNY from a domestic retail instrument to a cross-border wholesale settlement tool, explicitly linking the digital yuan’s architecture to mBridge’s interoperability protocols. The consequence is structural: any central bank that joins mBridge as a full participant is, in operational terms, integrating its wholesale payment flows into a PBoC-denominated liquidity pool. For Saudi Arabia, whose oil revenues are priced and settled overwhelmingly in dollars, public association with a 95-percent-renminbi platform carries direct diplomatic exposure to Washington.

Macao’s 23 transactions signal commercial viability, not systemic challenge

On 2 June 2026, the Monetary Authority of Macao activated live mBridge transactions for participating commercial banks. Twenty-three cross-border settlements were executed on the first day. The Bank of Communications Macau completed two inaugural transactions using the digital pataca, routing value between Macao, the Chinese mainland and the UAE. The figures demonstrate that the platform’s technical infrastructure functions at commercial scale. They do not demonstrate that it threatens the dollar’s structural dominance. Twenty-three transactions on activation day, even scaled linearly, represent a rounding error against the approximately $6.6 trillion in daily foreign exchange turnover that SWIFT and correspondent banking networks process. The operational achievement is real; the systemic displacement thesis is not supported by the volume data. What Macao’s activation does confirm is that mBridge has transitioned from central-bank experimentation to live commercial deployment without any Western institutional participant, a trajectory that was not the original design intent of the BIS Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre when the project launched in 2021.

Capital controls baked into the code cap the ambition

The platform’s architecture contains a constraint that its proponents rarely discuss publicly: foreign commercial banks are structurally prohibited from holding mBridge central bank digital currencies. Exchange-rate management and cross-border capital controls are embedded as core design principles within the four-layer Hyperledger Besu fork that underpins the ledger. This means mBridge cannot function as an open, liquid reserve-currency alternative. It cannot accumulate the deep, liquid offshore markets that gave the eurodollar system its gravitational pull. Every transaction must reconcile against the issuing central bank’s domestic monetary policy mandates in real time. The design preserves sovereign control. It simultaneously prevents the network effects that would be required to displace dollar clearing at scale. Saudi Arabia’s withdrawal, read against this architectural constraint, reflects a recognition that mBridge offers settlement efficiency for bilateral trade corridors but cannot deliver the open capital mobility that a petro-state requires for its sovereign wealth management operations.

BIS departure stripped the platform of its regulatory shield

The structural fracture that preceded and precipitated SAMA’s exit occurred on 31 October 2024, when BIS General Manager Agustín Carstens announced the institution’s withdrawal from mBridge. Carstens stated publicly that the BIS had “graduated out” and that the departure was “not because of political considerations.” Reporting by the Financial Times indicated that US officials had pressed the BIS to withdraw, citing concerns that China could gain influence over the platform’s standards for security, interoperability and sanctions enforcement. Carstens explicitly stated: “mBridge is not the BRICS bridge and I have to say the BIS does not operate with any countries subject to sanctions.” The withdrawal removed the institution that had provided mBridge with technocratic legitimacy, neutral hosting and regulatory cover. Without BIS oversight, the platform’s governance transferred entirely to the Steering Committee of participating central banks, which added the Bank of Mongolia as a full member in June 2026. The governance structure is now exclusively Sino-Asian. For any jurisdiction still requiring access to US capital markets, the compliance calculus shifted decisively.

The 12–24 month ledger: who absorbs the cost

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months, three consequences follow from the architecture now in place. First, mBridge will continue to grow in transaction volume—projected along the Macao activation curve—but the growth will be overwhelmingly denominated in renminbi, deepening its character as a PBoC instrument rather than a multilateral platform. Second, the absence of a Western institutional anchor means that any future sanctions enforcement action targeting a participant jurisdiction will have no BIS-mediated dispute mechanism; commercial banks routing through mBridge will face unilateral OFAC determinations without intermediary institutional protection. Third, Saudi Arabia’s discreet continued engagement, if the FT sourcing is accurate, creates a latent re-entry option that Riyadh can activate only if the platform diversifies its currency composition beyond the current 95-percent renminbi concentration. The cost of inaction falls on the smaller participants: the Bank of Thailand, the Central Bank of the UAE and the Bank of Mongolia, whose central banks now bear the full operational, legal and reputational risk of governing a platform that the two largest potential liquidity providers—the BIS and SAMA—have exited. The dollar’s primacy is not threatened by mBridge’s current architecture. What is threatened is the political feasibility of any future multilateral CBDC project carrying the mBridge name. - https://t.co/R1ksOKVzsl via @https://debuglies.com

text:
The flustered and contradictory stances of Ankara’s diplomatic apparatus reveal the profound shock caused to Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s calculations by Mohammed bin Salman’s sudden shift in direction. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan’s remarks in which he voiced objection, declaring that "dragging Saudi Arabia into a war between the US and the Islamic Republic is unacceptable," while simultaneously and hurriedly speaking of "Turkey’s readiness to meet all the Saudi Kingdom’s defense needs" clearly signal the scrambling of a nation watching its greatest geopolitical project of recent years collapse right before its eyes.

Turkey had envisioned that by signing a trilateral defense pact with Riyadh and Islamabad, it could detach Saudi Arabia from the traditional Western orbit; utilizing Saudi petrodollars, it hoped to both drive its own military industry and establish itself as the sole hegemon and security umbrella for the Islamic world. However, as tensions escalated and the Kingdom’s infrastructure came under constant threat from Houthi and Tehran-allied missiles and drones, Bin Salman realized that Turkish aircraft and Pakistani infantry could not provide the immediate, comprehensive deterrence he required during a crisis.

To counter the overlapping threats posed by the Iranian regime and the Houthis, Riyadh entered into a pragmatic security coordination with Israel a decision immediately rewarded by Washington with the green light to supply 48 fifth-generation F-35 fighter jets. Bin Salman’s pivot was not merely military; The sudden withdrawal of the Saudi Central Bank from the China-led multilateral financial platform "mBridge" signaled that Riyadh has burned the bridges of its "double game" playing both sides to circumvent the West and has fully realigned itself within the financial and security architecture envisioned by Washington.

It is precisely this radical shift that has struck fear into Ankara!

Today, Turkey finds itself trapped between two catastrophic scenarios:

On one hand, Ankara is deeply concerned that the integration of Saudi infrastructure and airspace into the US-Israeli offensive campaign could ignite an all-out war a conflict whose flames would directly scorch Turkey’s southern borders, the Kurdish issue, and regional energy transit routes. Consequently, Fidan while outwardly professing support for Riyadh warns that Saudi Arabia must not be dragged into this war.

On the other hand, Turkey’s hasty offer to address Saudi Arabia’s defense gaps against the Houthis is, in reality, a desperate attempt to win back a lost client. Ankara realizes that if Saudi bases and radar shields are integrated into the joint air defense network shared by CENTCOM and Tel Aviv, Turkey’s strategic influence in the Persian Gulf will effectively vanish.

The cautious rhetoric from Saudi analysts describing cooperation with Tel Aviv as merely "limited and pragmatic" is merely a diplomatic veneer designed to manage public opinion. The reality on the ground is that Saudi Arabia has charted its own course. Turkey’s alarm stems from the bitter realization that, far from becoming the undisputed leader of an Islamic coalition, it now finds itself encircled by a new order forged between Washington, Tel Aviv, and Riyadh. An order in which Türkiye is not the one setting the rules of the game, but rather a sidelined observer anxious about the consequences of tomorrow.

مواضع سراسیمه و متناقض دستگاه دیپلماسی آنکارا، پرده از شوک سنگینی برمی‌دارد که تغییر جهتِ ناگهانی محمد بن‌سلمان به محاسبات رجب طیب اردوغان وارد کرده است. اظهارات هاکان فیدان، وزیر امور خارجه ترکیه، که با لحنی معترضانه اعلام کرد «کشاندن عربستان سعودی به جنگ آمریکا و جمهوری اسلامی غیرقابل قبول است»، و هم‌زمان با دستپاچگی از «آمادگی ترکیه برای تأمین تمامی نیازهای دفاعی پادشاهی سعودی» سخن گفت، نشانه‌ای آشکار از دست و پا زدن کشوری است که می‌بیند بزرگ‌ترین پروژه ژئوپلیتیک چند سال اخیرش درست جلوی چشمانش در حال فروپاشی است.   

ترکیه تصور می‌کرد با امضای پیمان دفاعی سه‌جانبه با ریاض و اسلام‌آباد، عربستان را از مدار سنتی غرب جدا کرده و با دلارهای نفتی سعودی، هم چرخ صنایع نظامی خود را می‌چرخاند و هم خود را به عنوان تنها هژمون و چتر امنیتی جهان اسلام تثبیت می‌کند. اما وقتی آتش تنش‌ها بالا گرفت و زیرساخت‌های پادشاهی زیر تهدید مداوم موشک‌ها و پهپادهای حوثی‌ها و نیروهای هم‌پیمان تهران قرار گرفت، بن‌سلمان متوجه شد که پرنده‌های ترک و پیاده‌نظام پاکستان، بازدارندگی آنی و همه‌جانبه‌ای که او در لحظه بحران می‌خواهد را ایجاد نمی‌کنند. 

  ریاض برای دفع تهدیدات همپوشان رژیم ایران و حوثی‌ها، وارد یک هماهنگی امنیتی عمل‌گرایانه با اسرائیل شد؛ تصمیمی که بلافاصله با چراغ سبز واشنگتن برای تحویل ۴۸ فروند جنگنده نسل پنجم F-35 پاداش داده شد. چرخش بن‌سلمان صرفاً نظامی نبود؛ خروج ناگهانی بانک مرکزی عربستان از پلتفرم مالی چندجانبه «mBridge» تحت رهبری چین، نشان داد که ریاض تمام پل‌های بازی دوگانه و دور زدن غرب را تخریب کرده و تمام‌قد خود را در معماری مالی و امنیتی مورد نظر واشنگتن بازتعریف کرده است.   

همین چرخش رادیکال است که آنکارا را به وحشت انداخته است!

ترکیه امروز خود را میان دو سناریوی فاجعه‌بار گرفتار می‌بیند:

از یک‌سو، آنکارا به‌شدت نگران است که پیوستن زیرساخت‌ها و حریم هوایی سعودی به کارزار تهاجمی آمریکا و اسرائیل، جنگی همه‌گیر را شعله‌ور کند که آتش آن مستقیماً مرزهای جنوبی ترکیه، پرونده کردها و ترانزیت انرژی منطقه را بسوزاند؛ از همین رو فیدان با ژست حمایت از ریاض هشدار می‌دهد که عربستان نباید به این جنگ کشانده شود.   

از سوی دیگر، پیشنهاد عجولانه ترکیه برای برطرف کردن خلأهای دفاعی عربستان در برابر حوثی‌ها، در واقع تلاشی از سر استیصال برای پس گرفتن مشتری از دست‌رفته است. آنکارا می‌داند اگر پایگاه‌ها و سپرهای راداری سعودی در شبکه پدافندی مشترک سنتکام و تل‌آویو قفل شوند، نفوذ استراتژیک ترکیه در خلیج فارس به صفر خواهد رسید.   

ادبیات محتاطانه تحلیل‌گران سعودی مبنی بر اینکه همکاری با تل‌آویو صرفاً «محدود و پراگماتیک» است، تنها یک پوشش دیپلماتیک برای مدیریت افکار عمومی است. واقعیت روی زمین این است که عربستان مدار خود را تعیین کرده است. وحشت ترکیه از این واقعیت تلخ سرچشمه می‌گیرد که می‌بیند نه تنها به رهبر بلامنازع یک ائتلاف اسلامی تبدیل نشد، بلکه حالا در محاصره نظمی نوین میان واشنگتن، تل‌آویو و ریاض قرار گرفته؛ نظمی که در آن ترکیه نه تعیین‌کننده قواعد بازی، بلکه ناظری حاشیه‌نشین و نگران از پیامدهای فرداست.

💡 Business Model

Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc. (EOSE) designs, manufactures, and deploys zinc-based, long-duration energy storage systems (LDESS) optimized for utility, industrial, and commercial applications. Bypassing standard lithium-ion technology, the company’s signature non-flammable chemistry offers a safer, more sustainable solution for storing grid-scale renewable energy. It monetizes primarily through hardware equipment sales of its advanced Eos Z3™ battery cubes and its project execution platform, Frontier Power USA (FPUSA). Key target customers include green energy project developers, public utilities, and critical infrastructure providers, including the U.S. Department of War. Main competitors include traditional utility battery operators alongside flow-battery and long-duration storage innovators like ESS Tech and Fluence Energy.

📊 Financial & Cash Profile

Hyper-Growth Revenue Transition: 
Eos is experiencing a massive top-line expansion as its manufacturing capabilities mature. For the second quarter of 2026, revenue surged an immense 351% year-over-year to $68.8 million. First-half 2026 revenue of $125.7 million successfully eclipsed full-year 2025 results. Management has tightened full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $300 million – $350 million to prioritize long-term cost improvements.
Persistent Gross Losses & Manufacturing Spends:
Despite surging sales, bottom-line profitability remains heavily in the red. Eos logged an adjusted gross margin of -62% and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $71.4 million in Q2 2026. Net losses reached $276 million during the quarter, proving that the company is still actively spending significantly more to manufacture its battery components than it absorbs in pricing.

⚖️ Balance Sheet Strength

Short-Term Liquidity: 
Adequate Capital Runway. Eos holds a stable near-term cash cushion to navigate its commercial acceleration, ending Q2 2026 with $364 million in total cash and cash equivalents. The company achieves strong free cash flow conversion from its ongoing business operations, insulated by nearly $78 million in direct quarterly customer collections.
Long-Term Solvency: 
Highly Leveraged. To avoid devastating shareholder dilution during its expansion sprint, Eos relies heavily on debt and structured liabilities, resulting in an aggressive debt-to-asset ratio of roughly 91.87%. However, its solvency roadmap received a massive structural boost via a secure $87 million advance on its strategic loan from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to fast-track production lines.

⚠️ Critical Risks

Severe Margin Pressure & Manufacturing Consolidation: 
Eos does not suffer from a lack of client demand; rather, it faces a pressing unit-economics cost hurdle. To fix its negative gross margins, the company is enduring short-term capacity friction as it rushes to consolidate production lines into its flagship Thorn Hill manufacturing facility in Warrendale.
Backlog Execution Bottlenecks: 
While Eos commands a record $807 million commercial order backlog alongside a theoretical $24.6 billion opportunity pipeline, converting these paper commitments into actual revenue hinges completely on scaling automated factory output without encountering supply chain or technical glitches.
High Public Market Volatility: 
As a developing clean-tech enterprise trading near $3.96—sharply off its 52-week peak of $19.86—the stock remains heavily prone to dramatic trading swings driven by regulatory changes, grid integration constraints, and insider selling pressure.

text:
Advice from a below average engineering student who studied at a good institution and didn’t end up getting a job at the end when all my colleagues had at least 3 offers - this is a 2 parter:

folks who are yet to choose a career path - you have the internet at your disposal. Spend ungodly amounts of time online to figure out what you actually like. If you like sports, go into a college which excels in it, take up a degree that will allow you to concentrate on your sport and get a degree by the end of it. This is just one example. If you aren’t able to figure it out do what’s most comfortable for you. You get 3-4 years to figure out what you like. All my friends who had offers after engineering ended up in finance or management and I am in tech. Trust me no one knows. You will get family pressure, money issues, and what not. Think of how you can navigate through those obstacles. There are ways and means. The pain in the initial years is way better than what you will feel later if you are not doing what you like. Know that in the age of AI and YouTube no skill is inaccessible. You can learn the most obscure skill for free nowadays. I urge you to take advantage of these resources. 

folks who have already taken up something they don’t like and are deep in it - it’s not the end. I was one of them. Finish up what you have taken. Make it your only aim. Once done, take a job and burn that midnight lamp to get out of it. It’s difficult and every year you spend doing what you don’t like, it becomes even more difficult to get out. So it’s your determination that will help you and nothing else. The only saving grace is that you may not have to depend on anyone else for money. Make it your strong point. Put your hard earned money to learn that skill that you really like. By this time you should have already known what you like and don’t. Comfort zone is your enemy. Putting yourself in uncomfortable situations is the only way out. I’m sure you all can do it - that extra course, certification, singing class, coffee aficionado, cooking, whatever…. Just push yourself. One day you will make it. 

Last advice to all - you all can only dream and achieve if you keep yourself out of trouble. Social media has its benefits and curses. Beware. Don’t break the law and trouble your loved ones.

text:
REMARKABLE: Britain’s first prime minister’s desk has stayed put for three centuries

At Houghton Hall in Norfolk, begun in 1722, Sir Robert Walpole built a country home while shaping the job we now call prime minister.

Its grand front announces power. The more revealing room is much smaller.

Houghton’s library was Walpole’s private study. The room designed by William Kent remains largely unaltered, with Walpole’s custom-made mahogany desk still standing where it stood three centuries ago.

This was not merely a show library. Walpole worked and corresponded here, surrounded by roughly 1,200 books gathered across three generations of his family. A day bed beside the window offered somewhere to read or rest.

Above the fireplace hangs George I, the king whose support helped Walpole dominate government. Yet the title “prime minister” was still treated as an insult: Walpole officially served as First Lord of the Treasury from 1721 to 1742 and denied being a sole or prime minister.

Louise would notice the enormous house first. I keep returning to that desk (small enough for ordinary papers, but used by the man who helped turn political management into a permanent office).

Even the family dining room offers a contrast. Houghton’s Common Parlour is deliberately plainer than the state rooms, with William Kent’s original chairs still gathered around a far more intimate space.

The house displays Walpole’s wealth and ambition. His quiet study explains him better: books inherited from his family, a king watching from the wall, and political work conducted from one carefully placed desk.

I hope that little room keeps outlasting the machinery of power built around it.

Indeed, as the last knight of liberalism.   

Stripping this period of Mises' life of all context makes it sound like Mises was a fascist himself which only proves complete ignorance of the man.  

Indeed, without context, leads to a misunderstanding of Dolfuss as well (not that he was a saint, but under the circumstances one can understand his motivations at the very least).   

Quote:   
"The economic crisis heightened political antagonisms throughout Europe. Fewer and fewer citizens believed democracy could meet the current challenges. Only two alternatives seemed available, both based on violence: either the dictatorship of the proletariat (or more precisely the dictatorship of labor union bosses and socialist party leaders), or an authoritarian dictatorship ben on restoring the old order."  

(...)  

"Mises later said that it was the growing power of the Nazi party in Austria that prompted him to leave the country. With this remark, he did not refer to the government of Engelbert Dolfuss, which had reintroduced authoritarian corporatism into Austrian politics to resist the socialism of both the Marxist and the Nazi variety. Mises meant the Austrian branch of the National Socialist German Workers Party, which enjoyed strong backing from Berlin and fought a daily battle to conquer the streets of Vienna. Dolfuss's authoritarian policies were in his view only a quick fix to safeguard Austria's independence-- unsuitable in the long run, especially if the general political mentality did not change.  

In March 1934, Mises was delighted to receive an offer from the Geneva-based Graduate Institute of International Studies to become a visiting professor of international economic relations. He accepted immediately. However, he did not flee Austria, as he would when the Nazis seized control of the country four years later. He moved to Geneva in disgust, but he considered the move temporary.   

Mises had been an employee of the Kammer [the Vienna Chamber of Commerce] long enough to qualify for early retirement, but he did not wish to burn his bridges and eventually arrived at an agreement according to which he would do some work for it during his school vacations and be paid half his former salary. In early December 1934, he returned to Vienna for the first time and worked some weeks in his old position. Thereafter he continued to work as a consultant and liaison officer for the Vienna Kammer." (p 683-684)  

Hülsmann, Jörg Guido. Mises: The Last Knight of Liberalism. Auburn, AL: Ludwig von Mises Institute, 2007.  

This is the capacity in which Mises had been serving under the Vienna Chamber of Commerce LONG BEFORE Dolfuss came to power. And given that Mises viewed Dolfuss' reign as temprorary, Mises remained on staff.  

So, there you have it!   

Is there any other irrelevant information you would like to add or obtuse interpretations of an honorable man's life that you would like to drag through the mud?
